# Tender research appendix: every finding

Companion to [tender-research.md](tender-research.md), generated from the research data on 2026-10-22. Nothing here is summarised: it lists every requirement statement read in a tender, every supplier profile and every finding, each with its source link. Statement text is a short paraphrase of the source. Some English trust specifications sit behind supplier portals and are not included (see section 8 of the report).

## Contents

- [A. Every requirement statement, by feature (ranked by demand)](#a-every-requirement-statement-by-feature-ranked-by-demand)
- [B. Every supplier profile](#b-every-supplier-profile)
- [C. Every finding: policy, compliance, buyer patterns](#c-every-finding-policy-compliance-buyer-patterns)
- [D. Every tender with its full requirement list](#d-every-tender-with-its-full-requirement-list)

## A. Every requirement statement, by feature (ranked by demand)

**Two records bundle several notices.** T201 (NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, "2627 DS012 Digital PreOp Solution") also holds statements from NHS Golden Jubilee's patient pathway app tender (GJ24/004, won by Zimmer) and from other Scottish notices (national MSK, Connect Me, Netcall). Its "winner Zimmer" belongs to Golden Jubilee, not to GGC. T202 (DHCW, "Welsh Pre-Operative Digital System") also holds statements from a Welsh theatre-system engagement, a telehealth engagement and a Cwm Taf Morgannwg innovation call. For these two, follow each statement's own source link to see which notice it came from.

Demand = number of distinct tenders that state the feature. Pre-op = how many of those are pre-op assessment tenders. A statement can support more than one feature.

### 1. Price and licence model (award weight on price, subscription, per-use, enterprise) (CM06)

Group: commercial/service. Demand: **131 tenders** (pre-op 14; UK 42, IE 1, EU 88); 190 statements. Our status: **Missing**. Bid priority: P1. Note: Pricing not yet set. Suppliers that offer it: Aire Logic Ltd (AireFrame ePOA), Buddy Healthcare Ltd Oy (Elsie ePreOp), Concentric Health Ltd, DrDoctor, EIDO Healthcare Ltd (EIDO Inform), NEC Software Solutions UK Ltd, PreActiv, Surgery Hero (Sword Health), Tecnologías Plexus, S.L., VitalHub UK Ltd (Synopsis), Zesty Ltd (Induction Healthcare, now VitalHub).

### Aire Logic Ltd (AireFrame ePOA)

- **Also known as:** Aire Logic; Aire Logic Ltd; Aire Logic Limited; Aire Innovate Ltd; AireFrame ePOA; Smart preOp AI; AireBlocks; Forms4Health (forms4health); Aire Logic ePROMs
- **Based in:** UK (mentions list UK only; HQ city not stated)
- **Type:** pre-op specialist (also PROMs supplier and data-validation framework supplier)
- **Products:** AireFrame ePOA: low-code electronic pre-op assessment on AireBlocks, from surgical consultation to theatre booking, with optional Smart preOp AI risk stratification; ePROMs (All Wales PROMs framework); Forms4Health digital forms platform.
- **Integrations:** Open APIs to PAS, EPR and EHR; HL7; FHIR; openEHR; SNOMED; REST and GraphQL APIs; Forms embedded in Leeds' in-house PPM+ EHR; Smart preOp AI uses primary care and procedure data; Integrations priced at 5% of licence each (G-Cloud 15)
- **Accreditations:** ISO/IEC 27001 (BSI, 9 Oct 2023) (G-Cloud 15 service definition document 546146788659434 (research_competitors)); ISO 27001 (BSI, 19 Feb 2025) (G-Cloud 15 listing 453946191700706 (research_uk-trust-portals)); Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus (G-Cloud 14 and G-Cloud 15 listings); DSPT (exceeds) (Aire Logic G-Cloud 14 listing); DCB0129 compliance, supports buyer DCB0160, named Clinical Safety Officer (Aire Logic G-Cloud 14 and G-Cloud 15 listings); WCAG 2.1 AA (Aire Logic G-Cloud 14 listing); ISO 9001 (G-Cloud 15 listing 453946191700706); ISO 20000 (G-Cloud 15 listing 453946191700706); HSCN (G-Cloud 15 listing 453946191700706); G-Cloud 14 and G-Cloud 15 listed (Digital Marketplace listings); Aire Innovate: ISO 27001 stage 2 audit booked for Jun 2024 (G-Cloud listing (research_competitors)); Employee-owned B Corp (G-Cloud listing (research_competitors)); UK data storage (G-Cloud 15 listing)
- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 15: S tier (<5,000 patient transactions/yr) £14,000/yr; M (<10,000) £25,000/yr; L (10,000+) £2.40 per patient transaction; support at 20% of licence; each integration adds 5% of licence; professional services £1,000/day; 12-month minimum. G-Cloud 14: £2,500 per unit/licence per year; free trial.
- **Customers claimed:** Leeds Teaching Hospitals: AI ASA risk stratification trained on LTHT data, forms embedded in PPM+; almost all POA moved to remote completion, up to 50% of clinician time freed, 6,000+ face-to-face appointments removed a year, £57k admin saving per department (vendor claims); Risk model tested at Bradford; Says it helped Leeds Teaching Hospitals devise an alternative pre-op assessment system (Forms4Health), per its G-Cloud 14 social value text; All Wales PROMs Solution framework supplier (NWSSP, concluded 13 Oct 2023; unranked, 5 suppliers; share of a GBP 11.9m framework); National Data Validation Services framework supplier (Countess of Chester, 2025); Holds large NHS England digital delivery contracts
- **Differentiators:** Patient side needs no login or registration; Low-code platform (AireBlocks) with a forms designer, so trusts build their own forms; Optional Smart preOp AI: ASA 1-2 vs ASA 3+ cohorts and 30-day mortality prediction, trained on LTHT data; Broad standards support: HL7, FHIR, openEHR, SNOMED, REST and GraphQL; Strong assurance set: ISO 27001, CE+, DSPT exceeds, DCB0129 with named CSO, ISO 9001, ISO 20000, WCAG 2.1 AA; Transparent tiered G-Cloud 15 pricing; Employee-owned B Corp; On several frameworks: G-Cloud, All Wales PROMs, Data Validation Services, NHS SBS SBS10521 Lot 1

- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 15 annual tiers by consent episodes: 2,500 = GBP 10k; 10,000 = GBP 30k; 30,000 = GBP 50k; 60,000 = GBP 75k; 100,000 = GBP 100k; 200,000 = GBP 150k; 350,000 = GBP 200k; overage GBP 2 per episode; extra services GBP 200/hour. Contracts GBP 180k-300k per trust or group, often about GBP 45k-100k a year (Barts about GBP 45k a year).
- **Customers claimed:** 35+ NHS trusts trust-wide (claim); Circle Health (54 hospitals); UHL; UHCW; WUTH; Sandwell; Isle of Wight NHS Trust; West Herts; Imperial; Chelsea and Westminster; Moorfields; West Suffolk; Swansea Bay UHB; Kingston; Calderdale and Huddersfield; Plymouth; Royal Cornwall; Bradford Teaching Hospitals (credited in the IoW explainer film); Northumbria; Buckinghamshire Healthcare; Princess Alexandra; Barts Health / NEL trusts; Jersey
- **Differentiators:** Largest template library (3,000+) with Montgomery-compliant personalisation; Strong NHS SSO (CIS2, Entra ID, NHS.net Connect) and EHR launch in context; Wide NHS footprint (35+ trusts claimed; 17,000 consents a week in 2024); Expanding to Republic of Ireland and Australasia; Transparent episode-based pricing on G-Cloud 15
- **Gaps stated by sources:** No ISO/IEC 27001 (G-Cloud 15 listing)
- **Features:**
  - Digital consent with electronic signature (CW05): eConsent replacing paper; advanced electronic signature; adult, paediatric and capacity consent workflows; remote or in-person consent
  - Shared decision-making (PX13): Montgomery-compliant personalisation; clinician tailors risks, benefits and alternatives
  - Consent template library (QC04): 3,000+ clinician-authored templates (2,577 by end of 2024), PIF TICK
  - Procedure information for patients (PX06): Clinician tailors procedure information and shares it in person, by email or by SMS
  - Email/SMS links to patients (PX03): Patient gets an email/SMS link and verifies date of birth before reviewing
  - Remote patient review (PX01): Patient reviews and consents remotely before the visit
  - HL7 integration (IN02): HL7/FHIR integration with EPRs and trust integration engines (TIEs)
  - FHIR integration (IN03): HL7/FHIR integration with EPRs and TIEs
  - PDF written back to the EPR (IN05): Completed consent PDF pushed to the EPR
  - SSO and launch in context (IN07): SSO via CIS2, Entra ID and NHS.net Connect; iframe/patient-context launch from the EHR
  - Security controls (CS09): Role-based access, tamper-detectable audit trail, read-only users
  - UK GDPR (CS01): UK GDPR compliance claimed
  - Multi-tenant SaaS (HD01): Multi-tenant SaaS on Google Cloud
  - UK data residency (HD02): Google Cloud UK data centre (per WUTH and supplier)
  - Replaces paper consent (CW09): Replaces paper consent with digital consent episodes
  - Multi-trust deployment (CW06): One Barts contract covers five North East London trusts (Barts, BHRUT, Homerton, NELFT, ELFT); Circle Health 54 hospitals
  - Scale (HD08): Claims 12,000 clinicians and 38,000 patients a week; 2024: over 17,000 consents a week and over 500k patients
  - Framework routes (CM01): G-Cloud 13 and G-Cloud 15; resold by Softcat via NOE Total Technology Solutions
  - Published price tiers (CM06): G-Cloud 15 tiers by consent episodes

### Doctolib GmbH

- **Also known as:** Doctolib; Doctolib Hospital patient portal
- **Based in:** Germany (Berlin, per T072)
- **Type:** patient engagement platform
- **Products:** Doctolib Hospital patient portal (KHZG FTB2): online booking, treatment information, pre-admission forms, optional services, reminders, patient diary, messaging and hospital-practice referrals.
- **Integrations:** Thieme Compliance E-ConsentPro (partner/subcontractor); Recare (Lot 2 discharge partner at Havelland)
- **Accreditations:** TED 103330-2025 / deep-read_5 mention
- **Customers claimed:** Charité Berlin; Havelland Kliniken; Krankenhaus Ludmillenstift Meppen
- **Differentiators:** Pairs its portal with Thieme E-ConsentPro consent and patient-information videos.
- **Features:**
  - Online booking and appointment requests (PX08): Patients book or request appointments online.
  - Treatment information (PX06): Treatment information for patients; Thieme consent and patient-information videos supplied at Havelland via subcontractor.
  - Pre-admission forms (PX01): Patients complete pre-admission forms online.
  - Digital anamnesis (QC05): Claims to meet all KHZG mandatory criteria, including digital anamnesis.
  - Optional services (Wahlleistungen): Patients can choose optional services.
  - Reminders (PX03): Appointment reminders.
  - Patient diary: Patient diary.
  - Messaging (PX09): Messaging between patient and hospital.
  - Referrals between hospitals and practices: Referral exchange between hospitals and practices.
  - Digital consent (via Thieme E-ConsentPro) (CW05): At Havelland, Thieme Compliance subcontracts E-ConsentPro Patient; Doctolib and Thieme E-ConsentPro announced a cooperation.
  - Hospital patient portal (PX07): Patient portal (KHZG FTB2) at Charité, Havelland and Ludmillenstift Meppen.
  - KHZG funding criteria (CS11): Claims to meet all KHZG mandatory criteria.

### DrDoctor

- **Also known as:** ICNH Ltd; ICNH Limited; ICNH Ltd t/a DrDoctor; ICHN Ltd trading as Dr Doctor; Dr Doctor
- **Based in:** UK
- **Type:** patient engagement platform
- **Products:** Patient Engagement Platform / portal: digital and hybrid letters, appointments and self-booking, messaging, Document & Questionnaire Management (clinical smart forms, incl. digital pre-op forms), PIFU, PROMs, remote monitoring, NHS App integration, FHIR/HL7 write-back to the EPR.
- **Integrations:** NHS App / Wayfinder; NHS login; EPR/eDMS via FHIR Digital Assessment API and HL7 write-back; Hybrid mail providers via Digital Letters API; Bi-directional EPR interface (Warrington & Halton)
- **Accreditations:** G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 505878518749739; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; G-Cloud 14 listing 606705557370842; research_competitors
- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 14 listing shows 'GBP 1 per unit' (detail in pricing document). G-Cloud 15 pricing document: licence tiers by outpatient volume per instance, about GBP 23k to GBP 340k a year. Observed contracts GBP 18.6k (Dorset licences) to GBP 2.24m. Pre-op questionnaire usually bundled into the wider portal contract and cannot be split out (WWL FOI).
- **Customers claimed:** Says it serves 70+ trusts and health boards; Warrington & Halton; Lewisham & Greenwich; GMMH; Bradford; UHB (ROH, BWC); Walton Centre; Newcastle; Hull; Dorset County; PAHT; Moorfields; NNUH; WWL; Salisbury; NHS England
- **Differentiators:** Pre-op forms available inside the NHS App (Lewisham & Greenwich, from Sep 2025).; On the main NHS patient-communications frameworks (SBS10521, NHS Commercial Solutions) and G-Cloud.; Broad portal: letters, booking, messaging, forms, PIFU, PROMs in one contract.
- **Gaps stated by sources:** Replaced at Royal Berkshire by 'Royal Berkshire Connect' (Aug 2025) (deep-read_6).; None of its tender notices names pre-op; pre-op use is visible only through trust pages and FOIs (gap_England).; WWL contract expired Oct 2025 and was 'under review' (WWL FOI 10899).; BWC moved to Epic MyChart, with DrDoctor texts and letters continuing alongside (T066).; G-Cloud listing names UK, EEA and 'other' data locations, despite Azure UK hosting (deep-read_6).
- **Features:**
  - Digital letters and hybrid mail (PX10): Digital letters; Digital Letters API to hybrid mail providers; Bradford patient letters (digital and hybrid).
  - SMS, email, reminders and broadcast messaging (PX03): SMS and email links, reminders, broadcast messaging; SMS consumables.
  - Waiting-list validation ('Quick Question') (SW01): Patient-facing waiting-list validation via 'Quick Question'.
  - Online forms / clinical smart forms (PX01): Document and Questionnaire Management; clinical smart forms; NHS England Online Forms Pilot.
  - Digital pre-op forms (perioperative use case) (CW09): Pre-op health check forms that feed the EPR; used for pre-op pre-screening at NNUH, WWL and Salisbury; Moorfields digital questionnaire.
  - Re-contact while waiting (SW02): Questionnaires resent every 3 months while waiting (NNUH).
  - NHS App, NHS login and Wayfinder integration (IN06): NHS App / Wayfinder integration; pre-op forms available in the NHS App (Lewisham & Greenwich from Sep 2025); NHS login.
  - Patient login without NHS login: Login with surname, DOB and postcode plus OTP, or with NHS login / NHS account.
  - Two-way messaging (PX09): Two-way messaging.
  - Video consultations (PX14): Video consultations.
  - Patient-led booking and rescheduling (PX08): Self-service scheduling with EPR write-back.
  - AI attendance (DNA) prediction and overbooking (TR06): AI attendance prediction and overbooking.
  - Patient-initiated follow-up (PIFU): PIFU.
  - PROMs (PF01): PROMs collection.
  - Care plans: Care plans.
  - Remote monitoring and symptom trackers (PF04): Remote monitoring; symptom trackers.
  - Dashboards (CW01): Dashboards.
  - Configurable pathways (QC01): Configurable pathways with forms and logic.
  - Form logic (QC02): Configurable pathways with forms and logic.
  - Scores (QC06): Digital Assessment API writes responses and scores to the EPR/eDMS.
  - FHIR Digital Assessment API (IN03): FHIR Digital Assessment API.
  - HL7 assessment write-back (IN02): HL7 assessment write-back to the EPR or eDMS.
  - Write-back to EPR/eDMS (IN05): Responses and scores written back to the EPR/eDMS; pre-op forms feed the EPR.
  - Bi-directional EPR interface / open APIs (IN01): Warrington & Halton portal with bi-directional EPR interface and open APIs.
  - Patient portal (PX07): Patient portal; radiology patient information portal (Newcastle).
  - Patient information portal (PX06): Radiology patient information portal.
  - Cloud-hosted (HD01): Hosted on Microsoft Azure UK; HSCN-connected.
  - Data location (HD02): Azure UK, but the G-Cloud listing names UK, EEA and 'other' locations.
  - Availability SLA (HD04): 99.9% uptime.
  - Accessibility (CS08): WCAG 2.1 AA.
  - Framework routes (CM01): G-Cloud 13/14/15; SBS10521 Lots 1, 2, 4 and 7; NHS Commercial Solutions Lot 1 (patient messaging).
  - Licence model (CM06): G-Cloud 15 licence tiers by outpatient volume per instance.

### EIDO Healthcare Ltd (EIDO Inform)

- **Also known as:** EIDO Healthcare Limited; Eido Healthcare Limited; EIDO Inform; EIDO Inform Digital Consent Suite (ICS); EIDO Consent; EIDO Healthcare Library
- **Based in:** UK (Nottingham; Companies House 04030383; SME)
- **Type:** consent
- **Products:** EIDO Inform Digital Consent Suite: Inform procedure library (leaflets as PDF and digital articles, procedure videos), digital and remote consent (forms 1-4 and custom), leaflet builder/CMS, engagement reporting, custom procedure module, Easy Read, Large Print, Screen Reader, Translations, learning-disability and Educate e-learning modules
- **Integrations:** EPR; PAS; Pre-op assessment (POA) systems; HL7; FHIR; REST/JSON; EPR demographics pull/push; SSO; SMS/email
- **Accreditations:** Cyber Essentials (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-14/services/619380355073902); Cyber Essentials Plus (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); NHS DSPT (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); NHS DTAC (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); ISO 27001 for the AWS infrastructure only; EIDO's own certification expected (2024 per G-Cloud 14; 2026 per G-Cloud 15) (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); ISO 31000 (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); Annual CREST penetration testing (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); Content accredited under the DoH Information Standard (https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/017020-2025); Royal College of Surgeons-approved procedure library (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063); G-Cloud 13, 14 and 15 listings (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-14/services/619380355073902)
- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 14: GBP 7,500 per licence, free trial. G-Cloud 15: EIDO Consent GBP 150 (individual) to GBP 75,000/yr (X-Large, 200,000 episodes); EIDO Inform GBP 150-70,000/yr; custom implementation GBP 750/day; 3-6 month free trial. Observed: mostly GBP 14k-50k a year licences; CoCH about GBP 15k/yr licence + GBP 5k deployment; Medway GBP 13.7k a year.
- **Customers claimed:** 65% of NHS trusts (claim); Nottingham University Hospitals; Manchester University NHS FT; Barnsley; United Lincolnshire; Northern HSCT; South Eastern HSCT; UHNM; Shrewsbury and Telford; Warrington and Halton; Countess of Chester; Walsall; Simply Serve; Mid and South Essex; Medway
- **Differentiators:** College-approved, legally defensible procedure content (buyers' words); Very wide NHS reach (claims 65% of trusts); many renewals moving from 1-year to 3-5 year terms; Explicitly integrates with pre-op assessment (POA) systems; Accessibility and language modules (Easy Read, Large Print, Screen Reader, translations, Welsh); Often direct-awarded as the sole supplier
- **Gaps stated by sources:** Own ISO 27001 not held; only the AWS hosting is certified (G-Cloud 14/15); Only one competitive win found (SaTH); most awards are direct or single-tender (research)
- **Features:**
  - Procedure information library (QC04): Library approved by the Royal College of Surgeons / colleges; buyers call it clinically and legally validated; content accredited under the DoH Information Standard (SaTH notice)
  - Patient information leaflets and videos (PX06): Procedure-specific leaflets as PDF or digital articles; procedure videos
  - Digital consent (CW05): Consent forms 1-4 plus custom forms, completed at home or in hospital (remote consent)
  - Shared decision-making support (PX13): Patient engagement reports for SDM
  - Engagement reporting (CW07): Patient engagement reporting and tracking
  - Translations and Welsh (PX04): Multi-language/translation module; bilingual versions; Welsh-language content offered
  - Learning-disability and Easy Read versions (PX05): Learning-disability module; Easy Read
  - Accessible formats (CS08): Large Print and Screen Reader modules
  - Local customisation (QC01): Local customisation; custom procedure module; leaflet builder/CMS
  - Email/SMS patient links (PX03): Email/SMS link with surname plus date-of-birth check
  - EPR, PAS and POA integration (IN01): Integrates with EPR, PAS and pre-op assessment (POA) systems; the EPR stays the data master
  - HL7 (IN02): HL7 interface
  - FHIR and REST/JSON API (IN03): FHIR, REST/JSON API
  - EPR demographics pull (IN04): EPR demographics pull and push (CoCH spec)
  - PDF filed to the EPR (IN05): Completed consent PDF filed to the EPR
  - SSO (IN07): SSO (CoCH spec)
  - Cloud SaaS on AWS (HD01): Hosted on AWS
  - UK hosting (HD02): AWS UK
  - Retention (HD07): 180-day default retention
  - Penetration testing (CS09): Annual CREST penetration testing
  - Staff e-learning (Educate module): Educate e-learning module
  - Implementation services and free trial (CM04): Custom implementation GBP 750/day; 3-6 month free trial
  - Framework routes (CM01): G-Cloud 13, 14 and 15; DPS; direct awards
  - Published licence prices (CM06): G-Cloud 14 and 15 price lists

### Encare AB (ERAS Interactive Audit System)

- **Also known as:** Encare; ERAS Interactive Audit System; EIAS
- **Based in:** Sweden
- **Type:** other
- **Products:** ERAS Society protocol implementation programmes (11 specialty programmes + ERAS Essentials), prehabilitation module, and the EIAS SaaS audit, compliance-monitoring and benchmarking platform.
- **Accreditations:** Qualified on Mayo Clinic Platform_Solutions Studio (Aug 2025) (https://pharmatimes.com/news/encares-eras-system-gains-mayo-clinic-qualification-strengthening-global-reach/); Hosted on AWS in ISO 27001-compliant data centres in Frankfurt (data-centre compliance, not an Encare certificate) (https://www.kantonsspitalbaden.ch/documents/2025-06/eras_20250604.pdf); ERAS Society validated / partnership (Münster requirements imply ERAS Society authorisation) (https://www.kantonsspitalbaden.ch/documents/2025-06/eras_20250604.pdf; https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/509259-2026/xml)
- **Customers claimed:** Universitätsklinikum Münster: already holds EIAS data; named Encare as the reference solution in its 2026 ERAS market consultation (T012/T304, status planned, no award); Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana: named Encare as the reference / only known solution in its 2025 PIN (T089, estimate EUR 100,000; no award found); Kantonsspital Baden (Switzerland) publishes an EIAS technical document; Used in Germany, Italy and others
- **Differentiators:** Named by buyers as the reference or only known ERAS solution (Münster 2026, Ljubljana 2025); Developed with and validated by the ERAS Society; Mayo Clinic Platform qualification (Aug 2025)
- **Features:**
  - ERAS programmes and prehabilitation (PF06): ERAS protocols and pathways: 11 specialty programmes plus ERAS Essentials; prehabilitation module.
  - Audit, compliance monitoring and benchmarking (CW07): EIAS web audit and benchmarking; SaaS audit and compliance-monitoring across surgical specialties.
  - SaaS (HD01): EIAS is SaaS (founded 2009).
  - EU hosting (HD02): Hosted on AWS in Frankfurt data centres (per the EIAS technical document published by Kantonsspital Baden).
  - Clinical and pathway expertise (CM07): Developed with the ERAS Society; ERAS Society validated/partnership.
  - Multi-site / international use (CW06): Used in Germany (UKM Münster holds EIAS data), Switzerland (Kantonsspital Baden), Italy and others.

- **Pricing:** Trusts often cannot split out the cost of pre-op functionality from the EPR contract.

  - Pre-op pro-formas (CW03): Dudley: Altera Sunrise pre-op pro-formas.

### Novacair B.V. (E-POS)

- **Also known as:** NovaCair; E-POS; Proposal UMM E-Pos

- **Accreditations:** NEN 7510 (badge on website) (https://novacair.com/); ISO 27001 (stated by one mention; another says not mentioned on the site) (https://novacair.com/en/products/e-pos/); CE medical device (implied by the Mannheim award; buyer requirement) (https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml); GDPR compliance (buyer requirement) (https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml); Scientifically validated by Amsterdam UMC (Journal of Clinical Anesthesia) (https://novacair.com/en/products/e-pos/); MDR not mentioned on the website (https://novacair.com/)
- **Customers claimed:** Universitätsklinikum Mannheim; Alrijne; Heelkunde Instituut Nederland; Bergman Clinics Naarden; FlexClinics; ETZ Tilburg (since 1 July, per VGZ item); Dijklander (first E-POS-HiX link); Haaglanden MC (HiX 6.3); Erasmus MC; Amsterdam UMC; Spaarne Gasthuis; Treant; Annatommie MC; The Hand Clinics; Partners: VGZ (insurer), ZKN (sponsorship since 1 Jan 2023); Calls itself the most-used digital POS tool in the Netherlands; aim 15-20 hospitals
- **Differentiators:** Scientifically validated triage (Amsterdam UMC; Journal of Clinical Anesthesia).; Claims about 60% time saving and 85% fewer outpatient consultations; 80% of records complete without extra questions; 29% approved digitally; 78% patient satisfaction.; Integrated with HiX and Epic; won a German university hospital by direct award.; Consent with animation videos built into the flow.

- **Features:**

  - Multilingual questionnaire (PX04): E-POS questionnaire is multilingual; site in NL, EN, DE, FR, ES.
  - Informed consent with animation videos (digital consent) (CW05): Step 2 of E-POS; digital consent in Mannheim scope.
  - Digital patient information and video-based patient information (PX06): Animation videos; digital patient information.
  - Validated triage algorithm (TR01): Flags patients needing attention; routes to digital approval, telephone or outpatient consultation.
  - Remote/digital approval of fitness for surgery (TR05): 29% approved digitally (study claim).
  - Decision support: guideline references, suggested work-up/diagnostics, contraindications (TR02): Health report with triage advice.
  - Health report / EHR report with colour-coded indicators (CW04): Step 4 of E-POS.
  - Report written to the EHR (IN05): EHR report.
  - HiX and Epic integrations (IN01): First E-POS-HiX link at Dijklander; Haaglanden MC on HiX 6.3; Epic link configured by an Epic consultant.
  - HL7v2 (IN02): Required by Mannheim.
  - FHIR and REST (IN03): Required by Mannheim.
  - CE medical device (CS07): Described as a medical device; Mannheim required a CE-marked medical device.
  - NEN 7510 (CS10): Badge on the website.
  - ISO 27001 (CS02): One mention lists it; another says the site does not mention it; Mannheim required it.
  - Replaces the paper pre-op process ('from data capture to the doctor's decision') (CW09): Mannheim scope.
  - Custom 'other care pathways' (QC01): Offered besides pre-op.
  - Implementation support at no extra cost (CM04): Stated on the website.
  - Research partnerships (CM10): Erasmus MC since 2 June 2020 with about EUR 1m Health Holland study funding; Amsterdam UMC validation.

  - PDF/A archiving (IN05): Documents archived as PDF/A (Documents Desk).

  - KIS integration (IN01): KIS integration (iMedOne, i.s.h.med).
  - E-ConsentPro connect: Connector module.
  - Partnership with Doctolib (since Sept 2022): Subcontractor to Doctolib at Havelland.
  - Group frameworks across many hospitals (CW06): Sana group framework (~33 hospitals); Rhön 5 sites; Albertinen group of 5.

- **Products:** Ultraprep pre-procedure assessment suite: MyPreOp / MyPreOp+ (anaesthetist-led pre-op), MyPreOp LA (ophthalmology/generic), MyPreOp Kids, MyEndo, MyCardio/MyCardiology, MyIR, MyMRI; cloud patient questionnaires, clinical portal, built-in PMS and BI.
- **Integrations:** PAS demographics via HL7 v2.4 QBP_Q21 / QRY_A19; Documents (Clinical Summary Report) via HL7 v2.4 MDM_T02 to EPR/EDMS; SNOMED CT and ICD-10 coding; Two Windows Server 2016 integration/relay servers on trust premises, outbound-only; SSO; Waitlist integration (MyPreOp+); Data warehouse export for BI
- **Accreditations:** DTAC (self-declared) (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf); NHS DSP Toolkit (self-declared) (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf); DCB0129 (self-declared) (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf); ISO 27001 (certified 17 Jan 2024, British Assessment Bureau); G-Cloud 15 listing mentions ISO27001-based access reviews (https://www.ultramed.co/; https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/799143724896306); Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf; https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/736086290488261); MHRA medical device registration ref 6625 (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf); WCAG 2.1 AA, audited with the RNIB (https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf); B Corp (https://www.ultramed.co/); King's Award for Enterprise (https://www.ultramed.co/); Listed on G-Cloud 13 and G-Cloud 15 (product specification Sep 2025) (https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/e3b61de0-a98d-42a1-a6b9-d5c86600a54e; https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf)
- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 15 MyPreOp (799143724896306): per submission, falling with volume, £5.00 (250-499 a month) to £2.80 (5,000+), or £4.80 to £2.50 if paid annually in advance; minimum 250 uses a month; SMS £0.0237 per fragment above fair use; includes implementation, clinical portal, demographic and document integration, SSO and support. G-Cloud 15 MyPreOp+ (736086290488261): £6.25 down to £3.50 per submission (monthly in arrears) or £6.00 down to £3.125 per use (annual in advance), banded 250-5,000+ a month; minimum 250 uses a month; SMS £0.0237 above fair use; includes implementation, patient pathway, clinical portal, demographic, waitlist and document integration, and SSO. Contract values: annual licences about GBP 51k-92k; multi-year about GBP 74k/yr (NWAFT) to GBP 80k/yr (Worcestershire); mostly 12-month licence renewals, increasingly 3-year terms via Softcat on reseller frameworks.
- **Customers claimed:** Claims 800,000+ patients across 29 NHS trusts and health boards in England and Scotland; Royal Wolverhampton (34% more clinic capacity); London North West University Healthcare (40% more capacity; 10,000+ patients); Walsall Healthcare; Shrewsbury and Telford; NHS Tayside (MyPreOp provided by Ultramed on Tayside's behalf); NHS Grampian; Dorset County Hospital; Northampton General (trust page); University Hospitals of Leicester (trust page); UHDB board reports a 'My Preop' tool (HTN, Jan 2026); Partner of Xyla's digital pre-op service; Cork University Hospital (Ireland); ROI helpline; Australian subsidiary Ultraprep Pty Ltd
- **Differentiators:** Published per-submission pricing on G-Cloud 15 with implementation, integration, SSO and support included; MHRA-registered medical device; WCAG 2.1 AA audited with the RNIB; Broad specialty suite (endoscopy, ophthalmology, kids, cardiology, IR, MRI); Clinical logic: ASA, Rockwood frailty, task suggestions, NPSA steroid alert, prehab identification; 3-monthly re-contact while waiting (MyPreOp+), aligned to NHSE 5 core requirements claim; Bought quickly via Softcat on DWS2 / NOE TTS reseller frameworks; Displaced VitalHub at Worcestershire; B Corp; King's Award for Enterprise
- **Gaps stated by sources:** No NHS login or FHIR claimed (research review of G-Cloud 15 documents); No DTAC or DCB0129 claim seen on its product page (one review); other sources say these are self-declared on G-Cloud; Integration needs two Windows Server 2016 relay servers on trust premises; QEH King's Lynn: no renewal notice found after the contract ended 2025-03-31 (T052)
- **Features:**
  - Remote patient questionnaire (PX01): Cloud-hosted online pre-op questionnaire sent by a unique code over SMS/email.
  - Patient access by code + date of birth, save-and-resume: Patient access by unique (12-character) code plus date of birth; save-and-resume.
  - SMS/email invitations and reminders (PX03): Sent by SMS link/email; 3 daily automatic reminders; scheduled templated messaging tied to the TCI date.
  - Two-way SMS/email messaging (PX09): Two-way SMS/email messaging with scheduled templates.
  - Assisted and telephone completion (PX05): Clinician codes and in-person codes for assisted completion; telephone completion through the call centre (Dorset County Hospital).
  - Links to patient information and videos (PX06): Links to patient information and videos.
  - Branching questionnaire (QC02): Branching questionnaires; dynamic pathways.
  - ASA grade, risk scores and frailty (TR03): Questionnaire derives ASA grade and risk scores; Rockwood frailty.
  - Suggested tasks and actions (TR02): Suggests tasks (bloods, ECG) and actions (e.g. diabetic first on list).
  - NPSA steroid alert: NPSA steroid alert built in.
  - Automated screening and flags (TR01): MyPreOp+ automated screening when a decision to treat is made; auto-review of check-in responses with flags for clinical review.
  - Prehabilitation identification (TR04): MyPreOp+ identifies patients for prehabilitation.
  - Periodic re-contact while waiting (SW02): Automatic 3-monthly re-contact / follow-ups while waiting; recurring forms; tracking health changes on the waitlist.
  - Auto-send at decision to treat / auto-add patients: Questionnaire send triggered automatically at decision to treat; MyPreOp+ auto-adds patients.
  - Multiple forms per patient; pathways by procedure and priority: MyPreOp+ supports multiple forms per patient and pathways by procedure and priority.
  - Version change tracking (QC03): MyPreOp+ version change tracking.
  - Clinical portal worklists (CW01): Portal folders: Needs attention, Not started, In progress, Completed, Archived, Bin; tags; assignment to clinicians.
  - Clinical Summary Report (CW04): Clinical Summary Report.
  - Automatic export to EPR/EDMS (IN05): Clinical Summary Report exported automatically to the EPR/EDMS (HL7 v2.4 MDM_T02).
  - HL7 v2.4 (IN02): HL7 v2.4 demographics and document interfaces.
  - PAS demographics query (IN04): HL7 v2.4 QBP_Q21 / QRY_A19 demographics query; HL7 demographics feed.
  - SNOMED CT and ICD-10 coding (QC08): SNOMED CT and ICD-10 coding.
  - Single sign-on (IN07): SSO included in the G-Cloud price.
  - Waitlist integration: Waitlist integration included in the MyPreOp+ G-Cloud price.
  - Self-service BI and data warehouse export (CW07): Self-service BI with data warehouse export; built-in BI platform.
  - Built-in PMS: Built-in PMS.
  - Specialty pre-procedure questionnaires: MyEndo (endoscopy), MyPreOp LA (ophthalmology/generic), MyPreOp Kids, MyCardio, MyIR, MyMRI.
  - NHS England's 5 core requirements (claim) (CS11): MyPreOp+ listing claims to deliver 'NHS England's 5 core requirements'.
  - Cloud-hosted SaaS (HD01): Cloud-hosted patient questionnaire; hosted outside the NHS on Ultramed's servers (NHS Tayside page).
  - UK/EEA data on GCP (HD02): Hosted on GCP with UK/EEA data; UK public cloud.
  - On-premise integration relay servers: Needs two Windows Server 2016 integration servers on trust premises, outbound connections only.
  - WCAG 2.1 AA, RNIB audited (CS08): WCAG 2.1 AA, audited with the RNIB.
  - DTAC (self-declared) (CS05): Self-declared DTAC compliance.
  - DSPT (self-declared) (CS04): Self-declared NHS DSP Toolkit compliance.
  - DCB0129 (self-declared) (CS06): Self-declared DCB0129 compliance.
  - ISO 27001 (CS02): ISO 27001 (certified 17 Jan 2024, British Assessment Bureau).
  - Cyber Essentials / Plus (CS03): Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus.
  - MHRA-registered medical device (CS07): Registered with the MHRA as a medical device (ref 6625).
  - B Corp (CM09): B Corp.
  - Implementation, support and POA advice (CM04): Implementation, patient and staff support, POA advice; included in the per-submission price.
  - Anaesthetist-led clinical expertise (CM07): MyPreOp/MyPreOp+ described as anaesthetist-led pre-op; POA advice.
  - Framework routes (CM01): G-Cloud 13, G-Cloud 15; DWS2 and NOE TTS through Softcat; framework call-off at Worcestershire.
  - Reference sites with outcomes (CM02): Case studies: Royal Wolverhampton 34% more clinic capacity; London North West 40% more capacity, 10,000+ patients.
  - Board-wide roll-out (CW06): NHS Grampian rolling out to all adult POA clinics by end 2026; claims 29 trusts and boards.

- **Also known as:** Vitalhub UK Limited; VitalHub UK; Synopsis; Synopsis iQ; Synopsis Home; Synopsis Digital Pre-Operative Assessments; Intouch with Health / InTouch With Health (former name / trading name); eOutcomes; Novari; MyPathway; SHREWD; Induction Zesty (owned since June 2025)

- **Type:** pre-op specialist (also PROMs, patient flow and patient engagement via Induction/Zesty)
- **Products:** Synopsis digital pre-assessment (Synopsis iQ clinician platform, Synopsis Home patient questionnaire) for pre-op, endoscopy and paediatric pathways; eOutcomes (PROMs); patient flow/kiosks; SHREWD/OPEL dashboards; Novari patient access; owns Induction Healthcare (Zesty portal, Attend Anywhere).
- **Integrations:** PAS and EPR via FHIR/HL7 or CSV, bidirectional at data-item and document level; HL7 import/messaging; PDF outbound; Up to 2 interfaces included in the Pre-Screen module; Works as a PAS/EPR extension or standalone
- **Accreditations:** DCB0129 (G-Cloud 14 listing 233802663301544); MHRA registration (6625); CE marked (G-Cloud 14 listing 233802663301544); ISO/IEC 27001 (06/04/2023; BSI / British Assessment Bureau) (G-Cloud 14 listing 233802663301544); ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 (British Assessment Bureau, 30 Jul 2025) (G-Cloud 15 listing 214669371000433); Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus (G-Cloud 14 and 15 listings); DSPT org code 8JF22 (G-Cloud 14 and 15 listings); HSCN-connected; Tier 3 UK data centres; UK data residency (G-Cloud 15 listing 214669371000433); DTAC not stated (research_competitors (G-Cloud review)); G-Cloud 15; UK data storage (G-Cloud 15 listing (gap_England))
- **Pricing:** G-Cloud 14: £2.90 to £3.50 per unit. G-Cloud 15 Synopsis: £3.50 per pre-op (0–10,000), £3.20 (10,001–20,000), £2.90 (20,001+); implementation £10,000 a year plus 20% of year-one licence (as written). Pre-Screen module price includes hosting, iQ/Home question template, up to 2 interfaces plus PDF outbound, training and support. Pre-op call-offs seen at GBP 81k–124k.
- **Customers claimed:** More than 110,000 assessments a year in the NHS; average saving of £1.4m per trust a year (claims); 20% fewer last-minute cancellations and 94% less paper (G-Cloud listing claims); Northumbria Healthcare (launched Synopsis in 2022; Pre Assessment Software £123,985.08, Jul 2025–Jul 2027); Worcestershire Acute (£81,328.50, Feb–Oct 2024); NHS Highland (2023 launch); ROH/UHB eOutcomes (£85,550, 2025/26); Bahamas licensing deal reported; Many NHSE/ICB SHREWD and OPEL awards; Software licence payments over £25k at Epsom and St Helier, MTW, ESHT, BHRUT and RWT (product not shown)
- **Differentiators:** 250+ validated risk algorithms with NICE-based next-step suggestions; Coded output (ICD10, SNOMED, OPCS); MHRA-registered, CE-marked medical device with DCB0129; Sells both PROMs (eOutcomes) and pre-op assessment, a direct overlap with Preopsis; Owns Induction Healthcare (Zesty portal, Attend Anywhere) since June 2025; Low per-assessment price (£2.90–£3.50)
- **Gaps stated by sources:** Lost Worcestershire Acute to Ultramed after the Feb–Oct 2024 bridge contract (T099: replaced by Ultramed call-off C307884 from 2024-11-01); DTAC not stated on its G-Cloud listing; Neither the Northumbria nor the Worcestershire notice names the product
- **Features:**
  - Central electronic pre-op assessment system (CW09): Synopsis; works as a PAS/EPR extension or standalone; 94% less paper (claim).
  - Home-completed patient questionnaire (Synopsis Home) (PX01): Patient web questionnaire at clinic or home.
  - Simple patient questionnaire design (PX15): One question per page with yes/no/unsure answers.
  - Clinician pre-op management covering all assessments (CW03): Synopsis iQ: nursing, physical and anaesthetist assessments.
  - Clinical triage (TR01): Clinician triage; fast-tracking low-risk patients.
  - 250+ validated risk algorithms (TR03): ASA, STOP-BANG, P-POSSUM, POSPOM, SORT, frailty, cardiac and lung risk, mental capacity, mortality.
  - Decision support: NICE-based next steps (TR02): Algorithms suggest next steps, e.g. HbA1c for diabetics.
  - Fast-track low-risk patients (TR05): Fast-tracking low-risk patients.
  - ICD10, SNOMED and OPCS coding (QC08): Coded output.
  - Customisable questionnaires (QC01): Customisable questionnaires; iQ/Home question template included.
  - Messaging and reminders (PX03): Messaging and reminders in Synopsis iQ.
  - Reporting (CW07): SQL reporting database; real-time reporting.
  - Real-time clinician view (CW01): Real-time reporting and triage worklists.

## C. Every finding: policy, compliance, buyer patterns

### deep-read_1 (10)

- North West Anglia NHS FT direct-awarded Ultraprep annual support and maintenance (full implementation support, demographic integration, document upload integration, ongoing technical support for patients and staff, POA expertise) via Softcat under Digital Workplace Solutions 2: GBP 222,720, 2026-06-01 to 2029-05-31. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust awarded 'C307884 Digital Pre Op Solution' to Ultramed Ltd: GBP 240,000, 2024-11-01 to 2027-10-31, framework call-off. The renewal point is Oct 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- University Hospitals Dorset NHS FT bought a 12-month renewal of its MyPreOp online pre-op assessment tool through Softcat: GBP 92,160, 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31, framework call-off. The next renewal is due Mar 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2d78f3b3-5b19-4be3-86cf-3700525e3272)
- Somerset NHS FT awarded 'POAC Digital Solution - Pathpoint' to Open Medical: GBP 106,850, 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31, framework call-off, extension possible. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/1c16e332-f07c-4e99-b288-ff1e68cf56e1)
- Incumbent UK digital POA contracts are small annual or 2-to-3-year framework call-offs (G-Cloud, CDHS Integrated Health Economy, DWS2, DPS) or single tender actions, published only as award notices with no specification. These are bought by direct award, not open tender. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3f59eaa8-603e-4b0d-82f8-9b9dd6e99c4f)
- The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS FT (Birmingham) ran a pre-market engagement for a PROMs platform (Contracts Finder, published 2024-08-13). It notes that PROMs have been a nationally mandated data collection for all providers of NHS-funded care since April 2009, with paired questionnaires before and at least six months after surgery. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a5f1a235-f0a2-4b88-bd31-d8e8125ba487)
- The Ultraprep product specification (Sept 2025, G-Cloud 15) sets a bar for UK pre-op tools: DTAC, DSPT, DCB0129, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, MHRA medical device registration, WCAG 2.1 AA, HL7 v2.4 PAS and EDMS integration, and SNOMED CT/ICD-10 coding. [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf)
- The Pathpoint ePOA G-Cloud 14 listing prices the product at GBP 48,500 per instance per year and bundles digital consent capture with pre-op screening and anaesthetic escalation worklists. This shows consent being bundled into POA platforms. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/231234506205685)
- The Finnish wellbeing county Keski-Uusimaa bought its PROM platform through a restricted procedure: phased pilot, then optional expansion and continuous development; 40% price, 60% quality; a reserve supplier is named. The original 2021 estimate was EUR 2M. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/370574-2024)
- Hospital Universitario La Paz (Madrid) has bought PREMs/PROMs implementation as consecutive annual minor contracts of EUR 14,700 excl. VAT (CM 161/2022 and CM 129/2023), each with a single offer. [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D540_8933)

### deep-read_10 (8)

- South Tees Hospitals NHS FT ran an open tender for a 'Digital Consent and Sharing Decision Making Solution' on Atamis: GBP 135,018, deadline 2026-09-29, start expected January 2027, 36 months plus 2 x 12-month extensions, CPV 48180000. Status is closed with no award yet, so it is a near-term in-scope opportunity that may not be in the batch list. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Countess of Chester re-let its National Framework for Data Validation Services for 2025-05-04 to 2029-05-03 with Acumentice, Aire Logic, Answer Digital, Ideal Health Consultants and Insource Select. It is the route for RTT/PTL validation call-offs during PAS-to-EPR migrations (for example Princess Alexandra Hospital 2026). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7c2238df-5c23-4232-9498-1f60c9748cc9)
- The LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions (CDHS) framework (LPP/2024/005) is being used for direct awards on elective data quality and validation (NECS 2026, NUH 2026, Kingston and Richmond 2026). That makes it a likely route to market for perioperative and elective software. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4ac0cee4-f65c-4620-888c-f642b391b763)
- United Lincolnshire buys an electronic leaflet system 'to support patient in understanding proposed surgical procedures, treatments and associated care pathways' (GBP 129k, 2026-2029, awarded 2026-10-20). Procedure information is bought as a separate module next to consent and pre-op assessment. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/df666f8b-808a-4f66-9e88-472dc2ba2ecb)
- Barts Health bought e-consent for five North East London trusts (Barts, BHRUT, Homerton, NELFT, ELFT) at about GBP 45k a year on G-Cloud 13 (3+1 years). Consent is often bought for a whole system, at a modest annual value. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/6c82cb27-b277-42c4-b41f-8bb36547d70f)
- The EIDO G-Cloud 15 listing lists integration with pre-op assessment (POA) systems alongside EPR and PAS. The consent-content supplier positions itself as a partner to pre-op platforms, not a competitor. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063)
- NHS Devon's waiting-list validation software was bought to link the validation programme with the NHS App and to meet NHSE validation programme requirements. The contract ended 2026-09-12, so a renewal or replacement is likely due. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)
- Nottingham University Hospitals bought validation and correction of 72,000 RTT/PTL records to give clean cohorts for scheduling in its new EPR (MBI, GBP 397k, May 2026 to Feb 2027, CDHS direct award). EPR go-lives create one-off waiting-list data work. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/dd7782d7-b750-479d-9313-e0bd1c126e49)

### deep-read_11 (8)

- Rhön-Klinikum's direct-award justification says Thieme Compliance is the only full-range consent-form supplier (over 2,000 forms, more than 30 specialties, 20 languages) with over 90% DACH market share, and that switching would mean retraining all doctors. Content lock-in, not software, is the moat in German digital consent. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/238918-2024/xml)
- At Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein the patient-portal vendor (Dedalus) sends consent forms through the portal only with Thieme's consent system. This was used to justify a product-specific procurement (EUR 209,455, 3 years). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/673681-2026/xml)
- Sana Kliniken set a group-wide framework (max EUR 4.29m, 36 months from Nov 2024, rolling 12-month renewals, 6 months' notice) so every Sana hospital uses one uniform digital consent solution. Large private groups standardise centrally, and the 2027 renewal is the decision point. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/672595-2024/xml)
- Universitätsklinikum Mannheim directly awarded digital pre-operative screening ('Software Digitalisierung Prämedikation') to Dutch SME Novacair B.V. for 4 years. It required CE marking, ISO 27001, GDPR compliance and a bidirectional interface, and wanted to replace a paper-based, manual process with a validated, automated, interoperable system. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml)
- Universitätsklinikum Münster ran a market consultation (July 2026, responses due 4 Aug 2026) for an ERAS software solution. It wants digital support across the whole perioperative pathway, a web-based perioperative data platform, analytics, and migration of existing EIAS data. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/509259-2026/xml)
- Charité's open tender for digital consent drew only 1 bid. It weighted price to end-2025 at 30%, follow-on annual costs at 25%, optional Kann features at 20% and the implementation concept at 25%, with an unlimited term and rolling annual renewal. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/88646-2024/xml)
- KHZG funding category FTB2 drives tablet and hardware purchases specifically for digital patient consent (for example Gesundheit Nordhessen iPads 'für die digitale Patientenaufklärung im Rahmen des KHZG FTB2', and Erzgebirgsklinikum iPads). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/627898-2025)
- A TED API title search for 'Patientenaufklärung' since Oct 2023 returned 17 notices (for example AGAPLESION framework 382793-2024, Universitätsklinikum Halle 70031-2025, Kliniken Ostalb 466952-2025, SVD Austria 760405-2025). Digital consent tenders are frequent in DACH, and most awards seen go to the incumbent consent-content vendor. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/466952-2025)

### deep-read_12 (11)

- German digital-consent purchases since 2023 are dominated by one incumbent (Thieme Compliance E-ConsentPro). A TED full-text search for 'E-ConsentPro' since Oct 2023 returned 21 notices, many of them VEATs or direct awards extending existing paper-consent licences. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/705344-2024/xml)
- Eichsfeld Klinikum's VEAT says its anaesthesia information system (AIMS) only has an interface to the incumbent consent vendor, and that a market sounding of patient portals also found interfaces only to that vendor. Integration with the AIMS and patient portal is a gatekeeper for pre-op and consent products in Germany. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/705344-2024/xml)
- KHZG (Krankenhauszukunftsgesetz) funding drives these purchases. The Albertinen/Immanuel tender required KHZG-relevant operational readiness by 30 Sept 2025, and St. Joseph Berlin's award sits under KHZG Fördertatbestand 2 (patient portal). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/268718-2025/xml)
- Kliniken der Stadt Köln awarded 'Digitale Aufklärung, Einwilligung und Dokumentensignatur' (open procedure, 36 months) for EUR 883,780.91 in Aug 2025, after an earlier 'Digitale Aufklärung und Einwilligung' procedure (CN Nov/Dec 2024, notice 8848-2025). Tablets and signature pads were bought separately (722062-2025: Bechtle, ID Ausweissysteme). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/530180-2025/xml)
- A multi-hospital framework, 'digitale Behandlungsinformation und Aufklärungsvideos' (Klinikum Dahme-Spreewald, Sana hospitals, Herzzentrum Dresden and others), was awarded at EUR 4,294,108. The framework runs 36 months and renews automatically for 12 months unless cancelled 6 months before expiry. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/672595-2024/xml)
- Universitätsklinikum Mannheim published a VEAT for 'Software Digitalisierung Prämedikation' (pre-anaesthesia assessment digitisation) in Nov 2025. It requires a CE-marked medical device, ISO 27001 certification, GDPR compliance and a bidirectional interface to existing systems, replacing a paper-based, manually controlled process. This is a direct pre-op assessment buyer signal; the winner was not visible in the fields retrieved. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml)
- Universitätsklinikum Halle (Saale) awarded 'digitale Patientenaufklärung' (negotiated procedure with call) for EUR 338,287 (award notice Dec 2025). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/851883-2025/xml)
- German buyers often pair digital consent with patient portals and admission forms (SLK-Kliniken Heilbronn: consent plus admission forms with portal integration; GLG: consent framework tied to a central patient portal connecting KIS, LIS and archive). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/129435-2025/xml)
- In Spain, Castilla-La Mancha (SESCAM) bought a region-wide informed-consent document management and advanced digital signature platform (perpetual corporate licences plus 3 years of support) for EUR 596,123.51 (award 2026). Regional health services buy consent platforms centrally, while single hospitals use minor contracts under EUR 15k. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/335020-2026/xml)
- The Albertinen/Immanuel consent tender drew only one bid. Its selection criteria demanded 3 references of EUR 300k+ in German-speaking hospitals of 500+ beds, 5+ languages live and iMedOne or i.s.h.med integration, which are high barriers for new entrants. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/268718-2025/xml)
- NHS digital consent is bought by framework call-off with price-only award: Buckinghamshire Healthcare's Concentric contract was GBP 210k with a single tender. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/009469-2026)

### deep-read_13 (7)

- United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospitals replaced its one-year GBP 40.7k single tender action with a 3-year framework call-off (2026-07-31 to 2029-07-30), awarded 2026-10-20 and published 2026-10-22: 'System for providing electronic leaflets to support patient in understanding proposed surgical procedures, treatments and associated care pathways', value GBP 84.8k to 129.1k. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/df666f8b-808a-4f66-9e88-472dc2ba2ecb)
- South Tees Hospitals NHS FT ran an open tender (CPV 48180000, GBP 135,018) for a 'Digital Consent and Sharing Decision Making Solution': 36 months from January 2027 plus 2 x 12-month extensions, bids closed 2026-09-29 on Atamis, award not yet published. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Northern Ireland trusts justify direct awards for consent-information libraries on sole-supplier and continuity grounds ('to go with alternative supplier would result in considerable disruption'; 'not aware of any other provider'). This is the incumbent's lock-in pattern for a challenger to counter with evidence that alternatives exist. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/071397-2025)
- North East London trusts (Barts, BHRUT, Homerton, NELFT, ELFT) bought a shared digital consent solution through one Barts-led G-Cloud 13 call-off (about GBP 45k a year, 3+1 years from April 2024, to April 2028 at the latest). Groups of trusts in a system buy consent tools together. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/6c82cb27-b277-42c4-b41f-8bb36547d70f)
- Typical digital consent and consent-library contracts are small, about GBP 20k to 60k a year per trust, bought through G-Cloud 13/14, DPS call-offs, regional frameworks (e.g. OE Total Technology Solutions) or below-threshold direct awards. - Barnsley Hospital NHS FT bought 'Digital Consent Software' (e-consent implementation and licences) as a 5-year framework call-off: GBP 105k, 2025-09-29 to 2030-09-28. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7af91ea8-535a-4bc8-a105-48829a293c57)
- Nottingham University Hospitals bought a 'Medical Procedure Consent Library' through a DPS call-off: GBP 110k to 116k, 2026-01-31 to 2029-01-30, CPV 48517000/72261000. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/bff5a924-895a-42b6-ae71-99b815e69b36)

- German university hospitals are buying sqior's OR-coordination assistant mainly by single-source VEATs or PINs, each claiming technical exclusivity. TED lists 10 notices mentioning sqior (Dec 2024 to Aug 2026): MHH Hannover, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Rostock, Erlangen, LMU München, Bonn (market consultation and VEAT), Mainz and Mannheim. [source](https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search)
- Mannheim's VEAT (18/08/2026) for a digital OR assistant in its DC-OP went to sqior for 3 years. The price is unpublished by agreement between sqior and UMM, and the justification says a market consultation found only one product covering the full OR-coordination process. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/572086-2026/html)
- Mainz's PIN states that a market consultation rated sqior as currently the only product able to cover the whole day-of-surgery perioperative process. This leaves room for competition in pre-op and pre-day-of-surgery stages, which these notices do not cover. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/567501-2026/html)
- In Aragón's GUHARA-Q, the pre-anaesthetic assessment is done in the regional EHR (HCE) and sent to the surgical waiting-list system by HL7 (622 assessments in the Barbastro pilot). The PPT requires several users to be able to change a patient from 'not fit' to 'fit', so pre-op fitness is a status field in the scheduling system. [source](https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/wcm/connect/PLACE_es/Site/area/docAccCmpnt?srv=cmpnt&cmpntname=GetDocumentsById&source=library&DocumentIdParam=d7e64109-03e5-4acc-9014-a63d98d108f1)
- Spanish regional health services require HL7 v2.6 XML with ACKs, a regional patient ID (CIP) as primary key, EMPI QBP/RSP lookups and corporate AD/SSO sign-in for surgical-process systems. These are the integration expectations a pre-op product would face in Spain. [source](https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/wcm/connect/PLACE_es/Site/area/docAccCmpnt?srv=cmpnt&cmpntname=GetDocumentsById&source=library&DocumentIdParam=d7e64109-03e5-4acc-9014-a63d98d108f1)
- The GUHARA-Q tender scored 'number of hospitals where the bidder has implemented a solution similar to GuharaQ' at 10 of 100 points and price at 30. Only one bid was received. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/437423-2022/html)
- UK NHS eConsent support renewals are being published under the Procurement Act 2023 as below-threshold direct awards (UK7 contract details notices). Clatterbridge's runs 29 May 2026 to 28 May 2027 at about GBP 11.4k, which suggests small annual renewal cycles for digital consent. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/070372-2026)
- SERMAS hospitals are trialling AI surgical scheduling and pre-op tools through small minor contracts (under EUR 15k), such as La Princesa ophthalmology in 2025. [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D1452_2895)

VAT) runs to 2026-08-01 with one 12-month renewal to 2027-08-01, so it may come up for re-procurement by mid-2027. - Swedish regions buy self-monitoring (egenmonitorering) platforms regularly: Dalarna, Jämtland Härjedalen, Gävleborg, Uppsala, Halland, Örebro (IBD), Kalmar (joint procurement) 2024-25, and VGR's county-wide RFI (SEK 50m) in 2026. This is a large Nordic remote-monitoring market adjacent to post-discharge follow-up. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/272543-2026/xml)

### deep-read_19 (8)

- The current NHS LPP CDHS framework (awarded Oct 2024) has 81 suppliers. Those with perioperative, theatre, pre-op or patient-engagement products include Open Medical, Bluespier, Dendrite Clinical Systems, iMDsoft, DrDoctor, Patients Know Best, accuRx, Healthcall Solutions, Netcall, Mayden, MBI Healthcare Technologies, Nervecentre, Better, Alcidion, Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, System C and TPP. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032423-2024)
- CDHS supports direct award from a published national list-price catalogue as well as further competition. A pre-op SaaS listed on CDHS (or CDHS 2.0) can therefore be directly awarded by trusts without a full tender. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032423-2024)
- NHS trusts already buy electronic pre-op assessment (ePOA) SaaS as small annual CDHS call-offs, e.g. Princess Alexandra Hospital paid Open Medical GBP 74k (2025/26) and GBP 76k (2026/27) for Pathpoint ePOA Enterprise SaaS. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- CDHS 2.0 is expected to be worth GBP 2.4bn, possibly run 8 years, have its contract notice in early 2027 and go live around October 2027. The current CDHS ends in 2028. New suppliers cannot join the current CDHS mid-term. [source](https://www.publictechnology.net/?p=13604)
- The LPP page says CDHS is the only NHS CCF-accredited route to market for clinical systems, with suppliers tested to an 'FVRA gold level standard'. No DTAC, DSPT or Cyber Essentials condition is published on the page. [source](https://www.lpp.nhs.uk/categories-and-services/digital-technology-solutions/clinical-digital-health-solutions-cdhs/)
- CDHS is heavily used for EPR further competitions in 2026, e.g. Sherwood Forest (GBP 23.4m), Royal Orthopaedic Hospital (GBP 13.1m), Norfolk and Suffolk (GBP 3.15m) and Liverpool University Hospitals (GBP 53.6m). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/search_notices/json)
- Madrid hospital contracts require personal-data servers in the EU (mandatory for special-category health data), with the supplier acting as a GDPR Art. 28 processor and declaring server location and subcontracting. This is a data-residency requirement for Spanish perioperative software. [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/medias/anonpcap2o2024-4-14483406920pdf/download)
- Spanish anaesthesia departments use negotiated procedures without publication, on technical-exclusivity grounds, to extend incumbent perioperative systems once piloted (Ramón y Cajal MEDLINETEC: pilot in Feb 2024, then expansion to 98 posts with 100% price criterion and 1 offer). [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/medias/anonmemoriaexp20244000140pdf/download)

### deep-read_4 (10)

- Korbach's KHZG patient-portal contracts (m.Doc portal, Recare discharge) run 36 months from 28 Nov 2023 and auto-extend by 24 months unless terminated, so the renewal or exit point is around Nov 2026, i.e. now [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/283930-2023/xml)
- German KHZG portal tenders gate bidders on KIS-specific references (ORBIS at Korbach and Saarburg, NEXUS at Andernach and Odenwaldkreis), so integration references with the dominant KIS are the key qualifier [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/444820-2025/xml)

- Gematik INA working group on patient portals (Feb 2026): KHZG use cases link admission, discharge and appointment management (e.g. booking triggers the right consent form); FHIR is the target, but many KIS still use HL7 v2 instead of ISiK; patient-portal operation via gematik with eGK login possible since summer 2025 [source](https://www.ina.gematik.de/fileadmin/Arbeitskreisdokumente/Patientenportale/20260219_Protokoll_AK_Pat.Portale_INA.pdf)
- Dedalus (at the INA working group) describes the portal's 'fast lane': targeted pre-admission questions so better-prepared patients are admitted faster [source](https://www.ina.gematik.de/fileadmin/Arbeitskreisdokumente/Patientenportale/20260219_Protokoll_AK_Pat.Portale_INA.pdf)
- POLAVIS states its portal roadmap includes care pathways, service-group allocation and OP, resource and bed planning, moving portal vendors toward perioperative scheduling [source](https://polavis.de/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Patientenaufnahme-als-Startpunkt-der-uebergreifenden-Patientenreise-20260317.pdf)
- Swiss hospitals buy patient portals outside the KHZG model, with narrow first use cases (invoice copies at KSW and USB/myUSB); pre-op questionnaires are not yet named [source](https://www.unispital-basel.ch/en/patient-innen---besuchende/myusb)
- Havelland Kliniken (KHZG) patient portal tender required deep KIS integration and home completion of pre-existing condition, anamnesis and medication questionnaires sent to the ward [source](https://www.heuking.de/de/anwaelte/profil/projekte/projekt/beschaffung-und-einfuehrung-eines-patientenportals.html)
- Stadtkrankenhaus Korbach separately procured a PDMS including an anaesthesia information management system (AIMS) on ORBIS (2023), requiring ISO/IEC 80001-1 certification for the whole term [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/473071-2023/xml)

- West Hertfordshire Hospitals bought a 'Zesty Form Builder' (digital forms and questionnaires) for £100,000, 2024-03-31 to 2027-03-30, as a framework call-off. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/2ec6666c-bb54-4957-aeef-1ac9b334fb2a)
- Princess Alexandra Hospital switched portal suppliers from DrDoctor (G-Cloud 11, £60k, 2023–24) to Zesty. It also bought a separate CRIS-to-Zesty integration licence (£30.9k, 2025–26), so integration is costed separately from the portal licence. - Warrington & Halton's DrDoctor portal went live 12 June 2024. ### deep-read_8 (11)

- Dorset County Hospital's pre-operative assessment questionnaire is MyPreOp, provided by Ultramed on the trust's behalf. Patients get a unique code by SMS or email, it takes 30 to 60 minutes and saves progress, telephone completion is offered, and patients are told not to wait for an operation date to complete it. [source](https://dchft.nhs.uk/?p=177526)
- Universitätsklinikum Münster published a market consultation (PMC, 23 Jul 2026) for an ERAS software solution. Its minimum requirements for alternatives to Encare are ERAS Society partnership and certification, eleven specialty ERAS programmes plus ERAS Essentials, a digital prehabilitation module, an international audit and benchmarking platform, full migration of existing EIAS data, research infrastructure, and no extra implementation costs. It also asks about KIS interfaces, patient communication and monitoring, data protection, and licensing models. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/509259-2026)
- The Institute of Oncology Ljubljana awarded an open tender for the development, implementation and 7-year maintenance of an Onkološki kirurški modul (oncology surgical module) to FIDURO d.o.o. for EUR 935,188.56 (90 months). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/249188-2026)
- Contracts Finder notice b62c55b2 (DrDoctor patient portal, GBP 865,000, 27 Oct 2023 to 26 Oct 2028) belongs to Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust. The portal lets patients view records and results, update appointments and request changes to planned surgery dates. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/b62c55b2-5418-4845-9233-ad9840d42162)
- Hull University Teaching Hospitals awarded a DrDoctor patient engagement platform via G-Cloud 13 (RM1557.13), GBP 101,016, 30 Mar 2024 to 29 Mar 2025. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7bec8dbf-2dec-4213-b88c-bed546fcaeda)
- Gateshead Health published a separate GBP 37,000 Cancer Prehabilitation Programme (a structured 12-week pathway for 120 patients over 12 months) on 23 Jan 2026, with no supplier shown on the public page. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-060da0)
- In a feasibility study of Surgery Hero at the Northern Gynaecological Oncology Centre, Gateshead (Apr to May 2024), 15 of 29 eligible patients activated, with 93% participation and 4.5/5 satisfaction. The main barrier was a median of 20 days from consent to surgery. Licences cost GBP 150 + VAT each. [source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12441255/)
- Cheshire and Merseyside ICS extended the C2-Ai waiting-list risk-stratification model to all nine acute trusts (Sep 2023). It identifies prehabilitation needs and feeds a 'waiting well' programme; NHS England reported a two-thirds reduction in ICU need for the highest-risk patients and 125 bed-days saved per 1,000 patients. [source](https://cheshireandmerseyside.nhs.uk/posts/region-wide-ai-deal-to-help-tackle-waiting-lists-across-nine-nhs-trusts)
- Mid Cheshire Hospitals uses AI to pick higher-risk surgical patients, who are invited by SMS or email to 12 weeks of Surgery Hero digital coaching funded by Cheshire & Merseyside ICB (Feb 2025). [source](https://mcht.nhs.uk/news-and-events/news/ai-project-helps-trust-offer-free-digital-health-coaching-surgery-patients)
- Buyer pattern: several NHS digital prehab buys are small, 12-month, below-threshold direct awards with no competition (West Herts GBP 51k, Gateshead GBP 19k), so renewals come round each year without a tender. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/083730-2025)
- University Hospitals Plymouth contracted QuestPrehab for a year-long digital prehab trial for liver-transplant waiting-list patients (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset). [source](https://htn.co.uk/2024/07/17/telehealth-provider-chosen-for-digital-prehab-trial-in-devon-cornwall-and-somerset/)

- Princess Alexandra Hospital contracted the Zesty patient engagement portal for GBP 155,000 via an NHS SBS framework call-off, to end of March 2027. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/07/14/princess-alexandra-hospital-contracts-patient-engagement-portal/)

- TRUST MAP – Hull University Teaching Hospitals (and the Humber and North Yorkshire partners York and Scarborough, Harrogate and NLaG): a digital pre-assessment pathway on Patients Know Best questionnaires (HTN 2023). The PKB portal was re-awarded 2025-03-31 to 2027-03-30, GBP 669,927, as a direct award under NHS SBS TECS 2. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/05/05/deep-dive-coverage-benefits-and-research-on-patient-portals/)
- TRUST MAP – Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust: the patient portal launched through the NHS App in Dec 2023 lets patients complete health questionnaires before pre-assessment appointments. The supplier is not named in HTN. Isla and Concentric list Bucks on their websites. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/12/15/buckinghamshire-healthcare-launches-new-patient-portal-via-nhs-app/)
- TRUST MAP – The Rotherham NHS FT: its EPR is Meditech, extended to 18 Mar 2028 (option to 2030) while it tenders for a new EPR. Its pre-op assessment pathway has 'entered its first phase', and pre-assessments are now supported through the NHS App. The trust has bought several Netcall patient-hub modules. This is an early-stage pre-op opportunity tied to the EPR re-procurement. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/03/09/the-rotherham-nhs-extends-epr-contract-to-2028-to-prepare-and-tender-for-new-epr/)
- TRUST MAP – Kingston and Richmond NHS: plans to add a digital pre-op triage health form to its patient portal (board, Jan 2026) alongside a planned re-procurement of its integrated acute and community EPR. No standalone pre-op supplier was found. Concentric lists Kingston as a consent customer. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/01/28/7-million-investment-approved-for-robotic-process-automation-ai-data-cloud-at-kingston-and-richmond-nhs/)
- TRUST MAP – South West London ICS: patient engagement portal work at its three Oracle/Cerner sites includes a pilot of NHS App pre-operative questionnaires. This is the route native to the EPR and the NHS App. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2025/02/24/south-west-london-icss-digital-strategy-for-2025-2028-infrastructure-integrating-systems-ai-framework-data-strategy-and-innovation/)
- POSSIBLE GREENFIELD (with caveats) – In the over-GBP 25k spend files checked (data.gov.uk links, roughly 2023–2026), no payment to any pre-op supplier was found for: Portsmouth Hospitals UHT (only Concentric consent through Softcat and a Healthcare Communications portal), Dudley Group (PKB GBP 160k Jul 2026; Healthcare Communications), Isle of Wight (Healthcare Communications), Milton Keynes UH (Zesty portal only), East Sussex Healthcare (PKB portal, Netcall, Accurx) and United Lincolnshire (Eido, Open Medical MSK, Netcall). Payments under GBP 25k or through resellers would not show, and vendor websites (e.g. Isla) list some of these trusts. [source](https://www.mkuh.nhs.uk/document/mkh_spend_01-feb-2024_to_29-feb-2024)
- PURCHASE ROUTES – Every pre-op purchase found in England was a call-off from an existing framework, mostly direct awards, and published after award. Routes: a direct award at Worcestershire, G-Cloud, Digital Workplace Solutions 2 through Softcat (NWAFT), an unnamed framework through Softcat (UHD), and the CDHS for the Integrated Health Economy framework (PAHT). Since 2023-10 no English acute trust ran an open competition for pre-op; South Tees used an open procedure only for consent/SDM. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- RESELLER EFFECT – Softcat is the named supplier on Contracts Finder for at least three peri-op software buys: Ultraprep at NWAFT, MyPreOp at UHD and Concentric e-consent at PAHT. Portsmouth's spend file also shows Concentric paid through Softcat (Apr 2023). Searching by vendor name alone undercounts these sales. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/0d978ff9-f1e5-44a0-87c9-af3e7827f57d)
- PRICE BENCHMARKS – Annual software cost for digital POA in English acute trusts runs about GBP 51k–92k: QEH Ultraprep GBP 51.3k, Somerset Pathpoint about GBP 53k/yr, Northumbria VitalHub about GBP 62k/yr, PAHT Pathpoint GBP 74–76k, NWAFT Ultraprep about GBP 74k/yr, Worcestershire Ultramed about GBP 80k/yr, UHD MyPreOp GBP 92k. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- RENEWAL CALENDAR – Upcoming expiries of pre-op contracts: UHD MyPreOp 2027-03-31, PAHT Pathpoint 2027-03-31, Northumbria VitalHub 2027-07-05 (no extension), Worcestershire Ultramed 2027-10-31 (no extension), Somerset Pathpoint 2028-03-31, NWAFT Ultraprep 2029-05-31. NHS Devon's Netcall waiting-list validation ended 2026-09-12. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- MARKET STATEMENT – Open Medical says Pathpoint is used across 150+ NHS sites by 25,000 daily active clinicians. Concentric says 35+ NHS trusts use its consent product trust-wide. Induction says 70% of NHS trusts use its products. DrDoctor says 70+ trusts and health boards. Surgery Hero was implemented by 18 trusts. These are vendor claims and are not specific to pre-op. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/602302860349329)
- POLICY DRIVER – NUH's pre-op matron describes centralised POA teams working to implement the NHSE pre-screening and optimisation mandate. MyPreOp+ on G-Cloud says it is built to the NHS England 5 core requirements, with screening at decision to treat, 3-monthly follow-up and prehab identification. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/736086290488261)
- G-CLOUD 15 PRE-OP CATALOGUE (Lot 2b SaaS): Ultramed MyPreOp+ and Ultraprep, Open Medical Pathpoint ePOA and SurgiCare, VitalHub Synopsis, Aire Logic/Aire Innovate AireFrame ePOA, Isla Digital Pathway Platform (Acute), Rumi Medtech Remcare, Ufonia Dora, Concentric, Pathpoint eConsent, EIDO Inform, Surgery Hero, PreActiv and Pathpoint eScreening. The G-Cloud route is open to any supplier listed on it. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/214669371000433)

### gap_France,_Spain_and_Italy (15)

- Resah's 2025 innovation catalogue (2024-R063, 17 lots) awarded on 2025-04-28. Consent management went to DrData, PROMs to SKEZI and PREMs to BETTER WORLD, each at EUR 10M maximum. The operating-theatre flow and coordination lot (010) closed without a winner. French hospitals can buy these without their own tender. [source](https://boamp-datadila.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/boamp/records?where=idweb%3D%2225-68840%22)
- Resah 2026-R035 is a single-supplier, end-to-end patient-pathway framework with AI modules: EUR 80M estimated, EUR 250M maximum, up to 73 months from 2026-12-01. Resah justified the long term because the AI modules may not be on the market at notification. [source](https://boamp-datadila.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/boamp/records?where=idweb%3D%2226-63480%22)
- UniHA's SAD M_3399 (EUR 30M estimated, open until June 2031) is the open route for new digital care-pathway vendors to get referenced with UniHA. Members run specific contracts and invite every admitted operator. Seven operators were admitted by March 2026. [source](https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr/index.php?page=Entreprise.EntrepriseDownloadReglement&id=Mjc5MzYzMw==&orgAcronyme=x7c)
- CAIH carries a digital medical consent offer: CHU Toulouse bought 'CAIH Consentement Médical' from Docaposte for EUR 470,000 (2025). The CAIH contracts visible in DECP are otherwise mostly infrastructure. [source](https://tabular-api.data.gouv.fr/api/resources/22847056-61df-452d-837d-8b8ceadbfc52/data/?objet__contains=CAIH)
- French pre-admission and follow-up incumbents are often renewed by negotiated award without competition, e.g. CHU Limoges–Exolis ENGAGE (pre-admission module) and AP-HP–Calmedica Memoquest (EUR 2.27M). Market entry depends on catalogue referencing or the incumbent's renewal date. [source](https://tabular-api.data.gouv.fr/api/resources/22847056-61df-452d-837d-8b8ceadbfc52/data/?titulaire_nom__contains=EXOLIS)
