- Calmedica says it is referenced with UniHA, RESAH and CAIH, holds ISO 27001 and HDS, integrates with Orbis, DxCare, Easily, Hopital Manager, Xplore+ and Sillage via HL7/API/EAI, and serves 200+ establishments. [source](https://www.calmedica.com/services/memoquest)
- Maela's website lists only CAIH and 'Upag' as purchasing channels, with ISO 13485 and Spain's ENS, and names no customers. [source](https://www.maela.fr/)
- Hopi Médical's site describes assisted teleconsultation (Clinic Alpha), not pre-op or pre-admission, so it is probably not a direct competitor. [source](https://www.hopimedical.com/)
- Italian buyers mostly buy surgical-pathway and OR software through orders under Consip 'Sanità Digitale' frameworks, so many CIGs cite framework codes (8765571A03, 9030521DAA, 903054517C, 9820895AED, 9188224A4D). A pre-op SaaS would usually need to sit inside a Consip framework holder's offer or come in below the direct-award threshold. [source](https://dati.anticorruzione.it/opendata/download/dataset/cig-2023/filesystem/cig_csv_2023_12.zip)
- ERAS programmes are a growing purchase category in Italy: ASST Valcamonica EUR 635,800 (2026), Niguarda EUR 210,000 (2025), AO Brotzu EUR 180,000, FTGM EUR 120,000 for 36-month ERAS® certification, AUSL Romagna ERAS audit via Medtronic EIAS, and ULSS 2 DREAM ERAS teleconsultation (B. Braun). [source](https://dati.anticorruzione.it/opendata/download/dataset/cig/filesystem/20261001-cig_csv.zip)
- Niguarda (Milan) is extending its Smart Data Platform/INVITA360 for a prericovero (pre-admission) project, worth EUR 323,000 (2026-08). This is the clearest Italian digital pre-op signal found. [source](https://dati.anticorruzione.it/opendata/download/dataset/cig/filesystem/20260901-cig_csv.zip)
- Brescia's OR and surgical-pathway tender sets the specification norms for Lombardy: SISS-signed operating reports, HL7 under the regional AS-PS_R-SEHL7#01, servers in ARIA cloud only, offline mode, waiting-list alarms using ASA class, and ECM-accredited training. [source](https://www.asst-spedalicivili.it/system/files/bando_gara/files/9113/17284/82628_20261002133138_signed.pdf)
- In Spain, digital informed consent is a regional-scale purchase dominated by Plexus (Assentio): SESCAM, Canarias and Murcia. SESCAM's 2025 tender scored @Firma signature support, biometric pads and roll-out to 45–50 services. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/335020-2026/xml)
- Spanish digital surgical-block buys found are patient tracking (RTLS at Hospital del Mar, Parc Taulí, MySphera at CSI) and planning (CIRUS in the Basque Country). No public pre-anaesthesia or pre-op questionnaire tender was found in TED or in the scanned PLACSP aggregated and minor-contract feeds. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414800-2025/xml)
- The IOV Padova 'preospedalizzazione' contract (TED 689852-2023, EUR 960,000) is outsourced front- and back-office staff, not software, so it was excluded. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/689852-2023/xml)

### gap_Ireland (20)

- The HSE Health App now shows hospital appointments shared by 36 public hospitals, 23 community services and two surgical hubs (Cork and Swords). It also shows inpatient/day-case waiting lists with priority status (no wait time), discharge summaries and GP referrals. 'Coming soon' items include checking wait times and 'reading information before and after appointments'. The app does not mention pre-op questionnaires. [source](https://www2.hse.ie/health-app/about-your-hse-health-app/)
- PQ 40643/26 (27 May 2026): St James's has almost completed its EHR with no patient portal. The Minister says a St James's portal proposal is 'under consideration', questions separate portals and logins per hospital, expects the new children's hospital portal to be popular with parents, and points to the HSE Health App and National Shared Care Record. The question also says the One Health Record procurement is expected to extend to 2027. [source](https://data.oireachtas.ie/akn/ie/debateRecord/dail/2026-05-27/writtens/mul@/dbsect_302.xml)
- National EHR (One Health Record): after vendor shortlisting and Gate 2 approval, competitive dialogue could take about 12 months, followed by Gate 3. Investment then extends over 7–10 years with incremental delivery. Health regions take part in selection with the aim of ONE system for all six regions. [source](https://data.oireachtas.ie/akn/ie/debateRecord/dail/2026-07-28/writtens/mul@/dbsect_3245.xml)
- Minister's list of Irish public hospitals with EHRs (Jul 2026): St James's (enterprise EHR); MN-CMS in five stand-alone maternity hospitals plus the Kerry maternity unit; National Rehabilitation Hospital; National Forensic Mental Health Service; CHI implementing an enterprise EHR before the new children's hospital opens. Other sites have only digitised parts of the patient journey. [source](https://data.oireachtas.ie/akn/ie/debateRecord/dail/2026-07-28/writtens/mul@/dbsect_3227.xml)
- In May 2025, PQs from Deputy Pádraig Rice asked CHI's pre-operative assessment protocols for spinal fusion and growth-rod surgery: how long an assessment stays valid, time between assessment and surgery, and repeat assessment after cancellation. In June 2026 Deputy Cullinane asked how many of 126 children on the CHI spinal waiting list had completed pre-op work-up. Pre-assessment validity and readiness are live political issues in paediatrics. [source](https://data.oireachtas.ie/ie/oireachtas/question/2025-05-27/pq_730)
- PQ 43587/26 (9 Jun 2026) asked whether SMS reminders, waiting-list validation, digital appointment systems or patient portals had been formally evaluated for cutting non-attendance. The Minister referred it to the HSE as a service matter, so no national evaluation was cited. [source](https://data.oireachtas.ie/akn/ie/debateRecord/dail/2026-06-09/writtens/mul@/dbsect_1823.xml)
- HSE purchase orders over EUR 20k for Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 show no line for Ultramed, Oneview, Patients Know Best, EIDO, Concentric, DrDoctor, Netcall, Zesty or Marino. Digital-health engagement lines that do appear: myPatientSpace, Open Medical (OLOL, Cavan), Swiftqueue, patientMpower, Doccla, Dendrite, Qualtrics, DocuSign (EUR 80,678 ICT subscription), System C/Careflow (about EUR 852k once-off licences Q4 2025), Cerner, Dedalus, InterSystems, Clanwilliam. The file does not name the hospital. [source](https://about.hse.ie/publications/payments-to-suppliers-purchase-orders-over-20000-q4-2025)
- The HSE Q1 2026 purchase-order file (over EUR 20k) is published as CSV on about.hse.ie. Earlier quarters (2024–Q3 2025) could not be found at the same URL pattern. [source](https://about.hse.ie/publications/payments-to-suppliers-purchase-orders-over-20000-q1-2026)
- St Vincent's University Hospital Q1 2026 payments over EUR 20k list iMDsoft (perioperative/critical care clinical information system vendor) and Trend Care Systems, among others. No pre-op, consent or PROMs vendor appears. [source](https://www.stvincents.ie/app/uploads/2026/04/SVUH-Q1-2026-Payments-over-E20k.pdf)
- Mater Misericordiae University Hospital ran a 2023 tender to replace its PatientCentre PAS/EPR but could not award it for budget reasons. In Dec 2024 it direct-awarded Dedalus EUR 1.4m over 4 years to move PatientCentre to the cloud; any replacement will need a full tender. The Mater has no modern EPR to embed pre-op functions, so a standalone pre-op tool would be needed. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/789956-2024)
- Royal Victoria Eye & Ear Hospital VEAT (Aug 2024): its bespoke CAPAS PAS reached end of life 10 years earlier and is top of the risk register. It has waited for the HSE iPMS since 2017, and PFH got EUR 324,000 for support and migration. This shows how slowly Irish voluntary hospitals replace core systems. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/520980-2024)
- HSE National Shared Care Record (HSE 21246): competitive dialogue awarded to Ernst and Young (as named on TED) at EUR 81.7m for 20 years (contract 18 Mar 2025). It aggregates hospital, GP and community records for clinicians and for patients at the point of care and self-care, making it a possible patient-facing channel alongside the HSE Health App. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/387406-2025)
- HSE Critical Care Clinical Information System awarded to Uniphar Medtech Ltd t/a Cardiac Services, EUR 7.08m (contract 20 Feb 2025, 4 tenders). The HSE reserved the right to reuse the outcome across HSE and HSE-funded hospitals. National framework-style reuse is a common HSE buying pattern. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/194830-2025)
- St Vincent's University Hospital published a preliminary market consultation (Sep/Oct 2026, est. EUR 300k) for moving from paper-based to electronic referrals with configurable workflows for National Cancer Care Pathways. Pathway-digitisation PMCs are how SVUH tests the market before tendering. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/681141-2026)
- Private sector: the My Mater Private app (registration by MRN) covers appointment requests, confirm/cancel/reschedule, bills and receipts. It has no pre-admission forms, questionnaires or test results, so Mater Private shows no digital pre-op capability. [source](https://www.materprivate.ie/mymaterprivate)
- Private sector: UPMC Sports Surgery Clinic arranges pre-operative assessment by phone or letter 2–3 weeks before surgery, as an in-person nursing and medical review lasting 1–2 hours. No online questionnaire is described. [source](https://www.sportssurgeryclinic.com/services/pre-assessment-clinic/)
- Public Mater Misericordiae pre-operative assessment clinic page describes an in-person nurse assessment (history, allergies, lifestyle, fasting information) and no online form. [source](https://www.mater.ie/services/pre-operative-assessment-clinic/)
- Swiftqueue (online appointment booking, used in Irish hospitals) lists Dedalus Healthcare Ireland Ltd as its Irish contact entity, so it is now part of the Dedalus portfolio. [source](https://www.swiftqueue.com)
- Open Medical's site carries a testimonial from University Hospital Limerick (HSE) on Pathpoint eTrauma: real-time documentation from A&E to wards to theatre, plus a Procedure Planner workspace. Open Medical runs an Irish entity, Open Medical (Europe) Ltd, Dublin 2. [source](https://www.openmedical.co.uk)
- Patients Know Best's only Irish contract found is St Patrick's Mental Health Services (2020, three years). HSE Living Labs piloted PKB with Full Health Medical in 2022. No acute hospital pre-op use was found. [source](https://patientsknowbest.com/2020/07/02/st-patricks/)

### gap_Netherlands_and_Belgium (16)

- Buyer pattern (NL): in the UMCG VEAT, UMCG states that the two general hospitals joining its Epic EPD (OZG and Treant) 'zijn niet aanbestedingsplichtig' (are not bound by procurement law). This is why digital pre-op tools at Dutch general and STZ hospitals don't appear on TenderNed; only the UMCs publish. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/395484)
- The Gerechtshof Arnhem-Leeuwarden (ECLI:NL:GHARL:2026:2351, reported 22 April 2026) overturned ChipSoft's injunction and lifted the EUR 100,000/day penalty. UMCG, OZG and Treant need not re-tender the shared Epic EPD, because the 2015 tender included the regional option. Treant is shown as a NovaCair E-POS logo customer, so its pre-op tooling may move with the Epic switch. [source](https://www.dutchitchannel.nl/news/730331/chipsoft-verliest-hoger-beroep-over-regionaal-pati%C3%ABntendossier)
- MUMC+ (Maastricht) awarded its ZIS/EPD lot to EPIC Europe B.V. (contract 2023-03-27, 10 years with extension option). MUMC+ pre-op tooling will be decided inside the Epic programme. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/293380)
- Diakonessenhuis runs digital pre-op screening on ChipSoft HiX triage. The questionnaire gives a provisional ASA score: ASA 1-2 are usually assessed digitally, ASA 3-4 get a phone or in-person visit. 55% of screenings have been fully digital since Feb 2024. The BeterDichtbij app sends reminders, including for informed consent, and Indiveo provides anaesthesia videos. [source](https://www.conclusion.com/en-nl/cases/diakonessenhuis-digitises-preoperative-screening)
- Wilhelmina Ziekenhuis Assen started E-POS digital pre-op screening in June 2024. The system advises whether extra tests are needed. A post-discharge 'Thuismeten' app is monitored by Altide medical service centre. [source](https://www.skipr.nl/nieuws/wza-gaat-patienten-digitaal-begeleiden-rond-operatie/)
- Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep emails an 'E+POS' questionnaire, to be completed within 2 days and before the pharmacy appointment. It is available in 9 languages and followed by videos on lifestyle rules and anaesthesia techniques; the patient consents to the anaesthesia technique through the questionnaire. Email and mobile are checked in the Mijn Noordwest portal. [source](https://www.nwz.nl/media/vqold0u1/nwz-11501-nl.pdf)
- Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis does pre-op screening mainly by a 10-20 minute phone call, with an in-person visit if the anaesthetist requires it. Its portal is MijnJBZ, the 'HiX Patiënt' app. [source](https://www.jeroenboschziekenhuis.nl/afdelingen/preoperatieve-screening-pos/pdf)
- Bravis: patients complete the pre-op questionnaire before the POS clinic, at home through MijnBravis with DigiD or at the hospital with help. An anaesthesia assistant reviews it and decides on extra tests (bloods, ECG, specialist referral). [source](https://www.bravis.nl/1/webcore/leaflet/pdf/3892)
- Albert Schweitzer ziekenhuis emails a link to a health questionnaire with anaesthesia information. The answers decide whether a separate POS appointment is needed; kiosks and help are available at the Dordwijk, Sliedrecht and Zwijndrecht sites. [source](https://asz.nl/files/folder.php?id=881)
- Belgium: Sint-Trudo Ziekenhuis uses a digital pre-operative questionnaire in mynexuzhealth, required for every procedure and including home medication, which is filed in the patient record. This shows the EPR-native route at nexuzhealth KWS hospitals. [source](https://www.sint-trudo.be/sites/default/files/public/mcm_plus/00226-NL.pdf)
- AZORG currently sends patients to their GP for pre-op tests, using the KCE pre-op infographic and app. It does the anaesthesia consultation only when needed and asks patients to complete a medical questionnaire. The new digital pre-op tender would move this in-house and online. [source](https://www.azorg.be/nl/professional/huisartsen/preoperatieve-medicatie-onderzoeken)
- Upcoming Belgian EPR decisions that will set the pre-op choice: (1) CHU de Liège competitive dialogue for one integrated DPI for the ELIPSE network hospitals (contract notice 2026-06-03); (2) Clinique Saint-Pierre Ottignies DPI (contract notice 2025-09-02, 12 years, criteria include TCO, DPI quality, hosting, sustainability); (3) Clinique Saint-Jean joining Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc's DPI through horizontal cooperation within H.uni (VEAT 2025-10-16); (4) ISoSL Liège DPI (open procedure, deadline 2026-04-24, 5 years). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/379038-2026)
- AZ Jan Palfijn Gent awarded a single-supplier framework for an integrated EPD to ChipSoft ZIS B.V., award value EUR 117,626,479.61, concluded 2026-07-24, 10 years per the PIN. Pre-op screening there will default to HiX. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/646663-2026)
- Belgian purchase routes: hospital tenders run on 3P (cloud.3p.eu, with reCAPTCHA) or the BOSA e-Procurement workspace. Purchasing centres seen: HeCaPP (anaesthesia software awarded to ICARE) and MercurHosp (only pharmacy flow-traceability software in the IT categories, not perioperative). No Mediq framework award lists were found. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/632883-2025)
- The Epic hospitals' association in NL (Epic Vereniging NL), led by Amsterdam UMC, consulted the market in October 2024 on an API-management platform for Epic hospitals, a shift from HL7/EDIFACT to APIs. This matters for how third-party pre-op tools integrate with Epic sites. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/353322)
- NovaCair's HiX integration runs through the ChipSoft Zorgplatform connection, included with HiX Standard Content 6.1-6.3. A completed questionnaire creates a task on the clinician's worklist, and the E-POS report is viewable from HiX. [source](https://novacair.com/koppelingen/chipsoft/)

### gap_No_renewal_or_expiry_dates_on_awarded_contracts (14)

- Renewal calendar summary. About 45 contracts in scope end or reach a decision point between Nov 2026 and Dec 2028. The re-procurement window for 18 of them (end minus 9 to 6 months) has already passed or is open now (Oct 2026). Examples: UHD MyPreOp (ends 2027-03-31), PAHT Pathpoint ePOA (2027-03-31), PAHT Concentric (2027-03-31), WHHT Zesty form builder (2027-03-30), W&H/UHNM/SEHSCT/Clatterbridge consent licences (Dec 2026 to Jun 2027), NNUH PROMs (2027-05-31), Northumbria Vitalhub pre-assessment (2027-07-05) and Gateshead Surgery Hero (2026-11-19). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2d78f3b3-5b19-4be3-86cf-3700525e3272)
- Pre-op assessment renewal pipeline 2026-2028 (actual end dates): UHD MyPreOp 2027-03-31; PAHT Pathpoint 2027-03-31; Northumbria Vitalhub 2027-07-05; Worcestershire Ultramed 2027-10-31; Somerset Pathpoint 2028-03-31. NWA Ultraprep runs to 2029-05-31 and EDV UpHill to about 2029-09 (estimated). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- Several trusts publish pre-op awards months in arrears. PAHT's 2025/26 Pathpoint award was published on 2026-03-19, near the end of its term, and the 2026/27 award on 2026-10-01. Northumbria's Vitalhub award was published on 2026-01-28 for a term that started 2025-07-06. Notice-watching alone will therefore miss renewal windows, so contract end dates are the better trigger. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3f59eaa8-603e-4b0d-82f8-9b9dd6e99c4f)
- QEH King's Lynn bought Ultraprep licences each year with falling spend (2022/23 £137,854.20; 2023/24 £74,856.96; 2024/25 £51,300). No 2025/26 or 2026/27 notice exists on Contracts Finder, so the account may have lapsed or be running on unpublished renewals, and it is worth approaching. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2a16f909-6217-466a-8958-111cacff13b8)
- ESNEFT bought 'Digitisation of Pre-Operative Assessment' (CA7369) via Softcat for £276,000: 3 years from 2020-09-01 with an option of 24 more months (maximum about 2025-09-01). No successor notice was found on Contracts Finder, so this is another possibly lapsed or unpublished pre-op renewal. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/33e19a48-8a0e-4f96-abaf-c7db9f244637)
- Chesterfield (DSFS) held MyPreOp software from 2020-02-01 to 2024-01-31 (£129,199), and Dorset County Hospital held UltraPrep/MyPreOP licences from 2022-03-30 to 2024-03-29 (£76,800). Neither has a published successor on Contracts Finder, so both are possible renewal or replacement targets. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/d81390f5-8fdf-4571-b7b8-2f865a6eedb4)
- ULHT turned a one-year single-tender Eido consent-leaflet licence (2025/26, £40,701.80) into a 3-year framework call-off (2026-07-31 to 2029-07-30, up to £129,130.27). The notice was published 2026-10-22, nearly 3 months after the term started. This is a pattern of 1-year pilots converting to 3-year terms. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/df666f8b-808a-4f66-9e88-472dc2ba2ecb)
- The NHS Devon waiting-list validation contract with Netcall (£132,195, required NHS App linkage) expired on 2026-09-12. No re-procurement or extension notice is on Contracts Finder, so this is a live opening. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)
- The All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, £11.9m awarded) was set up for '3 years with an option to extend for a year' (48 months) from 13 Oct 2023. Its initial term ended about Oct 2026 and the maximum runs to about Oct 2027, so an all-Wales PROMs re-procurement is likely during 2027. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/031093-2022)
- The NHS England Outcomes and Registries transition contract with NEC (£4.16m) ends 2027-09-30, so the national PROMs/registries platform replacement must be in market by about Q1 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9)
- ULS Coimbra (Portugal) renewed UpHill Route 'Percurso Clínicos Integrados Peri-Operatório' maintenance and licensing by direct award: EUR 139,650 for 1096 days from 2025-11-03, so it ends about 2028-11-03 (estimated). Portuguese perioperative-pathway buyers renew incumbents by direct award on 3-year cycles. [source](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=11991481)
- German consent and portal contracts typically have a 36-month minimum term with automatic 12-month renewal unless cancelled 3 to 6 months before the term ends (Albertinen group, Sana framework, Charité). The real decision point is therefore the cancellation deadline, not the end date. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/672595-2024)
- Procurement Act UK7 'contract details' notices on Find a Tender now carry explicit contract dates and extension headroom for small below-threshold renewals: Gateshead Surgery Hero £19k, NNUH PROMs £15.4k, CoCH Eido with extension to 2030-05-13. FTS has become the main source for small renewals since Feb 2025. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/058752-2026)
- Other perioperative-adjacent contracts found while dating records (not in the existing set): Walton Centre DrDoctor platform 2024-03-31 to 2026-03-30 (£148,425); Newcastle radiology DrDoctor portal from 2024-12-31 (£148,073); WSFT Synertec patient communication 2025-07-01 to 2026-10-31 (£700,000). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/search_notices/json)

### gap_Scotland,_Wales_and_Northern_Ireland (11)

- No national pre-op triage contract exists in Scotland. NSS's 2023 PIN (NP510123) combined a National Pre-op Assessment online triage solution with theatre scheduling, but only theatre scheduling was tendered (NP510124, Nov 2023) and awarded (Infix, May 2024). Boards have since bought pre-op tools locally. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/035364-2023)
- Scottish board pre-op tools as found: Tayside and Grampian use Ultramed MyPreOp; Lanarkshire and Fife use Buddy Healthcare ELSIE; Highland uses VitalHub Synopsis; GGC is going to market (DS012, contract notice expected Apr 2027). No evidence was found for Lothian, Golden Jubilee, Ayrshire & Arran or Forth Valley because the search budget ran out. [source](https://www.nhsgrampian.org/news/2026/may/new-online-service-to-streamline-pre-operative-assessments-for-adults/)
- The NHS Grampian MyPreOp rollout (May 2026) sends patients a secure SMS link. Nurses complete the same questionnaire with patients who face digital barriers, and booking staff can see at a glance who is ready for surgery. [source](https://www.nhsgrampian.org/news/2026/may/new-online-service-to-streamline-pre-operative-assessments-for-adults/)
- NHS Tayside's patient FAQ says MyPreOp is hosted on secure servers outside any NHS organisation and that patients log in with their date of birth. It takes 30-60 minutes, and phone completion is offered. [source](http://www.nhstayside.scot.nhs.uk/OurServicesA-Z/Pre-AssessmentClinicPAC/PROD_383781/)
- DHCW's all-Wales Pre-Operative Digital System (est. £5m excl. VAT, Jan 2027 to Dec 2032 plus 2 years) had its tender notice estimated for 1 May 2026, but by 22 Oct 2026 the FTS procurement record still held only the UK2 engagement notice. The tender is late and could appear at any time. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-06667b)
- Before the national DHCW buy, Betsi Cadwaladr UHB ran its own Digital Preoperative Assessment System PIN (Apr 2022, through NWSSP). It asked for risk categorisation by the board's criteria, integration with the Welsh PAS and Clinical Portals, bilingual English/Welsh patient information, and implementation within 6 months. This shows likely Welsh requirements (Welsh language, WPAS and WCP integration). [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/search_switch.aspx?ID=120692)
- DHCW's January 2026 public accountability evidence paper describes PROMs/PREMs infrastructure, the National Data Resource and the NHS Wales App as the digital front door. A pre-op product would likely need to feed national data repositories and possibly the NHS Wales App; the paper does not mention pre-op directly. [source](https://www.gov.wales/sites/default/files/publications/2026-03/public-accountability-meeting-evidence-from-digital-health-and-care-wales.pdf)
- Northern Ireland: encompass (Epic) went live in all five HSC Trusts between Nov 2023 and May 2025, with the My Care patient portal. The My Care privacy notice lists 'responses you give to questionnaires' and 'self-reported medical, surgical, and family history' as data patients can be asked for, so the regional EHR portal can already deliver questionnaires. That is a strong barrier to a standalone pre-op product in NI, though no source confirmed pre-op questionnaires specifically. [source](https://dhcni.hscni.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Privacy-Notice-Encompass-My-Care-ver-2.1-FINAL-DRAFT-1-4.pdf)
- The NI Elective Care Framework Funding and Implementation Plan 2026/27 (July 2026) keeps recurrent investment in pre-operative assessment services (patient optimisation, fewer cancellations). It also commits to promoting the MyCare app for patients waiting for elective care ('Waiting Well', digital-first communication) and to regional waiting list validation in general surgery. NI policy channels digital patient engagement through MyCare rather than separate tools. [source](https://www.health-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2026-07/Elective%20Care%20Framework%20-%20Funding%20and%20Implementation%20Plan%20-%20July%202026_0.pdf)
- The NI Elective Care Framework (May 2024) plans single regional waiting lists once encompass is fully live. It funded mega clinics including 2,100 pre-operative patients to cut DNA and CNA rates, asks Trusts to validate waiting lists regularly by contacting patients (Action 10), and estimates about £500k for a waiting-well policy. [source](https://www.health-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/health/Elective%20Care%20Framework%20-%20May%202024.pdf)
- No NI pre-op, consent, PROMs, patient portal or questionnaire software tender was found among the 1,060 notices in eTendersNI's public 'latest' list, which covers 2015-2026 and is not exhaustive. Matching health notices were BSO PaLS consumables only. Keyword search on eTendersNI is captcha-protected. [source](https://etendersni.gov.uk/epps/quickSearchAction.do?searchSelect=1&searchType=cftFTS&latest=true)

### research_competitors (17)

- Ultramed is winning share. Worcestershire Acute replaced VitalHub Synopsis (£81k bridging term to Oct 2024) with Ultramed (£240k, Nov 2024 to Oct 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/3e45d535-f2a1-4b00-a86c-5535f81031a9)
- Buyers favour framework call-offs and annual renewals for pre-op SaaS: G-Cloud 13/14, Digital Workplace Solutions 2, CDHS, OE TTS and NHS Commercial Solutions. Resellers such as Softcat often appear as the named winner (UHD MyPreOp, NWA Ultraprep, PAH Concentric). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2d78f3b3-5b19-4be3-86cf-3700525e3272)
- Digital Health & Care Wales plans an all-Wales pre-op digital system (£5m, 2027 to 2032, extendable to 2034). As of Oct 2026 only the PME (Mar 2026) has been published. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026)
- NHS National Services Scotland's 2023 PIN (NP510123) sought a national pre-op online triage solution and a theatre scheduling tool for 381 theatres across 14 boards. No national award was found; boards are buying locally instead (Tayside and Grampian with MyPreOp, Highland with Synopsis). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007268-2023)
- An FOI campaign in Jul to Sep 2025 asked trusts for their digital POA supplier, renewal date and value. Answers show many trusts have the questionnaire bundled into DrDoctor, PAS or EPR contracts, or still use paper (Sherwood Forest, St Helens & Knowsley); Dudley plans to introduce one. [source](https://www.dgft.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/FOI-072025-0001781.pdf)
- Sherwood Forest Hospitals (King's Mill) still used a paper pre-op questionnaire in Jun 2025, so it has no incumbent digital POA supplier. [source](https://www.sfh-tr.nhs.uk/media/e0fa3kkc/foi-260-theatre-management-systems-and-pre-operative-assessments-110625.pdf)
- Pre-op questionnaires now reach the NHS App. NHS England funded a DrDoctor 'Online Forms Pilot' (G-Cloud 13, signed 17 Aug 2023), and Lewisham & Greenwich patients complete digital assessments in the NHS App through DrDoctor. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/eca89ee2-1071-4c83-8ddd-84fcb6af96fd)
- The HIN South London evaluation (May 2026) of GSTT's Early Screening Tool, delivered through Epic MyChart: 98.6% sensitivity for medium or high complexity, 86% of scores unchanged after nurse validation, 71% completion, 19% needing digital support, and lower uptake in Core20 areas (50% vs 72%). [source](https://healthinnovationnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/HIN-Evaluation-of-the-Digital-Early-Screening-Tool-on-the-GSTT-Perioperative-Pathway-Final-May-2026.pdf)
- Chelsea & Westminster's Digital Health Questionnaire (Isla with Palantir): about 180 patients a month no longer needed assessment, POA-related on-the-day cancellations fell to 1.2%, and 7,897 patients said they were available at short notice. [source](https://www.chelwest.nhs.uk/about-us/news/digital-preoperative-assessment-triage-at-chelsea-and-westminster-hospital-nhs-foundation-trust-published-as-exemplary-case-study-by-nhs-england)
- European buyers ask for MDR/CE certification, ISO 27001, GDPR, HL7v2/FHIR/REST integration with SAP ISHmed, multilingual questionnaires (DE/EN/AR/FR) and video-based consent for digital premedication (Mannheim VEAT to NovaCair). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml)
- Belgium's AZORG has a live tender for a digital pre-op screening system (deadline 10 Nov 2026, 48 months), weighted 50% price, 30% technical/IT and 20% quality including a demo. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/702720-2026/xml)
- In the Netherlands, pre-op screening is often run inside the EPR. Diakonessenhuis uses ChipSoft HiX triage to compute a preliminary ASA, and 55% of screenings have been fully digital since Feb 2024. [source](https://www.conclusion.com/en-nl/cases/diakonessenhuis-digitises-preoperative-screening)
- In Sweden, regions run digital pre-op health declarations through 1177 and the regional systems; Skaraborg uses one common form in Orbit, available in real time to the surgical workflow (Mar 2026). [source](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4280407/digital-halsodeklaration-okar-patientsakerheten-infor-operation?lang=sv)
- Digital consent is a fast-growing adjacent category. Concentric and EIDO won at least 7 NHS awards between 2024 and 2026 (£105k to £300k each), and South Tees has an open tender for Digital Consent and Shared Decision Making (£135k, starting Jan 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Published prices give pricing benchmarks: Ultraprep £2.50 to £5.00 per submission; Synopsis £2.90 to £3.50 per unit; Pathpoint ePOA £48,500 per instance a year; AireFrame £2,500 per licence a year; Remcare £3 to £10 per user a year. [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-pricing-document-2026-01-15-1455.pdf)
- Mersey & West Lancashire ICS runs C2-Ai risk stratification of elective waiting lists across all 9 acute trusts, a driver for prehab and 'waiting well' interventions. [source](https://www.htworld.co.uk/?p=23335)
- Several contracts end soon and may come up for renewal or re-procurement: UHD MyPreOp (Mar 2027), PAH Pathpoint (Mar 2027), Lewisham & Greenwich's wider pathway work, WHHT Zesty (Mar 2027), WHHT QuestPrehab (Oct 2026), Devon Netcall (Sep 2026), Northumbria Synopsis (Jul 2027), Worcestershire Ultramed (Oct 2027), DBTH CaMIS (Oct 2026) and Dudley Sunrise (about Dec 2026). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/2ec6666c-bb54-4957-aeef-1ac9b334fb2a)

### research_compliance (45)

- DTAC v2.0 (last updated 24 Feb 2026) replaces v1.0: manufacturers must provide v2.0 from 6 Apr 2026. Structure: A company info and B value proposition (not assessed), C1 Clinical safety, C2 Data protection, C3 Technical security, C4 Interoperability (pass/fail), D1 Usability and accessibility (comparative, not pass/fail). The form must be kept current for each product version. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- DTAC v2.0 C1: if the product qualifies as SaMD/AIaMD under UK MDR 2002, the supplier must also submit the medical device Pre-Acquisition Questionnaire (PAQ). Otherwise it must evidence a DCB0129-compliant clinical risk management system, a Clinical Safety Case Report and Hazard Log (scope, approach, hazards, test summary, outstanding defects, transferred risks), and a named Clinical Safety Officer who is a registered clinician (can be outsourced). The NHS-specific CSO training requirement is removed. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- DTAC v2.0 C2: DSPT 'Standards Met/Exceeded' for current or previous year if the supplier accesses patient data; ICO registration; a product DPIA (data fields, data flows, controls, storage countries, supplier staff access, retention, sub-processors, data subject rights); transparency materials; fair T&Cs. Hosting must be declared as 'UK only' or 'Outside UK'; outside UK needs adequacy or an IDTA/BCR plus transfer risk assessment. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- DTAC v2.0 C3: a valid Cyber Essentials certificate is required (Plus is not mandated), checked against the IASME database. Signatories of the NHS Cyber Security Charter skip the rest of C3. Others need an external penetration test within 12 months including the OWASP Top 10 with no CVSS ≥7.0 findings, confirmation of the DSIT/NCSC Software Security Code of Practice, an MFA plan (preferably identity federation) with MFA on all privileged supplier access, and defined logging and audit trails. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- DTAC v2.0 C4: exposed APIs must use justified international/industry standards and follow GDS Open API best practice, openly documented. Products exchanging patient data must use the NHS Number and validate it via PDS or local record systems. Patient-facing products should use NHS login, or else meet DAPB3051 (Identity Verification and Authentication) or describe equivalent robust authentication. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- DTAC v2.0 D1 (not scored): user journey / instructions for use, usability testing with intended users, confirmation the Accessible Information Standard was considered, WCAG 2.2 AA (or a plan and timeline to reach it), a published accessibility statement, and average service availability over the past 12 months to two decimal places. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx)
- The refreshed DTAC form has about 25% fewer questions, removes duplication with the DSPT and the pre-acquisition questionnaire, and aligns scope with NICE's software-based digital health technologies. Published 4 Mar 2026; full transition by 6 Apr 2026. [source](https://innovation.nhs.uk/news/updated-nhs-england-digital-technology-assessment-criteria-dtac-form-and-guidance/)
- The DTAC page says DCB0129 and DCB0160 are under review and DTAC will be updated when they change. DTAC sits alongside, and does not replace, medical device certification and ICO registration. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/digital-technology-assessment-criteria-dtac)
- DCB0129 (manufacturers) and DCB0160 (deploying organisations) are information standards under s250 of the Health and Social Care Act 2012, and compliance is mandatory. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/clinical-safety/clinical-risk-management-standards)
- MHRA standalone software guidance: decision support that applies automated reasoning (calculations, algorithms) is likely a medical device. 'Triage', 'risk of', 'predicts' and 'screening' are indicative device words. Software that only books appointments or replaces a paper record is unlikely to be a device, and neither is software that only reproduces a paper form while the clinician decides. A pre-op questionnaire with automated risk triage is therefore at risk of qualifying as SaMD in GB. [source](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6abf6c8c943e890cb55e5e52/Medical_device_stand-alone_software_including_apps__including_IVDMDs.pdf)
- GB medical device reform: post-market surveillance regulations came into force 16 Jun 2025. A further statutory instrument with pre-market requirements and an international reliance route is to follow in 2026. A Feb–Apr 2026 consultation proposed indefinitely extending acceptance of CE-marked devices (page updated 12 Mar 2026). [source](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementation-of-the-future-regulation-of-medical-devices/implementation-of-the-future-regulations)
- EU MDR Rule 11 (MDCG 2019-11 rev.1, June 2025): software providing information used for diagnostic or therapeutic decisions is class IIa; class IIb if a wrong decision could cause serious deterioration or surgical intervention; class III if it could cause death or irreversible deterioration; other MDSW is class I. Information systems that only transfer, store, convert, format or archive data are not devices, but modules alongside EHRs that analyse patient data can be. [source](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en?filename=mdcg_2019_11_en.pdf)
- MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 adds EHDS interplay: where MDSW claims interoperability with an EHR system, the manufacturer must comply with both MDR/IVDR and the EHDS EHR-system requirements (EHDS Recital 42, Art 2(2)(k)). [source](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en?filename=mdcg_2019_11_en.pdf)
- EHDS Regulation (EU) 2025/327 was published 5 Mar 2025 and entered into force 26 Mar 2025. Key implementing acts are due by Mar 2027; patient summaries and ePrescriptions exchange from Mar 2029; images, lab results and discharge reports by Mar 2031. It sets security and interoperability criteria and certification for EHR systems. [source](https://health.ec.europa.eu/ehealth-digital-health-and-care/european-health-data-space-regulation-ehds_en)
- NHS login integration is free of charge, supported by NHS England, and takes about 3–4 months via the integration toolkit (apply, discovery, integrate, go live). [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/nhs-login/nhs-login-for-partners-and-developers)
- NHS login identity levels: P0 (email and phone only), P5 (matched to PDS), P9 (photo ID check). Services giving access to sensitive data require high verification (P9) with suitable authentication; mixed services can step users up from P5 to P9. Level selection follows DAPB3051 Appendix D. [source](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/vectors-of-trust/)
- NHS App integration standards: WCAG 2.2 AA minimum with an accessibility audit as evidence, all 17 points of the NHS service standard, DCB0129/DCB0160 and MHRA standalone software guidance, and UK GDPR and PECR, all certified in a Supplier Conformance Assessment List (SCAL). [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/nhs-app/how-to-integrate-with-the-nhs-app/standards-for-nhs-app-integration)
- NHS App routes for suppliers: web integration (online consultation services must be commissioned via an NHS England recognised framework); Notifications and Messaging via NHS Notify onboarding; and, for secondary care, the Patient Care Aggregator (Wayfinder). NHS login integration is a prerequisite. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/nhs-app/partners-and-developers)
- Patient Care Aggregator (Wayfinder) entry criteria for secondary-care portals: represent at least one eligible trust; integrate NHS login and the NHS App through a single endpoint; deep linking and NHS App look and feel; DCB0129 (supplier) and DCB0160 (trust); EHIA. Optional API endpoints can return questionnaires and documents. Onboarding needs DSPT, a formal ISMS, a CSO, NHS-predefined hazards in the hazard log and penetration testing, with DSPT and pen test renewed annually. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator/integrating-a-secondary-care-booking-system)
- IM1 pairing with GP systems (Optum EMIS Web, TPP SystmOne, plus new DCSF foundation suppliers) requires a clinical and IG prerequisites form, a SCAL, NHS England assurance ('Recommended to Connect'), and a Model Interface Licence with each GP system supplier. For AI products the DCB0129 safety case, hazard log and DPIA are reviewed. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/gp-it-futures-systems/im1-pairing-integration)
- GP Connect: Access Record (HTML/structured) and Send Document (live since 2023) are available, but there is no longer an onboarding route via GP Connect for new developers for appointment management or Update Record. Suppliers must complete national onboarding and assurance. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/gp-connect)
- HL7 UK published FHIR UK Core 2.0.0 STU2 (FHIR R4-based) on 13 May 2024, followed by 2.0.1 bug fixes. UK Core is the national baseline for FHIR APIs. [source](https://simplifier.net/organization/hl7uk/news/160)
- Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s121 / Sch 15 amends HSCA 2012 s250 so that information standards can cover IT and IT services and bind providers of IT used in health and adult social care in England. This is the legal basis for future mandatory interoperability standards on suppliers. [source](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/18/notes/division/12/index.htm)
- NHS England Digital off-shoring guidance (last edited 28 May 2025): UK hosting is the default. Hosting outside the UK, in the EEA, an adequate country or the US under an IDTA, needs a low-risk transfer assessment and SIRO/EMT approval, and dev/test environments abroad may use synthetic data only. In practice this pushes suppliers to UK-region hosting. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/data-and-information/looking-after-information/data-security-and-information-governance/nhs-and-social-care-data-off-shoring-and-the-use-of-public-cloud-services)
- Cyber Security Charter for suppliers to the NHS (issued May 2025) has eight commitments: patching, DSPT Standards Met, MFA/identity federation, 24/7 monitoring, immutable backups, board-level exercises, timely incident reporting, and the DSIT/NCSC Software Security Code of Practice. Signing is a voluntary statement of intent. From Jan 2026 NHS England may contact suppliers about these controls. The signatory list was updated 1 Oct 2026. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-and-data-security/guidance-and-resources/cyber-security-charter-for-suppliers-to-the-nhs)
- The Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations require WCAG 2.2 AA and a published accessibility statement. Bodies remain legally responsible for third-party software they paid for, so trusts pass WCAG 2.2 AA down to suppliers. [source](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/accessibility-requirements-for-public-sector-websites-and-apps)
- NHS Standard Contract 2026/27 SC3.18: acute providers must implement and maintain a system of early screening, risk assessment and health optimisation for all adult patients waiting for inpatient surgery, per the Perioperative Care Pathways Guidance. SC10.6 requires regard to PIFU guidance. SC23.7 requires regard to the NHS Digital Architecture Principles when procuring IT. The contract also requires NHS Number as the consistent identifier and compliance with the Accessible Information Standard. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/25-nhssc-fl-scs-2526-2627-comp.pdf)
- NHS England earlier-screening guide has five core requirements: screen and triage risk factors as early as possible; proactive personalised optimisation for at-risk patients; contact inpatient waiters at least every three months; give a surgery date only once confirmed fit; and shared decision-making. It cites the July 2022 digital health and care plan expectation that all providers offer digital pre-assessment by September 2024, with digital health assistants and non-digital alternatives. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/earlier-screening-risk-assessment-and-health-optimisation-in-perioperative-pathways/)
- GIRFT POA guidance (endorsed by NHS England's National Clinical Director, published Aug 2023) has seven principles. They include giving a TCI date only after POA is complete, a ready-list of pre-assessed patients, early screening, maximum use of decision support tools, and an 80% nurse-led model. Its low-risk ePOA model includes an electronic screening questionnaire via the NHS App (or 15–20 screening questions), 3-monthly electronic health updates and medication reminders via the NHS App integrated with TCI/scheduling, digital consent, minimum nursing documentation (e.g. VTE) and integration into the trust EPR. [source](https://gettingitrightfirsttime.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/GIRFT-Pre-operative-assessment-guidance-FINAL-V1-July-2023.pdf)
- Elective reform plan (6 Jan 2025): routine patients get a procedure date only once confirmed fit at pre-assessment. NHS England will use digital questionnaires through PEPs and the NHS App, including NHS App questionnaires to validate waiting lists. 70% of elective appointments are to be viewable and manageable in the NHS App by Mar 2026; PIFU standard in all appropriate pathways by Mar 2026 and at least 5% of outpatient appointments by Mar 2029. Validation counts as activity in the 2025/26 Payment Scheme, and the Digital Weight Management Programme extends to hip and knee waiters in 2025/26. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/reforming-elective-care-for-patients/)
- 2025/26 planning guidance: validate RTT waiters after 12 weeks and then every 12 weeks using digital tools. It also requires at least 70% of elective appointments viewable and manageable in the NHS App, NHS App-first communications, PIFU within referral optimisation, completion of planned EPR procurements, and FDP adoption (85% of trusts by Mar 2026). [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/2025-26-priorities-and-operational-planning-guidance/)
- Medium Term Planning Framework 2026/27–2028/29 (24 Oct 2025), section 2.4 'Doing digital differently': providers must let patients receive and complete pre- and post-appointment questionnaires through the NHS App, implement digital PIFU per GIRFT guidance, and make at least 95% of appointments available via the NHS App, with full coverage by the end of 2028/29. It also covers moving patient messaging to NHS Notify by 2028/29, full compliance with the Digital Capabilities Framework minimum standards, and implementing core national products by the end of 2027/28. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/)
- Medium Term Planning Framework elective targets: 92% RTT within 18 weeks by the end of 2028/29. In 2026/27 each trust must improve 18-week performance by at least 7% or reach at least 65%, towards a 70% national target. Waiting lists must be managed with thorough validation, using FDP or equivalent. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/)
- 10 Year Health Plan (updated 30 Jul 2025): the NHS App becomes a full front door to the NHS by 2028, with booking, communication, care plans, 'My Specialist' direct booking into tests and a single patient record. It does not mention pre-op assessment specifically. [source](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/10-year-health-plan-for-england-fit-for-the-future/fit-for-the-future-10-year-health-plan-for-england-executive-summary)
- Germany KHZG Fördertatbestand 2 (Patientenportale) 'Muss' criteria for digital admission management include: online booking or requesting of appointments and admissions, digital anamnesis by patients from home, upload of documents and the federal medication plan (or consent-based access to an existing record), FAQs, referral upload by referrers, staff-to-patient messaging, in-clinic digital anamnesis, and interfaces to KIS/ERP so captured data flows into downstream processes. Digital consent and chatbots are 'Kann' (optional) criteria. [source](https://WWW.IB-SACHSEN-ANHALT.DE/fileadmin/user_upload/Dokumente/Krankenhausfinanzierung/Krankenhauszukunftsfonds_Richtlinie_BAS.pdf)
- Under KHZG, hospitals that fail to implement the digital services in Fördertatbestände 2–6 face a 2% deduction on inpatient revenues from 2025 (as stated in a Gesundheit Nord tender). This drives German patient-portal and digital admission procurements. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/508990-2025/pdf)
- Germany §393 SGB V: providers may process health data in the cloud only in Germany, the EU or adequate third countries, and the processor needs a German branch. A current BSI C5 attestation is required: Type 1 until 30 Jun 2025, Type 2 from 1 Jul 2025, with an 18-month Type 1 grace period for newly launched systems. The Ministry of Health and BSI may recognise equivalent standards. [source](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__393.html)
- France HDS certification referential v2 (arrêté 26 Apr 2024, published 16 May 2024): physical hosting of health data must be exclusively in the EEA. Hosts must inform clients contractually of risks from non-EU access or law and publish a map of transfers outside the EEA. Existing hosts had to recertify by 16 May 2026. [source](https://cms.law/en/fra/news-information/nouveau-referentiel-de-certification-des-hebergeurs-de-donnees-de-sante-hds)
- Netherlands: NEN 7510-1:2024 and NEN 7510-2:2024+A1:2026 apply from 1 Jun 2026 to exchange systems and care information systems under the Besluit elektronische gegevensverwerking door zorgaanbieders. [source](https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/stcrt-2026-17743.html)
- Norway Normen requirements for suppliers of digital patient communication tools: electronic, granular consent; controller-side correction and deletion (documentation-duty data not editable by patients); logging per Normen 5.4.4; a data processing agreement; no registers combining several customers' data; routines to detect, handle and report breaches. [source](https://www.helsedirektoratet.no/normen/digital-pasientkommunikasjon/implementering-av-nye-kommunikasjonsverktoy/krav-til-leverandorer)
- The Procurement Act 2023 went live on 24 Feb 2025. Since then UK notices use the new UK1–UK17 forms (e.g. UK3 planned procurement and UK4 tender notice, as on the Royal Surrey ePOA tender). [source](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/transforming-public-procurement)
- Buyer pattern: the NHS Scotland national theatre scheduling ITT asked bidders to evidence Cyber Essentials, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018 and the UK Government 14 Cloud Security Principles, scored functional 40, non-functional 30 and price 30. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-03b258)
- Buyer pattern (Germany): Universitätsklinikum Mannheim's pre-op screening procurement required a CE-certified medical device, ISO 27001, GDPR, bidirectional integration with SAP ISHmed/KIS via HL7 v2, FHIR and REST, at least four languages including Arabic, and video-based patient information with digital consent. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/pdf)
- EPR integration pattern used by an incumbent pre-op vendor: PAS demographics via HL7 v2.4 QBP_Q21/QRY_A19 queries and a PDF/document return to the EPR/EDMS via HL7 v2.4 MDM_T02, with on-premise integration servers. The vendor claims DTAC, DSPT, DCB0129, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus and MHRA registration. [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf)
- Buyer pattern (UK PEP): a trust required that all patient data be held in the EPR, with questionnaires and forms linked to the patient record, NHS App sign-in and surfacing of forms, and continued Wayfinder compliance. Portals are expected to be EPR-backed rather than standalone stores. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/041626-2024)

### research_dach (14)

- BAS KHZG guideline (Version 02), FTB 2 Muss-criteria for digital admission: patients must be able to complete an anamnesis digitally from home, and admission staff must be able to take a digital anamnesis in the clinic. Interfaces to KIS/ERP are mandatory. Digital consent to documents and chatbot anamnesis are only Kann-criteria. All Muss-criteria in 4.3.2.1–4.3.2.3 must be met. [source](https://WWW.IB-SACHSEN-ANHALT.DE/fileadmin/user_upload/Dokumente/Krankenhausfinanzierung/Krankenhauszukunftsfonds_Richtlinie_BAS.pdf)
- BAS guideline: FTB 2 treatment management must let patients learn about their treatment (e.g., education videos) and note questions on their own device. PROMs surveys are a Kann-criterion. Funded projects must use international interoperability standards, be transferable to the ePA (§ 341 SGB V), and spend at least 15% of funds on information security. [source](https://WWW.IB-SACHSEN-ANHALT.DE/fileadmin/user_upload/Dokumente/Krankenhausfinanzierung/Krankenhauszukunftsfonds_Richtlinie_BAS.pdf)
- Digitalisierungsabschlag: hospitals that do not provide FTB 2–6 services face a deduction of up to 2% per inpatient case from 2025. FTB 2 (patient portals) ranks second in priority, with a 0.5% availability share in 2025–2026. Usage is assessed from 31 Dec 2027, and no deduction applies if every FTB is at least 'commissioned'. This keeps German portal demand alive beyond the funding. [source](https://www.roedl.com/insights/krankenhauszukunftsfonds-digitalisierungsabschlags-vereinbarung-dkg/)
- § 393 SGB V: cloud processing of health data by German providers is allowed only in Germany, the EU or adequacy countries, with a German establishment and a current C5 attestation. Type 1 sufficed until 30 Jun 2025; Type 2 is required from 1 Jul 2025. This is a gating requirement for SaaS pre-op tools in Germany. [source](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__393.html)
- Buyer pattern: German consent procurements are dominated by Thieme Compliance. Several are direct awards or VEATs justified by existing form content (e.g., Mittelrhein: market analysis found no other supplier with consent forms for all specialties). Rivals won only occasionally (medavis at GLG, synMedico at SLK). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/237286-2026/xml)
- Buyer pattern: the only explicit DACH pre-op screening procurement (Mannheim, Nov 2025) was a direct award to a Dutch specialist (Novacair E-POS). It required a stand-alone CE-marked medical device, ISO 27001, GDPR, SAP ISHmed/HL7v2/FHIR integration and four languages including Arabic, plus video consent. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml)
- Market scale signal: UK Halle processed about 116,000 consent forms per year through the E-ConsentPro base module before digitising. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/851883-2025/xml)
- Many German FTB 2 portal tenders explicitly require digital anamnesis questionnaires linked to appointments and sent in structured form to the KIS (Münster, Nürnberg, Leipzig, Agatharied, Darmstadt, Andernach, Mittelbaden). A pre-op questionnaire product can therefore be positioned as a portal module or as a partner to portal vendors. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/524073-2024/xml)
- Deloitte Pulse Check (2025/26, 25+ interviews, 15 hospitals in DE/AT): portals are seen as a key lever but under-used. Typical use cases are appointments, anamnesis, consent and treatment preparation. In Austria the ELGA connection is treated as a central part of portal strategy from the start. [source](https://www.deloitte.com/content/dam/assets-zone2/at/de/docs/studien/2026/pulse-check-patientenportal-at.pdf)
- Universitätsspital Basel published an advance notice (2026-10-01, publication forecast 2026-12-14) for an integrated full clinical system (KIS, PDMS, RIS, LIS) including digital patient interaction such as a patient app, capacity and process steering, and third-party integration. [source](https://www.simap.ch/api/publications/v1/project/facd7bca-b512-4cfe-8884-9d09646bed23/publication-details/eebea46a-e499-4806-ad2b-2f8d7acaacbb)
- Klinik-Kompetenz-Bayern eG framework: Siemens Healthineers won a multi-tenant interoperable patient portal for 56 hospital operators and 111 clinics (reported 1 Dec 2023), largely KHZG-funded. Hospital cooperatives and shared-service frameworks are an important buying route in Germany. [source](https://www.wfw.com/press/wfw-advises-more-than-50-hospital-operators-on-pioneering-patient-portal-project-with-interoperability-platform/?l=en)
- Encare's EIAS technical summary (used by Kantonsspital Baden): web SaaS hosted on AWS in ISO 27001-compliant data centres in Frankfurt; no directly identifying patient data stored; positioned as non-operational quality software. A useful benchmark for Swiss and German hosting expectations. [source](https://www.kantonsspitalbaden.ch/documents/2025-06/eras_20250604.pdf)
- Austria: Vinzenz Gruppe launched the 'Hallo Gesundheit' patient portal in Sept 2023, starting with outpatient clinics and plastic surgery and obesity clinics in Vienna. An ELGA connection is planned. It was not found as a public tender. [source](https://wien.orf.at/stories/3223970/)
- Novacair reports that E-POS saves about 60% of pre-op process time and digitally approves 29% of patients in an academic population, and integrates with Chipsoft, Epic, CNS-connect and EMMA Timeff. [source](https://novacair.com)

### research_devolved (13)

- NHS NSS's March 2023 PIN (before the window) asked for a national Digital Pre-operative Assessment online triage tool. Patients would complete a remote pre-op questionnaire and get support at set intervals, and clinicians would triage and route them. It was bundled with theatre scheduling, but only theatre scheduling went to tender and award (Infix, 2024). PCS keyword searches (pre-op, pre-operative, preoperative, pre-assessment) found no separate national pre-op contract notice afterwards. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAR473603)
- In Scotland, demand has moved to board level. NHS GGC issued a 'Digital PreOp Solution' PIN in May 2026 (contract notice expected about 21 April 2027) and a separate Theatre Patient Management System PIN in Sep 2025 (contract notice expected about 1 April 2027). [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAY555591)
- Wales plans a single national pre-op system (DHCW, GBP 5m ex VAT, 2027-2032 plus extensions to 2034). The planned tender date of 1 May 2026 passed with no tender notice found on Sell2Wales by 22 Oct 2026, so the procurement looks delayed but live. [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAR596518)
- A precursor BCUHB (North Wales) PIN from April 2022 already set the Welsh pre-op template. It asked to replace all paper POA within 6 months, offer home completion, give multiple users access to the record, auto-assign risk category by surgical severity and medical history, integrate with Welsh PAS and Clinical Portals, and provide bilingual (English/Welsh) patient information. [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/search_switch.aspx?ID=120692)
- The All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, contract dated 13 Oct 2023, 3 years plus 1) reaches the end of its initial term about October 2026. A Welsh PROMs re-procurement or extension is imminent, and PROMs collection is a natural add-on to a pre-op platform. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032382-2023)
- Belfast HSC Trust board paper P74-2025: pre-op assessment has historically been under-funded and resources are inadequate. The executive team approved a business case on 2 Dec 2024 for a fully functional adult pre-operative assessment service (Option 2, phased), with a funding request of GBP 1,688,649, to cut on-the-day cancellations and raise day-of-surgery admission. The paper names no software procurement. [source](https://belfasttrust.hscni.net/download/730/09-january-2025/21913/p74-2025-bhsct-meeting-template-adult-pre-operative-assessment-services-bhsct-excludes-mph-and-paediatric-pre-assessment.pdf)
- Scottish boards buy patient-engagement and digital tools mostly through frameworks and resellers rather than open tenders: NHS SBS Patient/Citizen Communication & Engagement Solutions, CCS RM6259 Vertical Application Solutions Lot 2, G-Cloud 14, the SP-21-034 software reseller framework, and the Digital Technology and Cyber Services DPS. Softcat and Computacenter often appear as the contractor of record. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=DEC544775)
- The Golden Jubilee perioperative app tender shows what a Scottish buyer scores. It was 60% quality / 40% price, with pass/fail 'must haves' (HL7 v2.4 in and out, RBAC, encryption, MFA, audit logs, DPIA, UK GDPR, the 2018 accessibility regulations) and declarations on medical-device status. An on-site demo scored the ability to change pathway content locally, such as turning a smoking info page into a smoking/vaping questionnaire without supplier involvement. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959)
- Scotland's national Digital Front Door (MyCare.scot) is being built by NES with BJSS/CGI (GBP 27.85m). New national digital tenders, such as the Oct 2026 MSK PMC, now require compatibility with MyCare.scot. Scottish pre-op questionnaires will likely be expected to integrate with it. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT566180)
- In Wales, third-party patient-facing products must pass a DHCW-run accreditation process before the NHS Wales App signposts or integrates them. DHCW tendered a Third Party Provider Accreditation Service in April 2024. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/013493-2024)
- Welsh digital health notices consistently require Welsh-language (bilingual) delivery and WCAG accessibility. Examples are ABUHB's Theatre Management System PME and the CfIC planned-care challenge, which excludes English-only patient-facing delivery. [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=AUG535492)
- NHS National Services Scotland now appears on PCS as 'The Common Services Agency (more commonly known as Public Services Delivery Scotland) (PSD Scotland)'. Monitoring for national Scottish procurements should track that buyer name (PCS authority AA11883). [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAY555119)
- NHS Highland launched a digital pre-operative pathway on Synopsis (VitalHub UK) for its National Treatment Centre in April 2023. It replaced paper with a central auditable record and a patient health questionnaire completed at home, while keeping phone and face-to-face options. [source](https://buildingbetterhealthcare.com/nhs-highland-to-launch-digital-pre-operative-pathway-207037)

### research_ireland (16)

- WLAP 2025: the National Perioperative Patient Pathway Enhancement Programme (NPPPEP) aims to embed a standardised, data-driven approach to measuring, evaluating and optimising theatre capacity, and will expand in 2025. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- WLAP 2025: the NTPF will administratively validate OPD and IPDC waiting lists for patients waiting over 3 months, targeting 126,110 removals in 2025 (108,829 OPD, 17,281 IPDC), and will expand clinical validation. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- WLAP 2025: surgical hubs are being built in South Dublin (opening early 2025), North Dublin (Q4 2025), Galway (H1 2026), and Cork, Waterford and Limerick (phased 2026), with one under consideration in the North West. Once open they add 4,000 day cases, 5,800 minor procedures and 18,500 OPD appointments a year. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- WLAP 2025: the HSE App is to be the 'digital front door', adding appointment viewing and reminders (target Q4 2025), referral and waiting-list status (Q3 2025) and self-care support for four pathways. The aim is 75% of IPMS specialties and hospitals in 2025. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- WLAP 2025: robotic process automation to manage suspensions and waiting-list removals ran in 6 hospitals in 2024, with 16 more due Q1 2025. A DNA-management proof of concept is to scale to other sites. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- Galway (Merlin Park) Surgical Hub construction contract awarded to John Sisk and Son, EUR 38.4m. The building has operating theatres, preparation, recovery and waiting areas, and targets day-case waiting lists in the West (Sláintecare Action Plan 2023). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/534590-2026)
- Digital for Care 2024–2030 sets out a patient app for viewing appointments, prescriptions and results, a national shared care record, enterprise EHRs, and telehealth, virtual wards and remote monitoring as national priorities. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/digital-for-care-a-digital-health-framework-for-ireland-2024-2030.pdf)
- The HSE One Health Record (national EHR) scope lists 'Pre-Operative', Intraoperative, Postoperative and Surgery Scheduling in core functionality, which could absorb standalone pre-op tools in public hospitals from 2027–2032. Private hospitals are explicitly out of scope and connect via an external provider portal. [source](https://www.etenders.gov.ie/epps/cft/listContractDocuments.do?resourceId=7469411)
- HSE remote-monitoring procurements ask for NHS DCB0129 conformance, NHS DTAC, Cyber Essentials (CE+ desirable), EU MDR evidence, ISO 13485/14971 and ISO 27001, plus EEA hosting. Irish buyers use UK NHS assurance standards alongside EU regulation. [source](https://www.etenders.gov.ie/epps/dps/listDPSContractDocuments.do?resourceId=2692177)
- NTPF is setting up a EUR 700m, 48-month framework of private healthcare providers for adult and paediatric day case, inpatient and outpatient procedures (tenders closed 18 Sep 2026). This keeps outsourced elective surgery, and so pre-op assessment demand, flowing to private hospitals. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/551152-2026)
- HSE ran a mini-competition to buy private theatre capacity for Cork University Hospital (award notice Jan 2025), part of the pattern of insourcing and outsourcing surgery to meet waiting-list targets. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/13238-2025)
- Mater Misericordiae University Hospital tendered for a replacement patient management system in 2023 but could not award for budget reasons. In Dec 2024 it contracted Dedalus to move PatientCentre to the cloud (EUR 1.4m, 4 years) while it seeks funding to replace it. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/789956-2024)
- The Royal Victoria Eye & Ear Hospital has been waiting since 2017 for the HSE iPMS. Its bespoke PAS (CAPAS) is at the top of its corporate risk register. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/520980-2024)
- The Saolta/HSE West and North West Kainos Evolve EMR and eForms contract (clinical documentation at point of care) was extended to December 2027, giving a renewal window. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/161233-2025)
- HSE is buying a national Enterprise Integration Platform as a Service (HSE 28439, restricted, 15 years). Future clinical apps, including the One Health Record, are expected to integrate through it with EHDS-ready standards. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/635530-2026)
- St James's Hospital is implementing an Oracle Cerner PAS, capacity management/patient flow and billing, with a consultancy tender (EUR 3m) in 2024 and again in 2026. The Rotunda and MN-CMS run Oracle Cerner Millennium, where hospitals want embedded SMART on FHIR apps. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/501868-2024)

### research_nl-be (17)

- AZORG (Belgium) is running a live tender (published 12 Oct 2026, requests due 10 Nov 2026, 48 months) for a digital pre-op screening system. It covers home-based anamnesis questionnaires, multilingual questionnaires and anaesthesia animation videos, automatic analysis with next-step suggestions, and KWS/EPR integration. This is the only explicit pre-op assessment software tender found in NL/BE in the window. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/702720-2026)
- Belgian hospitals also buy pre-op assessment functionality inside anaesthesia information systems. HeCaPP's anaesthesia-record tender made a pre-anaesthesia consultation module (history, allergies, prior anaesthesia, pre-op exam, plan, pre-intervention checklist) a required option. Awarded to ICARE Healthcare. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/1380-2026)
- Belgian OR management tenders treat pre-op consultation data as an interface. AHSM's live OR, sterilisation and endoscopy tender lists DPI clinical data including pre-op consultations, plus the operating schedule, as required integrations. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/719516-2026)
- The 7 Dutch UMCs jointly measure patient experience with the PEM (Picker-based validated questionnaires), sent by email via a measurement bureau. In 2025 there were 284,733 respondents at 30% average response. The current contract started in 2019 and expires Q1 2027, and a European tender is planned. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/414102/documenten/13813844/content)
- UMCNL consultation outcome: respondents see multichannel delivery, adaptive questionnaires, dashboards and EPR integration as standard. They expect PREMs and PROMs to be increasingly combined with other data, and recommend a roughly 4-year contract with licence plus usage pricing. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/414102/documenten/14156625/content)
- LUMC's concept requirements for its telemonitoring platform require NEN 7510/7512/7513, WGBO and MDR certification. They also require DigiD or MFA for patients, integration through HiX standard facilities (CS Zorgplatform, HL7 ADT, external app/webviewer), FHIR export, and pathways that change over time such as pre-operative and post-operative. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/408350/documenten/13575475/content)
- LUMC merged its separate telemonitoring platform and home-device consultations into one planned tender with one lot covering platform, devices, logistics and service (PIN April 2026). [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/422834)
- Amsterdam UMC used a VEAT to award a 3-year contract (EUR 266k/yr) for the ikHerstel perioperative recovery app without competition, citing unique evidence-based algorithms and RCT evidence. This is a precedent for direct awards to evidence-backed perioperative apps. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/402893/documenten/13378635/content)
- Maastricht UMC+ requires integration with EPIC for its continuous monitoring tender, which identifies Epic as its EPR. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/427461/documenten/14331094/content)
- In Belgium, HiX (ChipSoft) won the AZ Jan Palfijn Gent EPR framework (EUR 143.5M result value, 2026). ZAS also runs HiX and integrates via FHIR, so HiX integration matters in Flanders as well as the Netherlands. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/646663-2026)
- ZAS (Antwerp) also built an AI clinical documentation prototype integrated into HiX via FHIR interfaces, which supports FHIR-based integration as a viable route at HiX sites. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/696940-2025)
- Flemish EPR tenders (HH Lier, AZ Oudenaarde, both won by nexuzhealth) require a patient portal that extends the record into the pre- and post-hospital period, where patients can add data. Pre-op questionnaires may be expected from the EPR portal there. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/416167-2026)
- ZAS tendered a transmural care-pathway ('patient journey') platform integrated with HiX and the federal Digital Referral Prescription (DRP) platform for telemonitoring. The DRP is a Belgian policy-driven integration point. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/66657-2026)
- Walloon/Brussels purchasing centre MercurHosp tendered consultancy in patient experience (PX) and value-based health care (VBHC) in two lots (4 years, July 2026). This points to demand for PROM/PREM programmes in Belgian francophone hospitals. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/484466-2026)
- The Dutch Ministry of Health (VWS) is funding work to embed shared decision-making (samen beslissen) in medical specialist care. CQT groep won the training contract (EUR 577,605, 2025), part of the Uitkomstgerichte Zorg (outcome-based care) programme context. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/612505-2025)
- CHU Liège (with CHR Citadelle) sought a patient communication and remote follow-up platform covering pre- and post-hospital phases, digital consent forms, education content and teleconsultation, integrated with its patient portal and DPI (2023). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/632831-2023)
- Most Belgian hospital tenders host documents on 3P cloud, which requires a reCAPTCHA step before download. Some use the BOSA e-Procurement app. Neither could be read by automated research, so specifications for AZORG, HeCaPP and AHSM need a manual browser download. [source](https://cloud.3p.eu/Downloads/1/1003/VJ/2026)

### research_nordics (14)

- Skaraborgs Sjukhus (Västra Götalandsregionen) has patients complete a single shared digital pre-operative health declaration in Orbit, with answers in real time for the surgical team. It reports fewer late cancellations and rebookings, and earlier detection of medication risks. Patients without Swedish, without 1177 digital consent or with protected identity follow separate routines (press release 2026-03-11). [source](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4280407/digital-halsodeklaration-okar-patientsakerheten-infor-operation?lang=sv)
- In Sweden, digital pre-op health declarations are typically delivered inside the surgical planning system (Orbit) or via 1177 rather than bought as standalone pre-op products. TED searches for 'hälsodeklaration', 'preoperativ', 'digital anamnes' and 'operationsplanering' returned no dedicated tenders since 2023-10. [source](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4280407/digital-halsodeklaration-okar-patientsakerheten-infor-operation?lang=sv)
- Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county sends cataract-surgery patients a letter asking them to complete an electronic pre-information questionnaire ('Kaihileikkauksen esitietokysely') in the oma.hyvis.fi portal using bank ID or mobile certificate. Staff contact patients who have not completed it before the procedure. [source](https://kymenhva.fi/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/KAIHILEIKKAUS-kutsukirje.pdf)
- Päijät-Häme wellbeing services county launched a surgical-patient digital pathway in the Päijät-Sote app (7 Oct 2026). It opens automatically when the patient is put on the surgery waiting list and has consented to e-services, and supports secure messaging and part of the pre-operative guidance. No vendor is named. [source](https://www.sttinfo.fi/tiedote/72392939/paijat-hameen-hyvinvointialue-leikkauspotilaan-kayttoon-uusi-helppokayttoinen-digipolku?lang=fi)
- Norway's national joint registry (Helse Bergen) has clinics send an electronic 'Preoperativ PROM' form to shoulder, knee and hip patients via the registry system, ideally 1–4 weeks before surgery. A pre-op form completed after surgery cannot be used (guide dated 2023-01-08, just before the research window). [source](https://www.helse-bergen.no/48ff02/siteassets/seksjon/nasjonal_kompetansetjeneste_leddproteser_hoftebrudd/share-point-documents/elektronisk-registrering-mrs/ledd/registrering-av-prom-leddregisteret.pdf)
- Helse Nord's 2025 RFI for theatre-utilisation software states that DIPS Arena's operating module will remain the system for perioperative overview and documentation. New Norwegian periop tools must complement DIPS Arena, not replace it. [source](https://doffin.no/notices/2025-105566)
- Finnish wellbeing counties increasingly buy perioperative IT as separate surgery/anaesthesia management systems, often through in-house IT companies such as 2M-IT Oy. GE Healthcare Finland won three of these awards in 2024–2025: Kanta-Häme surgical management, Keski-Suomi anaesthesia and Satakunta anaesthesia. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/608656-2025)
- 2M-IT Oy awarded Satakunta's anaesthesia system to GE Healthcare Finland Oy (EUR 1,308,632, contract 2025-07-07): four years with an indefinite-extension option and an optional ICU module, after the first round closed with no winner (TED 237421-2025). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/521704-2025)
- KPMG acts as procurement consultant or RFI technical lead on several Finnish digital-health procurements: Pohjois-Savo/Keski-Suomi digital services platform and the Kymenlaakso operations-management RFI. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/491497-2024)
- Kymenlaakso's 2024 RFI for an operations-management system asks for patient-flow and capacity management: real-time bed and patient location, patient service-path and planned-activity views, messaging between units, task management, and equipment tracking 'also outside the operating theatre'. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/491497-2024)
- Region Syddanmark's existing 'Mit Sygehus' patient app had just over 2,000 clinical users per month and about 3,500 citizens per day before it was re-tendered.
