The replacement must integrate the region's PRO solution and EPJ Syd and let departments send questionnaires. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/206912-2024)
- Region Hovedstaden ran a 2023 market dialogue on cutting postoperative complications across its hospitals, leading to a DKK 335M intelligent-monitoring innovation partnership. Its tender pack included a formal procedure for MDR assessment of software and security requirements for networked equipment. [source](https://eu.eu-supply.com/app/rfq/rwlentrance_s.asp?PID=395941&B=)
- Norwegian DHO (digital home follow-up) is procured regionally. Sykehuspartner says the current HSØ DHO framework agreement is expiring and planned a contract notice around 2026-06-30. Nordlandssykehuset re-tendered DHO in 2025 after cancelling the first attempt. [source](https://doffin.no/notices/2026-103578)
- Most Finnish wellbeing-county tender documents sit on Tarjouspalvelu.fi, which requires login to view publications. Swedish regional documents sit on Mercell TendSign (login required), Danish ones on EU-Supply (after expression of interest) and Norwegian ones on Mercell. [source](https://tarjouspalvelu.fi/khshp?id=550957&tpk=9f7ee875-0c79-44b8-92d9-dfe4b125a0dd)

### research_southern-eu (16)

- France's RESAH launched a national single-supplier framework for an end-to-end patient-pathway platform with AI modules: EUR 80m estimated, EUR 250m maximum, up to 73 months from 2026-12-01. One winner will be able to supply all French public hospitals. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/442265-2026/html)
- RESAH's 2024-25 innovation framework already holds single-supplier lots for PROMs (SKEZI), PREMs (Better World) and consent (DrData), each capped at EUR 10m. The operating-block flow-coordination lot had 2 bids but no award, so it is a gap that could be relaunched. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/399745-2025/html)
- RESAH scores digital solutions on functional/technical quality including hosting (35 points), price (25), innovation (15), services and interfacing (15), means (5) and CSR (5). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/399745-2025/html)
- The UniHA innovation SAD (EUR 30m, open to 2031) lets suppliers register at any time. UniHA can add categories (20 so far, none pre-op), and applications must be in French. [source](https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr/entreprise/consultation/2793633?orgAcronyme=x7c)
- GIP CPage, the publisher of a widely used French public-hospital patient-administration (GAP) system, tendered for a partner digital patient-pathway platform. Lot 1 covers online pre-admission. The platform must interoperate with the DPI (EPR), GAP and appointment (GRV) systems. [source](https://www.boamp.fr/pages/avis/?q=idweb:23-164258)
- In Portugal, perioperative and pre-anaesthesia digital pathways are already bought hospital by hospital. UpHill holds most of these contracts (Alentejo Central, Entre Douro e Vouga, Coimbra, Santo António). After the initial licence, hospitals renew support by direct award on exclusivity grounds. [source](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=11800854)
- Portuguese ULS hospitals often buy small (EUR 9k-40k) through Consulta Prévia with short bid windows (11-22 days) on Vortal, and several perioperative contracts are awarded on price alone. [source](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/cp_hora/2026/07/126/419965980.pdf)
- Madrid public hospitals pilot PROMs/PREMs, consent digitisation and AI surgical scheduling through contratos menores just under EUR 15,000, which are published only on the regional portal. [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D540_8933)
- Spanish regional health services require EU data residency (a signed server-location declaration), Esquema Nacional de Seguridad certification for medium/high category systems, FHIR (openEHR valued), and integration with the regional patient portal and the @Firma signature platform. [source](https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/poc?uri=deeplink:detalle_licitacion&idEvl=tT12RPWO3jaIzo3LHNPGcQ%3D%3D)
- Spain's NextGenerationEU-funded Plan de Asistencia/Atención Digital Personalizada drives regional patient-facing platform tenders. Aragón's ADP platform went to T-Systems for EUR 1.3m, and its specification refers to 17 pilot projects due by 2026-06-30. [source](https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/poc?uri=deeplink:detalle_licitacion&idEvl=YzaITRuazvBq1DdmE7eaXg%3D%3D)
- Lombardy hospitals must host new clinical systems on the regional ARIA cloud (ACN-qualified). Integrations are validated against the regional SISS HL7 specifications, and the MDR, NIS2 and ISO 27001-aligned measures are cited. [source](https://www.asst-spedalicivili.it/bandi/procedura-aperta-laffidamento-contratto-avente-ad-oggetto-fornitura-un-sistema-gestionale-sale-operatorie-e-percorso-chirurgico-aziendale-un-periodo)
- Italian regions also buy OR and surgical systems through Consip 'Sanità Digitale' frameworks (for example, the Marche regional operating-block system was awarded at quality 90 / price 10). The new Consip AQ ID 2837 (Data Governance & AI, EUR 662.4m, 4 lots) is a further framework that only admitted suppliers can use. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/421722-2024/html)
- Italian OR/surgical pathway tenders bundle pre-op anaesthesia assessment into large clinician-side systems (EUR 1.8m-5m) rather than buying patient-facing pre-op questionnaires separately. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/722510-2026/html)
- Polish operating-block software awards are price-only and won by the HIS incumbent (one bid at GCM Katowice), which limits openings for a foreign SaaS entrant. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/702142-2024/html)
- Portuguese hospitals are starting dedicated value-based-healthcare platform tenders (CROMs/PROMs/PREMs) weighted 70% on quality, e.g. ULS Gaia/Espinho at EUR 210k (2026). [source](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/cp_hora/2026/08/168/419971626.pdf)
- CHU Coimbra bought PROMs/PREMs, telemonitoring and OMOP project support from NTT Data Portugal by direct award (EUR 19,900, 2024), showing PROMs programmes run by integrators. [source](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=10729497)

### research_ted (14)

- The TED API (window since 2023-10-01) returned only one EU tender explicitly for a standalone digital preoperative screening system: AZORG (Belgium), published 2026-10-12, requests due 2026-11-10, 48-month contract. It asks for home-based pre-op anamnesis, multilingual questionnaires and videos, analysis of answers with next-step suggestions, and EPR (KWS) integration. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/702720-2026)
- German university hospitals buy pre-op/Prämedikation software by direct award. Mannheim used a VEAT (exclusive-rights justification) to give Novacair B.V. a 4-year contract, requiring a CE-marked medical device, ISO 27001, GDPR and a bidirectional interface. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/728166-2025)
- In Germany and Belgium, pre-op (Prämedikation / pre-anaesthesia consultation) is often bought inside anaesthesia information systems (AIMS). HeCaPP made a pre-op consultation module a required option in a 10-year anaesthesia software contract (EUR 1.07M, ICARE). Albertinen Hamburg required the AIMS to cover the Prämedikation visit and send its summary to the KIS. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/1380-2026)
- KHZG funding (Krankenhauszukunftsfonds, refinanced by the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility) drove a wave of German patient-portal (FTB 2) and digital-consent tenders. Kliniken Köln's notice says the funding comes from KHZF refinanced through the EU RRF and imposes FTB 2 must-criteria. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/530180-2025)
- A TED full-text search for 'Patientenportal' since 2023-10-01 returned 410 notices, nearly all German KHZG FTB 2 portals for digital admission and treatment management. Many explicitly include digital anamnesis questionnaires before admission (for example Klinikum Nürnberg: questionnaires for digital anamnesis, HL7 FHIR, gematik/TI). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/250338-2024)
- Digital consent in Germany is concentrated with Thieme Compliance (E-ConsentPro). It won Aachen, Köln (EUR 883,780.91), Halle (EUR 338,287), the Albertinen group, Mittelrhein, Fürstenfeldbruck, Charité and Rhön. Halle alone processes about 116,000 consent forms a year. Buyers now ask for consent forms pre-filled from KIS or portal anamnesis data and an at-home workflow. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/851883-2025)
- In German OR coordination, sqior medical has won repeated direct awards on uniqueness grounds (MHH, Heidelberg EUR 694,980, Rostock, Erlangen, LMU, Bonn, Freiburg, Mannheim; Mainz planned). Bonn ran an EU-wide market sounding (PIN) first and then direct-awarded. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/300707-2026)
- ERAS software buying in the EU points to Encare. UK Münster's 2026 market consultation set minimum requirements (ERAS Society authorisation, 11 specialty programmes, a digital prehabilitation module, audit and benchmarking platform, EIAS data migration) that effectively describe the incumbent. Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana (2025, EUR 100k) said EIAS was the only system it knew. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/509259-2026)
- France's central purchasing body GIP RESAH holds single-supplier 5-year frameworks (up to EUR 10M each) for PROMs (SKEZI), PREMs (BETTER WORLD), consent (DrData) and telemedicine (ROFIM). Its operating-theatre flow/coordination lot was declared without award for insufficient competition. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/399745-2025)
- Region Hovedstaden (Denmark) puts its regional volume at about 600,000 surgical procedures a year (of about 2 million in Denmark). Its needs assessment for reducing postoperative complications asks for PRO data collection, multidisciplinary risk decision support, shared decision-making with the surgeon, and better pre-anaesthesia access to patient information. Innovation partnership(s) were planned for 2024. [source](https://eu.eu-supply.com/app/docmgmt/downloadPublicDocument.asp?FMT=5&AT=3&LID=451184&DVID=16034215)
- LUMC's concept telemonitoring requirements (Jan 2026) include care paths that switch pre-operative to post-operative on a schedule, NEN 7510/7512/7513 + MDR + WGBO certification, DigiD/MFA patient login, HiX integration (CS Zorgplatform, HL7 ADT), a FHIR export API and >99.5% availability. LUMC is also piloting PROMs on LUMC@Home and plans one combined tender for platform, devices and logistics. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/408350/documenten/13575475/content)
- Belgian EPR replacements bundle perioperative and questionnaire features. HH Ziekenhuis Lier's EUR 8.69M, 120-month EPR (nexuzhealth) includes the anaesthesia nursing record, OR planning, and a patient portal for questionnaires with itsme authentication. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/416167-2026)
- Post-procedure remote monitoring is being bought through small direct awards in the Netherlands: Amsterdam UMC gave ikHerstel B.V. a 36-month award (estimated EUR 266,000 a year, about 750 users a month) for an app guiding physical recovery after procedures. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/70081-2026)
- Above-threshold EU buyers outside DE, BE, NL, DK, SI and FR published almost no pre-op, perioperative-pathway or PROMs software tenders on TED in the window. Searches in Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish, Finnish, Polish and Czech pre-op terms returned only device or service notices. [source](https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search)

### research_uk-cf (14)

- On Contracts Finder, digital pre-op assessment purchases are small call-offs or direct awards, typically £50k–£250k, made under frameworks rather than open tenders. Routes seen: G-Cloud 13/14, Digital Workplace Solutions 2, the LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions (CDHS) framework, NOE Total Technology Solutions and NHS SBS. No open pre-op assessment competition was published on Contracts Finder between Oct 2023 and Oct 2026. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Many pre-op deals are 12-month renewals (UHD MyPreOp 2026/27; PAHT Pathpoint ePOA renewed in 2025/26 and again in 2026/27). That creates frequent decision points for a challenger. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- Worcestershire Acute switched pre-op supplier in 2024: a Vitalhub interim term (Feb–Oct 2024, £81k) was followed by a 3-year Ultramed contract (£240k, Nov 2024–Oct 2027). Incumbents can be displaced. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- Renewal calendar from Contracts Finder: UHD MyPreOp ends 2027-03-31; PAHT ePOA 2027-03-31; Northumbria (Vitalhub) 2027-07-05; Worcestershire (Ultramed) 2027-10-31; Somerset (Pathpoint) 2028-03-31; NWAFT (Ultraprep) 2029-05-31. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecfccd32-f3aa-4601-b26f-c29dc6ed5ed8)
- Large resellers (Softcat) are often the contracting party for pre-op and consent SaaS (MyPreOp, Ultraprep, Concentric). Getting listed on reseller frameworks such as DWS2 and NOE TTS is a practical route to market. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/0d978ff9-f1e5-44a0-87c9-af3e7827f57d)
- The Atamis Health Family eCommercial portal (health-family.force.com) is the dominant gate for NHS trust tenders and PMEs found here (South Tees consent, ROH PROMs and Integrated Digital Pathway, Northumbria theatres, CHFT PEP, UHB anaesthetic middleware). Specifications are only visible after supplier registration. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a5f1a235-f0a2-4b88-bd31-d8e8125ba487)
- NHS Commercial Solutions is setting up a £1.4bn Patient Healthcare Communications and Related IT Services framework (2025-12 to 2033-12, 13 lots, including Lot 11 Streamlined Patient Pathways/flow and Lot 12 AI-enabled Digital Care). It replaces the NHSE-endorsed framework and requires compliance with government open standards. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1)
- Waiting-list validation buys name the NHS App as an integration (NHS Devon/Netcall) and tie the software to NHS England validation requirements and the 18-week RTT standard. Patient questionnaires are being used for validation (WHHT Zesty Form Builder). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)
- Digital consent is an active adjacent market on Contracts Finder (Eido, Concentric). South Tees has a live evaluation for a Digital Consent and Shared Decision Making solution (£135k, 3+1+1 years, start Jan 2027), so bundling consent or SDM with pre-op is a credible offer. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Trusts with a full digital surgical pathway assemble it from separate point solutions. Princess Alexandra holds separate contracts for Pathpoint ePOA (Open Medical), Concentric e-consent (via Softcat) and a Zesty patient portal (plus an earlier DrDoctor engagement platform). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/bb3a3afe-6cfb-4105-aa23-65298a55da8d)
- A G-Cloud single-supplier justification for surgical analytics (C2-Ai at Mersey and West Lancs) shows typical NHS minimum non-functional filters: UK data storage and processing, ISO/IEC 27001, private cloud, onsite support, mobile use, and the supplier not being a reseller. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3cf68fc8-3310-4f51-8172-c34e5675e97f)
- Specialist elective orthopaedic trust ROH ran pre-market engagement for both a PROMs platform (Aug 2024) and an Integrated Digital Pathway (Oct 2024). The PROMs notice stresses nationally mandated pre/post-surgery questionnaires and the separation of patient-identifiable data for linkage. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecb9175f-fa04-4a40-9e3c-b882333fc43c)
- Large EPR awards on Contracts Finder (e.g. Mid Yorkshire's £38.03m 10-year Nervecentre EPR via the LPP CDHS framework, Feb 2026) do not name perioperative or pre-op questionnaire scope in the public notice. EPR consolidation is still a risk to standalone pre-op tools. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3310b148-e5ce-4725-85da-c93412854033)
- A theatre system replacement at Northumbria (replacing Nexus Sapphire, about 1,000+ users) asked bidders to cost a flexible licence model (concurrent, perpetual, subscription or enterprise) because user numbers may change. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/5c2dc86f-b71f-4768-a52f-4728e0bfb2b8)

### research_uk-consent-sdm (14)

- UK buying for digital consent is dominated by direct awards and framework call-offs (G-Cloud 13, OE Total Technology Solutions), usually with price as the only award criterion and one tender received. South Tees (Sept 2026) is the only open competitive tender found for consent plus SDM, and it scores on more than price. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/083956-2026)
- Concentric publishes a model specification that buyers can copy into tenders. It asks for: a DTAC self-assessment, DSPT, Cyber Essentials Plus within 12 months, a DCB0129 safety case, an annual pen test, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+, a full audit trail per episode, and SSO (Entra ID/NHSmail/ADFS). It also asks for patient identity via e-signature or NHS login, launch in context from the EHR, demographic integration, 99.95% availability, and PIF TICK. Clinically: NICE ESF Tier B evidence, consent forms 1/2/4, multi-stage consent with revocation, 1,500+ templates, translations, registry (NJR) and tissue/research consents, and usage reporting by specialty. [source](https://concentric.health/deployment/delivery-playbook/digital-consent-specification/)
- An impact assessment by Health Innovation Oxford and Thames Valley (funded by the HTA&A Fund via BOB ICB) found Concentric digital consent saved over 7 minutes per consent episode at OUH ophthalmology. It projected £5.64 saved per episode, about £167k over 3 years at around 825 episodes a month. [source](https://www.healthcare-management.uk/widespread-digitisation-consenting-process-bring-multiple-benefits)
- A peer-reviewed micro-costing study (Imperial) found a paper consent episode costs about £0.90 more than a digital one, and estimated an average saving of £201,590 per litigation claim prevented. [source](https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/entities/publication/3212282c-4402-4de4-843a-16f5962e5546)
- Medway NHS FT's FOI (Sept 2024) shows a typical trust: EIDO patient information leaflets in every department at £13,691.64 a year (renewal 12 Aug 2025), but no e-consent solution in any department, including surgery. That is a whitespace for digital consent. [source](https://www.medway.nhs.uk/uploads/2024/09/FOI-9056-Contracts-Procurement-September-2024.docx)
- Mid and South Essex piloted EIDO digital consent from Nov 2024 (Breast, then ENT). Patients get links by email or SMS and verify with surname plus date of birth; NHS login is not mentioned. Consent can be signed on screen in clinic, sent to a parent or guardian for under-16s, and the PDF is saved into the EPR. [source](https://mse.nhs.uk/digital-patient-consent-system)
- WUTH's Concentric deployment works the same way: a unique link plus date of birth, email or SMS from Concentric, the PDF auto-transferred into the EPR, and data hosted on Google Cloud in a UK data centre. [source](https://wuth.nhs.uk/your-health/patient-portal/consent/)
- NHS England publishes free patient decision aids (decision support tools, built with the Winton Centre to the NICE SDM standards framework). Surgical topics include AAA, gallstones, glue ear, inguinal hernia, BPE, tonsillitis and varicose veins. With free content available, we found no standalone procurement of patient decision aids in the window; SDM is being bundled into consent tenders instead (e.g. South Tees). [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/shared-decision-making/decision-support-tools)
- NHS England's 2026/27 Referrals and Appointments fund (£15-20m, bids closed 31 May 2026) targets BaRS, e-RS, the NHS App/Wayfinder, PIFU and GIRFT pathway transformation. Trade-press coverage does not mention consent or pre-op; that funding route for consent rests only on a vendor's reading of offer 3a. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/05/15/up-to-20-million-national-funding-for-referrals-and-appointments-opens/)
- Concentric argues that offer 3a of the Referrals and Appointments fund (transforming GIRFT and Elective Care Programme priority pathways) can fund digital consent projects. This is the vendor's view, not NHS England's. [source](https://concentric.health/news/referrals-and-appointments-funding/)
- Concentric's 2024 review reports 250% year-on-year growth, about 6,000 new clinicians, over 500k patients, and weekly consents up from 7,500 to over 17,000. Top procedures were OGD, colonoscopy and cataract. Circle Health is rolling out to 54 hospitals; UHL was the first trust past 2,000 consents a week. [source](https://concentric.health/news/2024-review/)
- Northern Ireland trusts keep renewing EIDO by direct award, citing a sole supplier and exclusive licence rights (SEHSCT) or disruption from switching (NHSCT). Incumbent lock-in on consent content is strong there. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/023239-2025)
- Northumbria's Sept 2023 PIN limited its supplier day to vendors with a tried and tested, off-the-shelf consent platform ready to deploy. Buyers want proven products rather than co-development. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028353-2023)
- Contracts coming up for renewal: Warrington and Halton EIDO (31 Dec 2026), PAHT Concentric (31 Mar 2027), Barts/NEL Concentric base term (about Apr 2027, final end 1 Apr 2028), SEHSCT EIDO (1 Jun 2027), UHNM EIDO (11 Jun 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/0d978ff9-f1e5-44a0-87c9-af3e7827f57d)

### research_uk-engagement (17)

- NHS England's 2023/24 expectation: every non-specialist acute trust should have a patient portal. The minimum functions were viewing outpatient appointments, sending waiting list validation questionnaires, a single point of contact including cancellations, and access to correspondence. Trusts were asked to surface portals in the NHS App via Wayfinder, with revenue funding from April 2023. In March 2023, 84 trusts had portals and 19 were procuring. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/04/20/nhs-england-announces-investment-to-accelerate-patient-portals-with-implementation-target-set/)
- NHS England digital-first blog (7 Jun 2025): the NHS App becomes the primary channel, with NHS Notify fallbacks, and secondary care rolls out through PEPs to connect all acute and specialist trusts. The target is 270m app-first messages by Mar 2026. Rotherham sends preoperative triage questionnaires through the app to all surgical waiting-list patients, and over a quarter needed no face-to-face pre-assessment, saving 30-60 minutes of nurse time each. [source](https://nhsd-proxy.openprescribing.net/blog/transformation-blog/2025/a-digital-first-approach-to-patient-communications)
- Patient Care Aggregator (Wayfinder) onboarding: every feature needs the System Requirement Specification (SRS) and an SCAL. Notifications & Messaging and Documents are mandatory before additional features. Questionnaires require Documents onboarding. Each trust must update DCB0160, receive the PEP supplier's DCB0129 assurance, and update its DPIA, DPA/CCN, privacy notice and EHIA, and comply with the DSPT. Key metrics must be reported monthly. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator/additional-further-features-to-your-integration-with-the-patient-care-aggregator/eligibility-onboarding-kick-off-and-documentation)
- Requirements for a secondary-care portal to integrate with the PCA: NHS login authentication; one technical endpoint across NHS login, NHS App and PCA (not one per trust); Record Service API and Get Appointments API (which can return documents and questionnaires); NHS design system and Figma prototype; DCB0129/DCB0160, DSPT, ISO/IEC 27001, penetration testing, DPIA and EHIA. [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator/integrating-a-secondary-care-booking-system)
- In the PCA, the NHS App shows an 'actionable items' flag for documents and questionnaires, currently limited to acute outpatient appointments, and deep-links to the portal for completion. The roadmap has PIFU in the NHS App for Oct-Dec 2026 and secondary-care proxy access for Jan-Mar 2027 (page edited 10 Sep 2026). [source](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator)
- NHS App planned integrations (16 Sep 2026): EBO and TPP SystmOne for Documents and Questionnaires; PKB for Questionnaires (mental health) and PIFU; UHS My Medical Record and Cisco (Healthcare Communications) for NHS Notify secondary-care notifications. [source](https://nhsd-proxy.openprescribing.net/services/nhs-app/how-to-integrate-with-the-nhs-app/nhs-app-integrated-partners-and-services/partners-and-services-that-plan-to-be-integrated)
- Policy direction toward EPR-native NHS App integration: NHSE capital funded a TPP direct award (£960k) for SystmOne-to-NHS App (Wayfinder) integration. A consultancy commentary claims NHSE has 'put on notice' standalone PEP suppliers (DrDoctor, PKB, Induction Zesty), citing about £11m a year in savings. That is commentary, not an NHSE document. [source](https://www.healthcare.digital/single-post/the-disintermediation-of-patient-portals-in-england-the-nhs-app-direct-epr-integrations-and-digita)
- Lancashire & South Cumbria use an NHS-built regional portal (PEP+, built in-house by UHMBT's digital team under Project Wayfinder) across the ICS trusts. It covers appointments, letters, questionnaires linked to the patient record, a 'Set for Surgery' section and NHS App login. This shows in-house or regional build as an alternative to buying. [source](https://www.lancsteachinghospitals.nhs.uk/patientengagementportal)
- Princess Alexandra Hospital launched an electronic pre-operative assessment (ePOA) questionnaire in Oct 2025. Patients complete it at home through a secure web portal accessible from the NHS App, then nurses triage to phone or face-to-face assessment, anaesthetic review, exercise test, or referral to physio, diabetes or pharmacy. [source](https://www.pah.nhs.uk/?p=7047)
- Shrewsbury & Telford (SaTH) moved pre-op assessment online from 22 Jun 2026, starting with gynaecology. Patients get a text prompt to complete the questionnaire at home, and complex patients are still seen face-to-face. [source](https://www.sath.nhs.uk/news/47376/)
- A South Yorkshire trust's Patient Hub integration with the NHS App (Dec 2025) gives access to outpatient and surgical appointments, questionnaires, letters and pre-assessments. About 8,000 PIFU pathways could benefit by end of 2026. [source](https://southyorkshire.icb.nhs.uk/news/patient-initiated-follow-appointments-integrated-nhs-app-national-first)
- FOI requests to trusts commonly define a PEP as including completion of digital questionnaires such as pre- and post-operative assessments and PROMs/PREMs. Salisbury's PEP was DrDoctor, 01/04/2022 to 31/03/2025. [source](https://www.salisbury.nhs.uk/about-us/freedom-of-information-foi/previous-foi-requests/foi_7803/)
- Royal Berkshire directly awarded a patient portal add-on (video consultation and form builder) after evaluating six internally used patient portals in a rationalisation. Trusts are consolidating several portals into one. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/011620-2025)
- University Hospitals of Leicester hired Apira (Jul-Oct 2026, £58.2k) to map every PEP and patient-facing system at UHL, run a gap analysis and gather requirements for new systems. This points to a UHL PEP procurement in 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/571540ec-93ba-4400-9c67-c32b524ba8cd)
- Most PEP buys are short (often 12-month) framework call-offs via G-Cloud 13/14, NHS SBS SBS10175/SBS10521, RM6094 or the NHS Commercial Solutions framework. That creates frequent renewal points: ENHT Mar 2027, PAHT Mar 2027, KGH Oct 2026, UHB ROH/BWC Mar 2026, Hull/HNY PKB Mar 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/f134a186-463a-4202-9b0c-dfe5fdffa9ac)
- Cambridgeshire & Peterborough ICB digital front door market engagement (Oct 2024): mandatory conformance with the national Personal Health Record specification and NHS App alignment, mandatory NHS Login integration, open standards and APIs, and links to hospital portals such as MyChart. The scope is mostly primary care, self-care and 'waiting well', with no perioperative function. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/be6a71aa-a92a-424a-8daf-82d347fae437)
- Typical NHS digital assurance list in a 2025 ICB supplier briefing (primary care, Surrey Heartlands): DCB0129, DTAC, DSPT, ICO registration, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 27001 where applicable, MHRA medical device where applicable, WCAG 2.1 AA, NHS Login, NHS App onboarding, SystmOne/EMIS integration, NHS smartcard SSO. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7a05c6b6-5e59-443b-b6d7-5f07d32892ef)

### research_uk-frameworks (17)

- No national UK framework or DPS has a lot dedicated to digital pre-operative assessment. Trusts buy pre-op SaaS mainly through G-Cloud (13/14/15), the LPP CDHS catalogue and reseller IT frameworks (NHS SBS DWS2, NOE CPC TTS) via Softcat. Most call-off notices do not name the framework. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Pre-op call-off values are small and renewed yearly or over 2–3 years: about £51k–£123k a year (PAHT Pathpoint £74–76k a year; UHD MyPreOp £92k a year; Northumbria VitalHub £124k over 2 years; Worcestershire Ultramed £240k over 3 years; NWAFT Ultraprep £223k over 3 years). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- G-Cloud 15 pricing models for pre-op vary: per instance or team (Pathpoint from £48.5k a year), per transaction (AireFrame £2.40; Synopsis £2.90–£3.50 per pre-op; MyPreOp+ £3.13–£6.25 per submission), per patient (Remcare £3–£14 a year) and per specialty (NEC PACT £30k per specialty plus £0.25 per patient, with £20k onboarding). [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721733/214669371000433-pricing-document-2026-01-29-1809.pdf)
- Accreditations pre-op competitors advertise on G-Cloud 15: ISO 27001 (Open Medical, Aire, VitalHub, NEC, Ultramed, Buddy), Cyber Essentials Plus (nearly all), DSPT, DCB0129/0160 (Aire, Concentric, Isla, DrDoctor), DTAC (Concentric, EIDO, Isla, DrDoctor, PreActiv, Surgery Hero) and UKCA Class I medical device (Remcare). All state UK data storage. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/433084683660941)
- Integrations competitors advertise: PAS/EPR via HL7 v2 and FHIR, PDS, NHS e-RS, MESH, NHS Login (Remcare), NHS App (DrDoctor, Isla), EPR context launch (Isla for Epic/Cerner) and SNOMED-CT coding (Pathpoint). [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/283818920610894)
- NHS SBS's new Patient/Citizen Communication, Engagement & Hybrid Mail framework (SBS10521, £250m) explicitly covers Patient Engagement Portals and surveys, making it a route for questionnaire/engagement products. PAHT has already called off a PEP (Zesty) under it. [source](https://www.sbs.nhs.uk/news/new-250m-communication-framework-launched/)
- NHS SBS cites an estimated £1.2bn a year lost to missed appointments (DNAs) as the driver for its patient communication framework. [source](https://www.sbs.nhs.uk/news/new-250m-communication-framework-launched/)
- LPP plans CDHS 2.0 (about £2.4bn, possibly 8 years), with a contract notice expected early 2027 and a start around Oct 2027. The current CDHS (81 suppliers, single lot, Oct 2024 – Sep 2028) allows direct award from a list-price catalogue and has been used for pre-op SaaS (PAHT Pathpoint). [source](https://www.publictechnology.net/?p=13604)
- NHS England bought a G-Cloud 13 service (Mason Advisory, £272k, Nov 2023 – Mar 2024) for Wayfinder MI/KPI reporting and to set up a PEP supplier onboarding function and governance for NHS App/Wayfinder integration. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/fcbff905-a2f2-4055-b816-d2c895d4a131)
- Commentary (Nelson Advisors, not an NHS England primary source) says NHS England intends to move core appointment functions to the NHS App and disintermediate standalone PEPs (about £11m a year saving). It also says the planned-care pillar includes digital pre-operative questionnaires and that Epic–NHS App direct integration can push pre-assessment forms. [source](https://www.healthcare.digital/single-post/the-disintermediation-of-patient-portals-in-england-the-nhs-app-direct-epr-integrations-and-digita)
- Trust PEP specifications now require NHS App sign-in and Wayfinder surfacing of appointments, letters, forms and results, plus clinical questionnaires linked to the EPR (HIOW PEP pre-tender, £800k). [source](https://stotles.com/explore/notices/ac970a7a-6082-4bf9-88b7-1a4df9ee7620/patient-engagement-portal-pep)
- The NHS England national PROMs/registries platform (ORCA) is on a two-year transition contract with NEC (£4.16m to Sep 2027), and a replacement procurement is intended in 2026. This is a national PROMs opportunity adjacent to pre-op. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9)
- PROMs have been a nationally mandated data collection for all providers of NHS-funded care since April 2009, with paired pre-op and 6-month post-op questionnaires. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/a5f1a235-f0a2-4b88-bd31-d8e8125ba487)
- Digital consent is bought through several routes: G-Cloud 13 (Barts/NEL with Concentric, £45k a year), NOE CPC TTS via Softcat (PAHT with Concentric), a DPS (NUH with EIDO) and an open tender (South Tees Digital Consent and SDM, £135k, start Jan 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- The NHS SBS TECS2 remote monitoring framework (£150m, 19 suppliers, six lots) was extendable to January 2027, so a successor is due. It is relevant to post-discharge remote monitoring modules. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/03/27/nhs-sbs-updates-remote-patient-monitoring-procurement-framework/)
- Patients Know Best lists the frameworks a portal vendor can be bought through: NHS SBS TECS Lot 4, G-Cloud, HSSF Lot 2B and Lot 7 (Patient Empowerment and Activation), LPP CDIS Lot 3.6 (Clinical and Patient Portal), the Wales Digital Patient Service Partners DPS and an Online Consultations DPS. [source](https://procurement.patientsknowbest.com/business-docs/procurement-frameworks-to-purchase-pkb)
- The Digital Marketplace currently offers both G-Cloud 15 and G-Cloud 14 supplier services; most pre-op products are re-listed on G-Cloud 15 Lot 2b (SaaS). [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/106177073699977)

### research_uk-fts (19)

- Digital Health & Care Wales plans one all-Wales pre-operative digital system (£5m excl. VAT, 2027-2032, extendable to 2034) with health screening at listing, risk stratification, remote completion, digital inclusion and structured data for national repositories. A tender notice was expected 1 May 2026 but has not appeared on FTS. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026)
- Royal Surrey's £300k electronic POA tender weights scripted demonstrations at 25%, equal to technical response and price. Requirement-spec compliance is 15% and social value 10%. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073826-2026)
- NHS Scotland's 2023 PIN combined a national pre-op assessment online triage tool (remote questionnaire, staged patient support, clinician triage, EPR integration) with theatre scheduling across 381 theatres. Only theatre scheduling went to contract on FTS (Infix Support, £6.3m). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007268-2023)
- Betsi Cadwaladr UHB's 2022 pre-op PIN (before the window) set baseline requirements: replace all paper POA within 6 months, home completion, multi-user record access, automatic risk categorisation by surgical severity and history, Welsh PAS and Clinical Portal integration, and bilingual English/Welsh information. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/010485-2022)
- London North West University Healthcare awarded a digital pre-operative assessment platform contract in March 2022 (before the window): £52,780 against a £150,000 estimate, 7 tenders, quality 70/price 30. No successor procurement was found on FTS, so the account may be due for renewal. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007921-2022)
- Trusts are buying clinical insourcing to clear pre-op assessment backlogs through the NHS SBS Insourcing of Clinical Services framework (SBS10203) and urgent PSR awards (ULTH, Stockport, James Paget, Royal Wolverhampton). Royal Wolverhampton cited delays in listing patients for surgery. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/054233-2025)
- Royal Berkshire direct-awarded orthopaedic PROMs to Amplitude, saying that after market engagement no other provider had experience of both collecting PROMs/NJR data and uploading to registries. KPIs were not set: 'proprietary software with no other options in the market'. Registry-upload capability is a de facto entry barrier for perioperative PROMs. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/044783-2026)
- The All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, £11.9m, concluded 13 Oct 2023, 3+1 years) is at or near expiry, which points to a Welsh re-procurement in 2026-27. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/032382-2023)
- Bradford and Airedale re-tendered their patient experience portal in July 2026 (£4.33m) after the Dec 2025 award to Zesty, Xerox and Oracle. The minimum scope includes digital forms and waiting list validation, native Oracle EPR integration, and alignment with the NHS App and Patient Care Aggregator (Wayfinder). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/070821-2026)
- Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare's PEP requirements show the portal checklist trusts use: custom clinical questionnaires and online forms linked to the record, NHS App sign-in and Wayfinder surfacing of appointments, letters and forms, proxy access, two-way messaging, and all patient data held in the EPR. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/041626-2024)
- Warrington and Halton required its patient engagement portal to exchange data with the EPR through bi-directional interfaces and open APIs and to integrate with the NHS App and NHS login (DrDoctor, £2.24m, 2024). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024)
- King's College Hospital and Guy's and St Thomas' plan a £3.75m patient communication and engagement contract (SMS, portal, hybrid mail, chatbot, appointment management) integrated with Epic, framed around the elective backlog. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/034123-2025)
- United Lincolnshire has a £7m pipeline notice for a patient engagement portal and hybrid mail, 2028-2032 (extendable to 2035), expected to go through an NHS framework. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/048809-2026)
- Hywel Dda UHB, through CGI, is procuring a Patient Service Centre and 360-degree patient view that will work alongside a patient engagement platform. It covers waiting list support and pathway management, from 2027 to 2032. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/054009-2026)
- Waiting-list optimisation is being bought as services across the North East and Cumbria (Waiting Well), explicitly to cut the preventable postponements and cancellations identified in the national PACE study. These programmes depend on early pre-op risk identification. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073708-2026)
- Small perioperative SaaS (consent, prehab apps, PROMs) is usually bought below threshold without competition or as a G-Cloud call-off with one-year terms, such as WHTHT prehab, Gateshead Surgery Hero and Somerset Amplitude. Renewals cluster in Oct-Nov 2026. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/083730-2025)
- A signed G-Cloud 14 eConsent call-off (EIDO at Countess of Chester) shows typical hospital SaaS terms: about £15k a year licence plus £5k deployment, unlimited users and SMS, EPR demographics pull and write-back, SSO, the Buyer as data controller under UK GDPR, and Cyber Essentials on request. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/A-18118)
- Atamis (the NHS Health Family eCommercial portal) holds the specifications for most English trust tenders in this space: Royal Surrey, Somerset, UHB, ROH, Sheffield, South Tees, Bradford, QVH, Northumbria and NENC. Requirements are only visible after registering interest. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/060687-2025)
- Aneurin Bevan's Theatre Management System engagement requires Welsh-language bilingual support and WCAG compliance, which are likely baseline asks for any Welsh perioperative system. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/049165-2025)

### research_uk-proms-remote (19)

- NHS England plans to procure a strategic replacement for its national Outcomes and Registries platform (which captures PROMs/PREMs) in 2026. The NEC transition contract runs to 30 Sep 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9)
- The national registries platform spec requires NHS App integration, EuroQol (EQ-5D) integration, PDS/MPS linkage, UK cloud hosting, DSPT 'standards met' and alignment with the NHS Data Dictionary. These are a useful checklist for any PROMs product feeding national datasets. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/6b082f6d-d403-4494-9b9b-76f7d799c8ea)
- Royal Berkshire direct-awarded orthopaedic PROMs to Amplitude under the Procurement Act 2023. Market engagement found no other provider with proven PROMs and NJR collection and upload experience. NHS income tied to registry compliance makes buyers risk-averse. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-060e44)
- Trust orthopaedic PROMs buys also need submission to many registries (NHS England, PHIN, BOFAS, BSSH, NLR, UKKOR, NAHR, BSR, ICRS, HQIP/NJR via NEC), not only the national PROMs survey. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/006556-2026)
- Trust-level PROMs contracts are small, from about GBP 12k a year to GBP 150k over 3 years. They are often bought by single tender action or DPS/framework call-off, with annual renewals. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2bdf583c-7316-46af-8bd1-59c645ecee89)
- Wales buys PROMs nationally through the NWSSP All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, GBP 11.9m, concluded 13 Oct 2023, 3+1 years) aligned to the WViHC PROMs Standard Operating Model. By my inference the framework is due for renewal around Oct 2026–Oct 2027. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032382-2023)
- Welsh PROMs mini-competitions were weighted 70% quality / 30% cost. They allowed other health boards to onboard later without re-competition (Velindre, Cardiff & Vale). [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/search_switch.aspx?ID=146858)
- Sheffield Teaching Hospitals buys hip and knee PROMs as an outsourced survey service (CPV 79311000) in electronic and paper formats. Paper fallback remains a requirement. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/073670-2025)
- NHS SBS Technology Enabled Care Services 2 (SBS10144) Lot 1 Remote Clinical Monitoring is the main route for virtual ward/RPM call-offs (ESHT/SCFT, ULTH, Lincolnshire ICB, HIOW ICB, Northampton). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/62a982c3-7ee4-4a06-82ff-f141d0602052)
- NHSScotland is soft-testing a national multi-channel remote health monitoring and communications solution to replace or re-procure Connect Me (on Inhealthcare), with a contract notice expected Jul 2026. It explicitly includes early discharge and hospital at home. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAY555119)
- NHS LPP is scoping a framework or dynamic market for telemedicine and virtual ward services aligned with elective recovery (indicative 2026-12 to 2028-12). This is a possible future route for post-op remote monitoring. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2af38823-ffc8-4306-891f-4b5471f40433)
- NHS Commercial Solutions' replacement Patient & Healthcare Communications framework (GBP 1.4bn, 2025–2033) includes Lot 11 'Streamlined Patient Pathways/flow' and Lot 12 'AI-enabled Digital Care systems'. These are routes to market for patient-facing pathway tools. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1)
- NHS SBS ran an RFI in Oct 2024 for 'Patient Communication & Engagement Solutions 2' (SBS10521), another framework route for patient engagement and questionnaire tools. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/8103686e-aff5-49ce-a87c-42525cece2f3)
- The patient-app minimum spec in the NHSE SACT ePROMs contract lists essentials buyers expect: iOS, Android and PC access, NHS App compatibility, published DPIA, Edge browser support, no Google Cloud storage (IG/DaAG), quick PROM form edits, reminders, carer sharing, block pricing, DTAC/ISO/GDPR. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/6b88f2b0-2890-4213-99c5-bcc59d54e570)
- NHSGGC raised its Doccla virtual ward contract from GBP 307k to GBP 3.93m by modification for scale-up. RPM contracts often grow after award without new competition. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=SEP538698)
- UHB/BSol's GBP 1.67m Integrated Patient Pathway tender was abandoned in Dec 2025 because NHSE funding conditions needed material changes. A re-launch is likely. Its award criteria were Technical 70%, Social Value 20%, Presentation 10%. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-05a274)
- Vitalhub UK won both a pre-operative assessment software contract (Northumbria, 2025–2027) and ROH's eOutcomes PROMs support. One competitor spans pre-op and PROMs. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecfccd32-f3aa-4601-b26f-c29dc6ed5ed8)
- Scotland's national MSK digital solution preliminary market consultation (live to 18 Nov 2026) asks for self-referral, triage, remote monitoring and rehabilitation tools compatible with MyCare.scot. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT566180)
- NHS England ran an 'Online Forms Pilot' with DrDoctor via G-Cloud 13 from 17 Aug 2023, later varied for extra SMS consumables. NHSE is piloting digital clinical forms and questionnaires directly. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/eca89ee2-1071-4c83-8ddd-84fcb6af96fd)

### research_uk-trust-portals (29)

- NHS England's perioperative guidance (published May 2023, updated 21 May 2025) restates the NHS digital health and care plan expectation that all providers offer digital pre-assessment by September 2024. It sets five core requirements: earliest screening and triage after listing; personalised optimisation; contacting all inpatient-waiting patients at least every 3 months (automation allowed); dating surgery only after risk assessment and fitness; and shared decision-making. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/earlier-screening-risk-assessment-and-health-optimisation-in-perioperative-pathways/)
- The 2024/25 NHS Standard Contract (section 3.18) requires providers to implement and maintain early screening, risk assessment and health optimisation for adult inpatient surgery waiting-list patients, with the five core requirements for all inpatient pathways by April 2024. This is a contractual driver for pre-op software spend. NHS England also says it is working with suppliers to broaden patient engagement portals. [source](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/earlier-screening-risk-assessment-and-health-optimisation-in-perioperative-pathways/)
- GIRFT published guidance (17 Sep 2024) on choosing a digital supplier for pre-operative care. It includes comparison tables for 15 suppliers, based on technologies available as of July 2023; the document sits on FutureNHS (login required). [source](https://gettingitrightfirsttime.co.uk/girft-offers-guidance-to-choosing-a-digital-supplier-to-support-pre-operative-care/)
- Buyer pattern: almost every pre-op and adjacent award found was a framework call-off or direct award, not an open tender. Routes included G-Cloud 13/14, LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions, Digital Workplace Solutions 2, NHS SBS SBS10521, CCS RM6094 and OE Total Technology Solutions. Contracts were short (often 12-24 months) and frequently bought through a reseller (Softcat). Royal Surrey (2026) is the main open-procedure pre-op tender found. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Atamis (Health Family eCommercial System) is the dominant portal for these NHS trust notices: nearly all relevant Contracts Finder records were created by an Atamis user, and tender documents (Royal Surrey, South Tees, ROH, Northumbria theatres, Bradford) are gated behind Atamis supplier registration. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Royal Surrey's 2026 open pre-op tender weights scripted demonstrations at 25%, equal to price (25%) and technical response (25%), with requirement specification 15% and social value 10%. Buyers now score live demos heavily. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-06d687)
- Supplier churn is real: Worcestershire Acute moved its pre-op platform from Vitalhub (contract to 31 Oct 2024) to Ultramed (direct award from 1 Nov 2024). Princess Alexandra moved its patient engagement portal from DrDoctor (2023) to Zesty (2026). Incumbency is not secure on short terms. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3e45d535-f2a1-4b00-a86c-5535f81031a9)
- Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals runs pre-op digital pre-screening through the DrDoctor patient portal, not a dedicated pre-op product. Patients log in with surname, DOB and postcode or their NHS account, and the questionnaire is resent every three months while on the elective list. General engagement portals compete for pre-op questionnaire work. [source](https://www.nnuh.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Pre-Screening-Information-Sheet.pdf)
- Princess Alexandra Hospital launched ePOA in October 2025. It is a secure web portal accessed via the NHS App, completed by all surgical patients, and used for triage of urgent surgery. NHS App access is a live expectation at some trusts. [source](https://www.pah.nhs.uk/patients-visitors/appointments/electronic-pre-operative-assessment/)
- Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital launched an online pre-op questionnaire tool from 22 June 2026, starting with gynaecology; the supplier is not named. This is a recent adopter whose supplier and contract are unknown. [source](https://www.sath.nhs.uk/news/47376/)
- Somerset FT governors paper (19 Feb 2024): the board approved year-1 funding in June 2023 for a perioperative screening and optimisation service. Phases were funded at GBP 81k (21/22), GBP 145k (22/23) and GBP 320k (23/24, mainly staff), and a dedicated Digital Nurse Lead was funded. Digital POAC (Pathpoint) is the screening front end. Pre-op software is bought as part of a wider perioperative optimisation business case, not standalone. [source](https://www.somersetft.nhs.uk/about-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/148/2024/02/Strategy-and-Planning-Monday-19-February-2024.pdf)
- Open Medical's SBRI-backed case study (June 2025, West Hertfordshire data from Jun 2024 to May 2025) claims GBP 78,633 savings and about 1,561 avoided in-person visits. The gains come from complexity stratification and from extending POA validity from 3 to 6 months for ASA I-II patients. Vendors now sell on carbon and validity-extension benefits. [source](https://sbrihealthcare.co.uk/impact-case-studies/case-studies/open-medical-electronic-preoperative-assessment-epoa-module)
- G-Cloud 15 lists several digital pre-op products: Aire Innovate/Aire Logic ePOA, Vitalhub Synopsis, Open Medical Pathpoint ePOA and SurgiCare, plus the Ufonia Dora voice assistant. Standard assurance claims across them are ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, DSPT, DCB0129, UK data residency and HSCN. [source](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/search?q=pre-operative+assessment&lot=cloud-software)
- Upcoming renewal windows from published terms: UHD MyPreOp (ends 2027-03-31); PAHT Pathpoint ePOA (ends 2027-03-31); Northumbria pre-assessment (ends 2027-07-05); Worcestershire pre-op (ends 2027-10-31); Somerset Pathpoint (ends 2028-03-31); NWAFT Ultraprep (ends 2029-05-31). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2d78f3b3-5b19-4be3-86cf-3700525e3272)
- Northumbria Healthcare launched Synopsis iQ and Synopsis Home in July 2022 across four sites. The model builds a pool of 'pre-op ready' patients to fill theatre lists at short notice, links pre-op to theatre utilisation, and gives multi-site access to notes. [source](https://www.northumbria.nhs.uk/media-centre/news-and-blogs/news-stories/northumbria-healthcare-launches-digital-pre-operative-assessments-optimise-theatre-use)
- Someone ran a coordinated FOI campaign in July-Aug 2025, sending one 13-question template ('use of digital pre-operative assessment solutions': elective volumes, centralised POA service, web questionnaire supplier, renewal date, contract owner, contract value) to many trusts. It looks like supplier market mapping. WWL named DrDoctor, contract expiring Oct 2025. [source](https://www.wwl.nhs.uk/media/FOI/202526/04%20-%20July%202025/10899%20-%20Use%20of%20Digital%20Pre-operative%20Assessment%20Solutions.pdf)
- Dudley Group (28,002 elective operations in 2024/25, centralised POA service) has no web-based pre-op questionnaire and said it plans to introduce one. This is an open prospect. [source](https://www.dgft.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/FOI-072025-0001781.pdf)
- East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust said in Oct 2025 that it has no digital pre-operative assessment system in place. [source](https://www.esht.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/25-668-Disclosure-Log.pdf)
- Sherwood Forest Hospitals (King's Mill) said in June 2025 that it uses a paper-based pre-operative questionnaire, with no electronic home completion. [source](https://www.sfh-tr.nhs.uk/media/e0fa3kkc/foi-260-theatre-management-systems-and-pre-operative-assessments-110625.pdf)
- Many trusts run POA inside the EPR or PAS (Altera Sunrise, EMIS CaMIS, Careflow, E-Care), and FOIs say the pre-op cost 'cannot be split' from the EPR contract. EPR renewal dates (for example DBTH CaMIS Oct 2026, LHCH Altera May 2026, Mersey and West Lancs Careflow Oct 2025 and Mar 2027) are therefore the trigger points for a standalone POA buy. [source](https://www.merseywestlancs.nhs.uk//resources/download/sthk-68e764798fa590.26725952)
- NHS England's Medium-term planning framework (2026/27 to 2028/29) expects providers to let patients 'receive and complete pre and post-appointment questionnaires through the NHS App' by the end of 2028/29, with transitions starting in 2026/27. NHS App integration will become a de facto requirement for pre-op questionnaires. [source](https://healthcareleadernews.com/news/majority-of-appointments-to-be-available-on-nhs-app-from-april/)
- Most digital POA buys found are small framework call-offs (G-Cloud 13, DWS2, CDHS Integrated Health Economy, NOE TTS), often through resellers such as Softcat. Many are annual renewals (UHD, PAHT, QEH), so switching windows recur each year. Values range from about GBP 50k to 240k. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Royal Surrey's 2026 open ePOA tender gives 25% of the score to scripted demonstrations, 25% to the technical response, 15% to the requirement specification, 25% to price and 10% to social value. Demo performance carries as much weight as price. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-06d687)
- Worcestershire Acute appears to have moved its digital pre-op solution from Vitalhub (Synopsis, bridging contract Feb-Oct 2024) to Ultramed (Nov 2024-Oct 2027, GBP 240k). This is inferred from two consecutive Contracts Finder awards. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- NNUH uses DrDoctor for pre-op digital pre-screening. The questionnaire link is sent by SMS or email within a week of the decision to operate, and patients log in with surname, DOB and postcode or their NHS account. Generic engagement-portal vendors compete directly with POA specialists. [source](https://www.nnuh.nhs.uk/departments/pre-admission-assessment/pre-screening/)
- Medway NHS FT's May 2026 board papers list 'reduce face to face appointments for pre-assessment, moving to electronic questionnaire' and a 'zero touch' digital assessment form as productivity schemes. Patients Know Best, NHS App onboarding and a Graphnet decision sit in the same programme. This is an early demand signal with no procurement yet. [source](https://www.medway.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/trust-board-in-public-may-2026-papers.pdf)
- Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital (SaTH) launched an online pre-operative assessment questionnaire on 22 June 2026, starting with gynaecology, with SMS prompts from 18 June. The supplier was not named. [source](https://www.sath.nhs.uk/news/47376/)
- Atamis (Health Family / ProSpend) is the dominant e-sourcing portal for these NHS buys (Royal Surrey, South Tees, ROH/UHB, Northumbria NHFM, Barts). Specifications sit behind supplier registration, so suppliers need an Atamis account to read requirements. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/ecb9175f-fa04-4a40-9e3c-b882333fc43c)
- Digital Health and Care Wales opened preliminary market engagement (10 Mar 2026) for an all-Wales Pre-Operative Digital System. Minimum requirements: a national screening questionnaire at listing, risk stratification to aid site selection, home or clinic completion, digital inclusion, structured data for national repositories, and integration with NHS Wales systems (devolved; for cross-reference). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-06667b)

### research_uk-waitlist-prehab (13)

- Policy driver: NHS England 2025/26 planning guidance target of 65% of patients waiting no more than 18 weeks by March 2026 is cited directly as the purpose of a trust validation contract. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/075228-2025)
- Route to market: the Countess of Chester F075 National Data Validation Services framework (est. £10m, 2025-05-04 to 2029-05-03) is the main vehicle for RTT/PTL validation. It explicitly ties validation to PAS-to-EPR migration and to building in-house central validation and booking teams. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/000142-2025)
- Route to market: the LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions (CDHS) framework is used for direct awards of validation (NUH, NECS LUNA) and for whole EPRs (Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, InterSystems, £13,147,716 over 10 years from 2026-02-26). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eb21056c-6ba3-4bb5-96b6-dcb409cb1f5f)
- Route to market: NHS SBS Patient/Citizen Communication, Engagement and Hybrid Mail Solutions framework (SBS10521, £250m ex VAT, 2026-01-07 to 2030-01-06). Lot 1 covers patient portals, AI and appointment management; Lot 7 covers combined solutions. Portal-bundled validation and digital forms are likely to be bought here. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/017717-2025)
- Buyer pattern: waiting list validation is increasingly bundled into patient portal procurements. Bradford/Airedale required waiting list validation and digital forms as minimum functions, with native Oracle EPR integration and alignment with the NHS App and Wayfinder. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/037999-2025)
- Buyer pattern: CSUs run validation as a managed service. The SCW CSU offer covers technical validation (waiting-time bands, specialty, IMD, pathway recording errors) and administrative validation by scripted patient contact, at about 50-75 technical validations or 50-100 patient contacts per person per day. A three-trust pilot removed more than 9,000 data quality errors. [source](https://scwcsu.nhs.uk/services/waiting-list-validation)
- Market evidence: Swansea Bay UHB's OWLi platform (Pro-Mapp) combines orthopaedic prehab, waiting-list monitoring, risk stratification and onward referral (smoking cessation, weight management) for more than 5,000 patients. The health board plans to extend it to other specialties. [source](https://sbuhb.nhs.wales/news/swansea-bay-health-news/major-award-for-digital-platform-that-cuts-orthopaedic-waiting-lists/)
- Policy driver: NHS England (via the Strategy Unit and MLCSU) commissioned research on 'Minimum standards for patients and carers on an NHS waiting list' (Ipsos, £93,441, Oct 2025 to Jan 2026). This signals forthcoming national standards for waiting-list communication and support. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/876502b1-85a8-4db3-b4aa-8d802419a5ce)
- HQIP re-procured the National Clinical Audit of Perioperative Care (England and Wales, plus Jersey): 3 years from 2025-08-01, maximum £1,110,000 ex VAT, with an option of 2 more years. It is a national perioperative data driver. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/27857701-afac-4b7c-8b59-e97210ecc913)
- Buyer pattern: waiting well and pre-surgery optimisation is mostly bought as community and VCSE services under the PSR or light-touch rules, often by direct award, with small values (£30k-£300k). Newcastle's programme targets pre-assessment postponements, on-the-day cancellations and failed day cases via diabetes, opiate, smoking and obesity interventions. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/054707-2025)
- Theatre productivity is also bought as consultancy: Gloucestershire Hospitals awarded 'Management Consultancy Theatres' to Akeso & Co twice in 2026 (£49,000 and £49,080) via CCS RM6309 MCF4 Lot 7. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/038c0871-6959-4e6a-9116-7647b10fc251)
- Adjacent pre-operative digital tooling: Northumbria awarded orthopaedic pre-operative templating software to Brainlab (£84,804.90, 2025-01-14 to 2028-01-13) via the NHS Supply Chain Surgical Navigation Systems framework, after a 2024 open tender that required calibrated, infection-control-compliant measurement. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ec9a4f28-11cc-4eb9-9a90-827c0a093b7c)
- Renewal watch: several contracts in this area expire around now. NHS Devon WLV (Netcall) ended 2026-09-12; West Herts digital prehab ends 2026-10-31; PAHT RTT validation ends 2027-01-11; NUH RTT PTL cleansing ends 2027-02-14; UHD MyPreOp renewal ends 2027-03-31; WSFT LUNA ends 2027-03-31. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)

- [functional] Patient prioritisation score that weighs priority, wait, age, comorbidities, social factors and pain → N210, SW03
- [functional] Trace all communications with patients, including phone calls; print a waiting-list confirmation and information sheets for the patient → N075, PX06, PX10
- [functional] Build OR lists per theatre with a graphical drag-and-drop planner and annual, monthly, weekly and daily views; check that required documents such as informed consent are present; support the anaesthesia briefing → CW05, N223, SW03
- [functional] Optional AI orchestrator to propose theatre allocation, re-planning and predictive use, and to propose pre-admission, admission and surgery dates automatically → N224, SW03, TR06
- [functional] Structured sign-in, time-out and sign-out checklist with timestamp, user and role; swab, needle and instrument count → N238
- [functional] Recovery-room management with Aldrete scoring and structured handover to the ward for surgical follow-up → N258, SW04
- [functional] Electronic signature and validation at each step, with double verification (read-back) where needed; full audit trail of changes → CS09, CW05, N252
- [non-functional] Production hosted IaaS on the regional cloud (ARIA S.p.A.) in ACN-qualified data centres; test environment possibly on premise → HD01, HD03, HD05, N404
- [non-functional] Mission critical: RPO of 15 minutes or less and RTO of 2 hours or less; offline mode with automatic re-sync → HD04, N409
- [non-functional] Full-web, responsive, multi-browser interface usable on tablet and mobile with no client install; W3C/WAI accessibility → CS08, PX02
- [non-functional] MFA through the regional IDPC, falling back to Active Directory; immutable logs, including system-administrator logs → CS09, IN07, N392
- [functional] Self-service reporting and export to XLSX, CSV, ODS and PDF → CW07, N358
- [non-functional] Availability of 99.5% monthly; screen loads under 2 seconds; at least 500 concurrent users; 24x7 full-risk maintenance; at least 15 evolution days per year → CM04, HD04, HD08, N445
- [integration] HL7 (FHIR where foreseen), DICOM and IHE profiles; integrations built to the regional SISS spec AS-PS_R-SEHL7#01 and validated by ARIA → IN02, IN03, N329
- [integration] Integrate with the ED system (Engineering PSWEB), ADT (GPI NGH), the EHR (GPI NGH CCE/CCA; Ascom Digistat), the MPI (NPRI), the document repository/FSE, two CUP booking systems, sterilisation, the warehouse (GPI Eusis), the data warehouse (Oslo Reportweb), order entry (Elco Fenix) and medical devices → IN01, IN04, IN08, N271
- [compliance] Comply with GDPR, D.Lgs 196/2003 and 101/2018, the MDR (EU 2017/745), NIS2 and ACN guidelines; ISO/IEC 27001/27002-aligned measures; supplier appointed data processor under GDPR art. 28 → CS01, CS02, CS07, N378
- [commercial] Award on quality 70 and price 30 points; Italian-language bids; tender valid for 12 months → CM06, N483

Several 2026 PQs raise digital-sovereignty concerns about this procurement. \| In scope because the national EHR explicitly includes a Pre-Operative and Theatres/Surgery/Anaesthesia module, plus a patient portal, waiting list management and consent. Private hospitals, GPs and private providers are out of scope and will connect through an external provider portal or Healthlink. Enabling services (configuration, testing, integration, training, data migration) will be procured separately, and the EHR winner may not be eligible for them. The EUR 150m turnover bar means a pre-op specialist could only take part as a subcontractor or integration partner. \| PREM-style narrative feedback, not structured questionnaires. Shows HSE wants patient-facing tools to publish through the HSE App and HSE.ie by API instead of running their own front ends. \| National PREMs programme. Its questionnaire engine requirements (branching, Irish language, SMS links with single-use codes, self-service authoring) are close to those of a digital pre-op questionnaire platform. \| Front-of-house patient check-in, adjacent to patient engagement. The integration and hosting requirements show the typical Irish voluntary hospital baseline (iPMS/HL7, data residency, DPIA). \| Digital clinical risk-assessment form integrated into an EHR, close to pre-op risk scoring (VTE assessment is a standard pre-op element). Shows Irish hospitals on Cerner want FHIR apps embedded in the EHR rather than standalone portals.

- [integration] Shared care records across health and social care: EMPI, Record Locator Service, integration platform/portals, VNA, reporting and population health analytics → CW07, IN04, IN09
- [commercial] Direct award and further competition both available. For direct award, suppliers must submit national list pricing, published as a catalogue to all drawdown authorities → CM01, CM06, N434
- [commercial] Catalogue approach: suppliers can add products during the term, provided they meet core functional compliance requirements → CM01
- [compliance] Suppliers tested to an 'FVRA gold level standard' → CM03
- [compliance] Framework endorsed by NHSE CCF (Digital and Technology Category Strategy, pillar 3: clinical software, SaaS and apps), with Cabinet Office approval → CM01
- [commercial] Accessible to all public sector bodies through the LPP access agreement. New entrants cannot join the current CDHS mid-term and are directed to DPSs → CM01
- [commercial] Open framework continuing CDHS as the route to market for core clinical and care digital solutions, supporting the NHS 10 Year Plan → CM01

Notes: Planned successor to NHS LPP's CDHS. The current CDHS was awarded in Oct 2024 to 81 suppliers (OCDS 032423-2024). Several of those suppliers sell perioperative, pre-op or patient-engagement products: Open Medical (Pathpoint ePOA), Bluespier (theatres), Dendrite, iMDsoft, DrDoctor, Patients Know Best, accuRx, Healthcall, Netcall, Mayden and MBI. Pre-op assessment is bought through CDHS today: Princess Alexandra Hospital called off 'Pathpoint ePOA Enterprise SaaS' from Open Medical via CDHS in 2025/26 (GBP 74k) and 2026/27 (GBP 76k). Perioperative and pre-op are not named in the CDHS scope text, but 'theatres' (specialist clinical) and PHR/portals (patient support) are. A pre-op SaaS would need to be on CDHS 2.0 to be directly awardable to London and other trusts from about Oct 2027. The LPP page gives the current CDHS dates 01-10-24 to 30-09-28 with a stated initial period of 2 years. PublicTechnology says the 48-month term includes 2 years of extensions already added. No DTAC, DSPT or Cyber Essentials requirement is published for CDHS. The CDHS 2.0 pipeline notice itself could not be found on Find a Tender: keyword search needs a session token, and the OCDS planning-stage pages for Mar to May 2026 did not contain it. \| A window for a pre-op SaaS vendor to get onto a catalogue that trusts can direct-award from. Facts come from PublicTechnology's report of the pipeline notice; the notice itself was not opened.

That contract was replaced by the region-wide PKB award. PKB's HUTH case-study page says PKB is used for digital pre-assessment questionnaires to triage patients before surgery, with answers feeding a local dashboard for admin and nursing staff. The same page lists post-surgery questionnaires with wound photos, oncology screening questionnaires and NHS App access (2021), and plans for automated questionnaire triggers, response extraction and EPR single sign-on. This is a directly relevant incumbent for pre-op questionnaires across the four HNY trusts. \| HTN (May 2023) says HUTH built a digital pre-assessment pathway on PKB patient questionnaires. In its first months that avoided 96 hours of face-to-face appointments and moved 94 hours to phone. \| A portal bought for a whole ICS. Patients Know Best also holds UH Sussex (£1.16m renewal 2025/26), ESHT and Sussex ICS (£240k) and HPFT. \| A regional collaborative award. Hull separately held a DrDoctor 'Patient Engagement Platform' via G-Cloud 13 (2024-03-30 to 2025-03-29, £101,016).
